items.title: Agricultural development fund, French agency sign rural development deal

original_payload.original_title: Agricultural development fund, French agency sign rural development deal
original_payload.original_body:
Agriculture  Agricultural development fund, French agency sign rural development deal
By  Nefisetu Yakubu   ·   5 hours ago   ·  2 min read
✓
✓
By Felicia Imohimi
The International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) and the French Development Agency (AFD) have signed a co-financing agreement to support the implementation of the Value Chain Programme in Northern Nigeria (VCN).
The programme, a Federal Government initiative, is co-financed by IFAD, AFD and the governments of nine participating states: Bauchi, Borno, Jigawa, Kano, Katsina, Kebbi, Sokoto, Yobe and Zamfara.
It seeks to reduce poverty, improve nutrition and strengthen the resilience of rural communities through sustainable agricultural value chain development.
The organisations disclosed this in a joint statement made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Abuja, saying the agreement marked a major milestone in the programme’s start-up.
IFAD Country Director, Mr Mohammed El-Ghazaly, said the partnership reaffirmed both institutions’ commitment to inclusive agricultural growth, improved rural livelihoods and resilient food systems.
He said the programme would strengthen food and nutrition security, increase rural household incomes and support rural transformation across northern Nigeria.
El-Ghazaly urged the Federal Government and the nine participating state governments to accelerate outstanding start-up activities ahead of the programme’s planned start-up workshop.
He said the agreement provided a coordinated implementation framework and clarified the responsibilities of the financing partners and implementing agencies.
According to him, IFAD will serve as the lead co-financier, providing technical, fiduciary, environmental and social support for AFD’s financing in line with the partnership framework between both institutions.
He said the agreement would streamline implementation procedures and strengthen the capacity of the lead implementing agency and programme coordination offices at national and state levels.
“The signing confirms the commitment of IFAD and AFD to working with the Federal Government and participating state governments to ensure its timely and effective implementation,” he said.
AFD Country Director, Mr Jacky Amprou, said the agreement reflected the strategic partnership between both institutions and their commitment to supporting Nigeria’s efforts to address rural poverty, food insecurity and vulnerability in the northern states.
He said the agreement was a significant step towards the full operationalisation of the programme.
Amprou said the framework would enable IFAD and AFD to jointly finance programme components and activities under agreed policies, procedures and accountability arrangements.
He said the arrangements were designed to promote efficiency, transparency and effective use of resources. (NAN)
FUA/TAK

items.title: How Nigerians can avoid snakebites – FMC Abuja MD

original_payload.original_title: How Nigerians can avoid snakebites – FMC Abuja MD
original_payload.original_body:
Snake bites and scorpion stings can turn life-threatening within minutes. But timely medical intervention could prevent fatalities, says Sa’ad Ahmed, professor and Medical Director of the Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Jabi, Abuja. In this interview with The ICIR’s Marcus Fatunmole, Ahmed sheds light on the growing concerns about reptiles encroaching on residential areas and explains why the first 15 to 30 minutes after a snakebite are often the difference between life and death. Excerpt
Your hospital recently treated a     lady     bitten by a mamba snake. From a medical perspective, how can people avoid  snakebites , especially during this hot season, amid concerns over El Niño?
Yes. El Niño, we all know, is a situation where we have increased environmental temperatures arising from the rise in temperature around the Pacific. So it affects, basically, what I can say is global warming. With that, you expect some reptiles to be affected. Certainly, they’ll come out of their hiding places to get to cooler environments where they can live.
That affects snake habitats as well. So you see cases where snakes will be moving from hotter areas to cooler environments for better conditions. In doing so, they can come into contact with humans. And if someone mistakenly comes into contact with one, it can actually lead to an encounter. So I think that may lead to the snakebite that we are talking about.
What has been the     experience with snakebites at the FMC this year?
So far, I think we have had 11 cases of snakebites this year. Virtually every month, we see one case until, I think, July, when we had two cases. In August, we had three cases and in October, two cases. So we have had 11 cases so far.
What are the first aid measures in the event of a snakebite?
I think the first thing, once there is a snakebite, is to first look at the affected area. You don’t need to wash it. You don’t need to start panicking. What needs to be done is to start preparing to move the patient to the nearest hospital.

items.title: US and rivals spar over next UN boss as race lurches towards deadline

original_payload.original_title: US and rivals spar over next UN boss as race lurches towards deadline
original_payload.original_body:
A tense race to replace outgoing United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres is heading into its final few weeks in advance of a deadline that has never been breached, as global powers spar over candidates in an opaque election process.
With eight candidates,  secret polls and geopolitical rivalries  at play, the choice of the UN’s next chief is still up in the air, even as Guterres must leave office on December 31.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items    list 1 of 3  How UN chief Antonio Guterres tests the limits of quiet diplomacy
list 2 of 3  Guterres warns of ‘unimaginable’ consequences of Iran-Gulf escalation
list 3 of 3  Why is the US sanctioning the International Criminal Court?
end of list
Competing interests from the Americas to the Middle East have complicated the process, raising fears that, for the first time in history, the new year could begin without a leader at the helm of the world’s central diplomatic organisation. The late inclusion of two candidates — Emirati diplomat Lana Nusseibeh and Turkish nominee Feridun Sinirlioglu — has further split the race wide open, with no name so far succeeding in overcoming opposition from all five permanent members of the UN Security Council (UNSC), who hold vetoes.
The protracted contest is part of a “struggle over who will exercise political influence within the UN at a time when multilateralism is under considerable pressure and attack”, Georgina Holmes, senior lecturer in politics and international studies at the Open University, United Kingdom, told Al Jazeera.
“P5 member states are not as politically aligned as they have been in previous eras, arguably even during the Cold War,” said Holmes, referring to the permanent members of the UNSC.
‘Most difficult job in the world’
The UN secretary-general has often been compared with a “secular pope” – a figure expected to unite countries and spearhead global diplomacy.

original_payload.original_title: Indonesian president apologises to Singapore, Malaysia for wildfire haze
original_payload.original_body:
⁠Indonesian President ⁠Prabowo Subianto has apologised to Singapore and Malaysia ⁠for the transboundary haze due to months-long wildfires.
Prabowo conveyed the apology during a session at the ASEAN summit that kicked off on Sunday in the Philippine capital, Manila, according to a statement from the Indonesian presidential office.
Recommended Stories

“I would like to apologise to my neighbouring countries Malaysia and Singapore when we had a very big forest fire, which took nearly four months for us to control. The haze travelled to Malaysia and to Singapore. It is not not our fault but once again we apologise but we have done our best,” he said.
Prabowo also said his government had and would continue to take firm ‌action on companies involved in forest fires while also preparing to establish a new body to strengthen wildfire prevention.
Indonesia has a “zero-tolerance policy” for any company contributing to the blazes, the statement quoted him as saying.
“We’ve revoked 17 concessions [permits] from companies. [Meanwhile] 26 companies are currently under investigation and 11 others have been charged. Another 23 companies are on the list to be charged,” he said.
“In total, 104 companies are currently under investigation by our police.”
He also said Indonesia had deployed 71,000 forest firefighters, and 16 people died while battling the blazes.
Philippine Foreign Minister Theresa Lazaro told a news briefing later on Sunday that Jakarta was “very frank and candid in expressing the efforts they have been exerting in addressing the forest fires in Indonesia” during the plenary session.

items.title: ASEAN, China fall short of agreeing on South China Sea code

original_payload.original_title: ASEAN, China fall short of agreeing on South China Sea code
original_payload.original_body:
China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) have failed to conclude long-running negotiations on a code of conduct for the South China Sea during meetings in Manila,  despite tentative agreement  on about 80 percent of a draft, the Philippines’ foreign minister said.
“There is no conclusion yet,” Theresa Lazaro told reporters at the  ASEAN summit  on Sunday, adding that several key issues remain unresolved, including whether the code would be legally binding.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items    list 1 of 4  Hegseth heads to Manila to shore up US ties with Asia-Pacific partners
list 2 of 4  Myanmar’s coup leader-turned-president wins back neighbours despite war
list 3 of 4  Myanmar’s detained ex-leader Suu Kyi receives package from King Charles III
list 4 of 4  Nearly 1,500 migrants arrive in Myanmar from Malaysia despite UN warnings
end of list
“The ASEAN countries plus China have also different views on how things are,” she added.
ASEAN and Beijing have been working on a code ⁠of conduct in the South China Sea, where they have overlapping claims, for more than two decades. The Philippines, as the current chair of the 11-nation association, had pledged to speed up the process and reach a deal by the end of this year.
Lazaro said she still hoped the code could be concluded under Singapore’s auspices, as the city-state takes over as chair next year.
Southeast Asian nations want the code to reflect international law, which some of them accuse China of ignoring. Beijing insists its actions have been lawful and professional.
China has laid claim to most of the South China Sea, clashing with the exclusive economic zones ⁠of Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam, making a functional code essential to keeping tensions from escalating and managing maritime encounters.
An international arbitration tribunal ruled in 2016 that China’s sweeping claims have no basis under international law, a decision Beijing rejects.

items.title: PIB nominal : l’Afrique du Sud en tête des dix plus grandes économies africaines en 2026

Selon les prévisions du Fonds monétaire international (FMI), publiées dans ses « Perspectives économiques mondiales » pour l’année 2026, l’Afrique du Sud devrait conserver sa position de première économie du continent africain en termes de produit intérieur brut (PIB) nominal. Elle devance l’Égypte et le Nigeria, qui occupent respectivement les deuxième et troisième places du classement.

L’Algérie occupe la quatrième position avec un PIB de 331,89 milliards de dollars. Elle est suivie par l’Éthiopie, dont l’économie est estimée à 201,42 milliards de dollars, puis par le Maroc, avec 195,63 milliards de dollars.
Lire aussi :  Économie : l’Afrique du Sud reprendra sa place de première économie africaine en 2024
Dans la seconde moitié du classement, l’Angola se positionne au septième rang avec un PIB de 157,30 milliards de dollars. Le Kenya arrive en huitième position avec 151,15 milliards de dollars, devant le Ghana (128,64 milliards de dollars) et la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), qui ferme ce top 10 avec 122,28 milliards de dollars.

items.title: Tripoli se prépare à accueillir le sommet Afrique-Turquie

original_payload.original_title: Tripoli se prépare à accueillir le sommet Afrique-Turquie
original_payload.original_body:
Afrique
Tripoli se prépare à accueillir le sommet Afrique-Turquie
À l'approche du sommet Afrique-Turquie prévu en décembre à Tripoli, les autorités libyennes, turques et l'Union africaine intensifient leur coordination sécuritaire et logistique.
Alwihda Info
16 nov. 2026
© DR
Tripoli renforce sa coordination avec Ankara et la Commission de l'Union africaine pour préparer le quatrième sommet du partenariat Afrique-Turquie, prévu les 8 et 9 décembre dans la capitale libyenne.
Les autorités libyennes et turques ont engagé des discussions approfondies sur les dispositifs de sécurité et les modalités logistiques de l'événement. Les échanges portent principalement sur la sécurisation des sites et la protection des délégations participantes, alors que les préparatifs entrent dans une phase décisive.
Dans cette optique, le ministre libyen de l'Intérieur par intérim, Imad al-Trabelsi, a reçu une délégation du gouvernement turc pour examiner les plans de coordination opérationnelle. Les deux parties ont souligné l'impératif de finaliser les préparatifs afin d'assurer le succès de cette rencontre diplomatique.
Au-delà des aspects organisationnels, Tripoli cherche à démontrer sa capacité à accueillir des rendez-vous internationaux de premier plan. Une ambition qui se heurte toutefois à un contexte institutionnel et sécuritaire encore fragile, rendant cruciale la coopération entre les services engagés.
En parallèle, des réunions trilatérales associant la Libye, la Turquie et la Commission de l'Union africaine se déroulent au ministère des Affaires étrangères. Elles rassemblent des représentants des trois institutions ainsi que les membres du comité préparatoire de haut niveau.
Ces travaux visent à finaliser l'ordre du jour et à harmoniser les dispositions diplomatiques et logistiques entre les partenaires. Pour Tripoli, l'accueil de ce sommet constitue un levier pour consolider ses relations avec Ankara et les instances africaines, tout en renforçant sa visibilité sur la scène continentale.

items.title: Building a Sustainable Global Security Shield Against Natural Disasters Through International Cooperation

original_payload.original_title: Building a Sustainable Global Security Shield Against Natural Disasters Through International Cooperation
original_payload.original_body:
English News
Building a Sustainable Global Security Shield Against Natural Disasters Through International Cooperation
As extreme weather events mount, enhancing cross-border cooperation, technology sharing, and early warning systems is vital for building a sustainable global security shield against natural disasters.
Alwihda Info
16 nov. 2026
A delegation from Djibouti visits the exhibition booth of the China Meteorological Administration at the 2025 World AI Conference. (Photo courtesy of Shanghai Meteorological Service)
Par Chen Danhong
As the world faces mounting natural disaster risks, advancing cross-border coordination in disaster risk governance and deepening international cooperation on disaster prevention and mitigation have become inevitable choices for the international community in safeguarding common security.
Ongoing global warming is contributing to frequent extreme weather events and natural disasters. The impacts of cascading disasters often transcend geographical boundaries, leaving no country immune.
In recent years, China has made sustained efforts to promote international cooperation on disaster prevention and mitigation in the field of natural resources, deepening pragmatic collaboration with many countries on emergency response, monitoring and early warning, scientific research, and capacity building.
China has jointly established emergency response mechanisms with other countries to provide timely disaster relief support. It has worked with African countries and member states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) on satellite remote sensing applications and established emergency response mechanisms.
Through these efforts, China has provided more than 1,000 satellite images captured before and after various disasters to support responses, including forest fires in Laos, floods in Pakistan, volcanic eruptions in Tonga, floods and landslides in Indonesia, and earthquakes in Venezuela.
When a debris flow struck Nepal in August this year, China promptly responded to a request from the Nepalese side, providing satellite imagery of the affected areas to support search and rescue operations and post-disaster assessments.
China has deepened cooperation with other countries on disaster monitoring and early warning to strengthen regional defenses against disaster risks. It has continued to advance regular cross-border cooperation on disaster alerts and early warnings. The South China Sea Tsunami Advisory Center (SCSTAC), a regional tsunami warning center built by China, has become operational. Over the past eight years, it has continued to issue warnings and provide round-the-clock earthquake and tsunami monitoring, early warning, and alert services for member countries in the region.
China provides Pacific Island countries and their neighboring areas with ongoing remote sensing services for disaster monitoring. A visualization system for marine environmental forecasting and disaster prevention and mitigation in South Asia, developed by China for South Asian countries including Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, provides forecasting and early warning services for marine environmental conditions, maritime search and rescue, oil spill trajectories, and the transport of pollutants.
China has strengthened joint research with other countries to improve risk identification and prevention capabilities. It has conducted basic marine geoscience research and comparative studies of geological hazards with ASEAN countries, advancing joint observations of earthquakes and geological hazards and carrying out in-depth research into the current status and mechanisms for controlling hazards such as land subsidence and seawater intrusion.
The country has worked with Central Asian countries to conduct research into technologies for monitoring glacier changes on the Pamir Plateau based on multi-source satellite observations. By sharing technologies, experience, and research findings, it has helped promote wider application of satellite remote sensing technologies in the region.
China has also shared knowledge and technologies with other countries to help strengthen their capacity to respond to disasters independently. The marine disaster preparedness and mitigation affiliated center of the China-Pacific Island Countries Center for Disaster Risk Reduction Cooperation has continued to publish Sea Level Rise Status in Island States under Climate Change reports, sharing technologies for sea-level rise analysis, projection, and risk assessment.
In cooperation with countries including the Maldives and Madagascar on dynamic sea-level observation, coastal erosion assessment, and marine ecological restoration, China has also helped extend disaster prevention and mitigation cooperation beyond technological support to the development of local expertise and talent through professional training.
Scientific and technological progress is a key driver of stronger disaster prevention and control capabilities, as well as an important pillar of deeper global cooperation in disaster risk reduction. China continues to innovate in observation and monitoring technologies and early warning methods, independently developing a range of observation and monitoring equipment and an integrated observation and monitoring system spanning space, air, land, and sea.
By applying emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) and digital twins, China is also developing intelligent early warning models to support dynamic disaster risk assessments and accurate early warnings, providing support for science-based decision-making on coordinated disaster prevention and control.
As demand for cross-border cooperation on disaster prevention and mitigation continues to grow, China remains committed to openness and collaboration, helping various countries harness science and technology to strengthen their disaster prevention and mitigation capabilities.
It has also actively supported United Nations (UN) initiatives including the "Ocean Decade" (UN Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development), the Decade of Action for Cryospheric Sciences, and the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration, promoting joint cross-border scientific investigations and collaborative research into disaster mechanisms, risk assessment, and prevention technologies.
A number of public goods developed by China, including the "MAZU" series of marine forecasting models, the "Jingwei" BeiDou-based multiparameter smart buoy, and the SkyOcean AI-based marine large model, have been introduced in neighboring countries and island nations to support marine disaster early warning.
Structural weaknesses remain in the international disaster risk governance system. The technological divide between developed and developing countries persists, barriers to cross-border data sharing have yet to be fully removed, and existing cooperation mechanisms still lack the foresight, systematic approach, and coordination needed to adapt to the evolving dynamics of natural disaster risks.
Looking ahead, countries should continue to build consensus and improve frameworks for cooperation. They should promote the development of cross-border coordination mechanisms and strengthen cooperation in science and technology as well as capacity building under the guidance of the principles of extensive consultation, joint contribution, and shared benefits.
Sustained efforts should be made to strengthen global capacity to withstand multiple hazards, including geological, marine, and cryospheric disasters, and to jointly build a more resilient and sustainable global security shield.
(Chen Danhong is the director-general of the department of international cooperation of China's Ministry of Natural Resources. This article is based on an interview Chen had with People's Daily reporter Chang Qin.)
original_payload.original_summary: As extreme weather events mount, enhancing cross-border cooperation, technology sharing, and early warning systems is vital for building a sustainable global security shield against natural disasters.
original_payload.author: Alwihda Info

items.title: African Coffee Finds a Growing Foothold in China Through Trade Fairs and Zero-Tariff Policies

original_payload.original_title: African Coffee Finds a Growing Foothold in China Through Trade Fairs and Zero-Tariff Policies
original_payload.original_body:
English News
African Coffee Finds a Growing Foothold in China Through Trade Fairs and Zero-Tariff Policies
Boosted by zero-tariff policies and platforms like the CIIE, African coffee from producers in Uganda and Kenya is gaining strong momentum and expanding its footprint across the Chinese market.
Alwihda Info
16 nov. 2026
A Kenyan exhibitor introduces Kenyan coffee to a visitor at the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai. (People's Daily/Li Qiang)
Par Dai Kairan, Huang Weixin, Li Xinyi, People's Daily
November marks the harvest season for coffee cherries on the East African Plateau, where clusters of plump fruit gradually turn red. After harvesting, sorting, washing, and sun-drying, the coffee is processed into green beans, graded, packaged, and shipped to China.
In recent years, China's domestic demand for coffee has continued to grow. The sustained policy benefits of zero-tariff treatment for all African countries that have established diplomatic relations with China, together with the platform effect of the China International Import Expo (CIIE), have opened up new development opportunities for the African coffee industry.
At the booth of Uganda's Kimco Processors Ltd. at the CIIE, freshly ground coffee powder emitted a rich aroma, drawing numerous visitors to taste and buy. The company made its debut at the Uganda National Pavilion during a previous edition of the expo.
Recalling the experience, Martha Wandera, executive director of the company, said, "At the time, I was both excited and nervous, worrying that our products might go unnoticed. To my surprise, visitors quickly lined up to ask about the origin, characteristics, and flavor of our coffee. Some even proactively sought out the story behind the brand. This showed me the immense potential of our products in the Chinese market."
Still thrilled by the memory, Wandera added, "We have participated in the expo for three consecutive years. The CIIE has provided us with an exceptional platform to showcase our products and allowed us to connect with many Chinese partners."
Kenya's Sumseron Coffee & Tea Ltd. has enjoyed similar success.
John Seroney, the company's founder and CEO, noted that during his participation in the CIIE, the enterprise successfully signed a memorandum of understanding with a Chinese company. After he returned to Kenya, many people reached out via social media to discuss potential cooperation.
Seroney said that the CIIE brings together coffee enthusiasts, professional buyers, logistics providers, and packaging and equipment suppliers, helping enterprises link with full-chain resources including brand solutions, packaging technology, and production equipment. This has powerfully propelled the company's business expansion.
Today, the company's coffee business has expanded to the U.S., the European Union (EU), Canada, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), and beyond.
"The CIIE provides enterprises with a platform to reach consumers worldwide, helping us open the doors to even more international markets," he said.
China has implemented zero-tariff measures for 53 African countries with which it has established diplomatic relations. This makes China the first major economy to provide unilateral, full-coverage zero-tariff treatment to all African countries with diplomatic ties.
"In the past, African green coffee beans entering the Chinese market were subject to an 8 percent tariff. The zero-tariff policy has made Ugandan coffee more competitive and given us greater confidence in exploring the Chinese market," said Joseph Nkandu, executive director at the National Union of Coffee Agribusiness and Farm Enterprises (NUCAFE) in Uganda.
Currently, the union covers over 2 million coffee farming households across Uganda, exporting more than 50,000 tonnes of coffee beans annually. About 30 percent of the acquired coffee beans are exported to China, making China one of its fastest-growing export markets.
Seroney noted that his company has already exported 50 tonnes of coffee beans under the zero-tariff policy.
"With profit margins up, our company has gained more confidence to further expand production. By continuously advancing high-standard opening-up and implementing zero-tariff measures, China has brought benefits to the entire African coffee industry chain," Seroney added.
The combination of the CIIE platform and the benefits of the zero-tariff policy has brought African enterprises and the Chinese market closer together. Recent editions of the CIIE have upgraded the Asia-Africa products zone, helping a wide array of distinctive African specialties, including coffee, avocados, cocoa, and cashews, cross oceans to enter thousands of Chinese households.
Beyond expanding exports through the CIIE, Nkandu looks forward to deepening cooperation with Chinese partners in coffee processing, technical exchanges, and more areas, striving to keep a greater share of processing operations in Uganda.
In the Ntungamo district of southwestern Uganda, a modern coffee industrial park is taking shape. The Inspire Africa Coffee Park is the country's first industrial park dedicated exclusively to coffee processing. Inside the workshops, many pieces of equipment bear instructions in Chinese.
The company previously dispatched over a dozen engineers to Weifang, in east China's Shandong province, to learn how to operate freeze-drying coffee equipment.
"Through the training, local employees have gradually mastered equipment operation and production techniques. Strengthening local processing capacities helps drive the coffee industry up the value chain," said Duncan Abigaba, the park's market operations director.
"The CIIE helps us connect with more buyers and industry partners, giving African coffee products the opportunity to reach broader markets," he added.
Looking ahead, as the CIIE's "circle of friends" continues to expand and cooperation deepens, more countries like Uganda and Kenya will leverage this platform to transition from raw material exporters to participants in extended industrial chains, sharing China's development opportunities and jointly forging a mutually beneficial future.
original_payload.original_summary: Boosted by zero-tariff policies and platforms like the CIIE, African coffee from producers in Uganda and Kenya is gaining strong momentum and expanding its footprint across the Chinese market.
original_payload.author: Alwihda Info

items.title: Sharing the Benefits of Openness to Promote Common Prosperity

original_payload.original_title: Sharing the Benefits of Openness to Promote Common Prosperity
original_payload.original_body:
English News
Sharing the Benefits of Openness to Promote Common Prosperity
As the Asia-Pacific region embraces deeper economic integration, the recent China International Import Expo has served as a vital platform for APEC economies to foster growth, innovation, and shared prosperity.
Alwihda Info
16 nov. 2026
A robot performs a picking task at the booth of a South Korean company at the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), held in east China's Shanghai. (People's Daily/Cao Pengcheng)
Par Li Xinyi, Li Anqi, People's Daily
As a major engine of global economic growth, the Asia-Pacific region is characterized by deep economic integration and closely interconnected industrial sectors.
Through business matchmaking and industrial cooperation, the China International Import Expo (CIIE) has provided a broad platform for Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) economies to share opportunities and promote development, contributing to deeper and more substantive progress in building an Asia-Pacific community.
The ninth CIIE, held in east China's Shanghai from Nov. 5 to 10, coincided with the 2026 APEC China Year.
Exhibits from APEC economies traveled far and wide to the expo, where displays, discussions, and business matchmaking turned exhibition booths into starting points for cooperation and products into bridges to new markets.
U.S. exhibitors secured more than 50,000 square meters of exhibition space, the largest area among participating economies for the eighth consecutive year, up 1,500 square meters from the previous year.
Canadian and New Zealand exhibitors recorded their largest exhibition areas to date, while Australian exhibitors expanded their space by 25 percent year on year.
These figures reflect strong participation by APEC economies, with both exhibition scale and product diversity continuing to grow.
Marriott International, which has participated in the CIIE for nine consecutive years, has witnessed the continued expansion of China's consumer services market.
Mao Yibing, a member of Marriott International's global executive committee and president of the company's China operations, said China's continued efforts to promote high-standard opening-up, its thriving tourism market, and evolving consumer demand have created broad opportunities for international hotel groups.
In 2021, New Zealand-based Pacific Alpacas brought more than 100 alpaca duvets to the CIIE. The products quickly sold out at its 9-square-meter booth.
A year later, the company shipped 3.3 metric tonnes of New Zealand alpaca fiber to China and partnered with Chinese companies to process the material using China's advanced fiber-combing techniques. In 2025, it established long-term partnerships with Chinese e-commerce platforms.
Hu Tao, chairman of Pacific Alpacas, said the CIIE provided the company with not only access to a vast market but also opportunities to work with various partners to improve its products and upgrade its industrial and value chains.
For many small and medium-sized enterprises from APEC economies, the CIIE has opened up valuable opportunities to expand their markets and reach global consumers.
Australian Natural Biotechnology Pty. Ltd (ANB) has participated in every edition of the expo, with its main product, Karibee Eucalyptus Pure Honey, continuing to gain popularity in the Chinese market.
Alpaca wool toys from Peru have also used the CIIE as a springboard into China, with orders generated at the expo helping more than 200 local artisan families improve their livelihoods.
APEC helps economies across the Asia-Pacific build consensus through dialogue and consultation and promote free trade and open cooperation, while the CIIE provides an important platform for translating these shared goals into tangible outcomes, said Datuk Ng Yih Pyng, president of the Associated Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia.
The expo not only facilitates access to the Chinese market for products from participating economies, but also strengthens trade ties among APEC members, he noted.
This year's CIIE focused on cutting-edge industries and innovation, showcasing new technologies, products, and services from participating economies and helping APEC economies tap into opportunities arising from China's high-quality development through innovative offerings.
During the expo, many visitors tried out Singaporean company OSIM's flagship massage chair, which made its China debut at the event, at Hall 5 of the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai), the main venue for the expo.
Deserine Lim, general manager of headquarters management at OSIM China, said the CIIE served as a launchpad for cutting-edge technologies from around the world to enter the Chinese market and as an important hub connecting China's innovation needs with markets across the Asia-Pacific region and beyond.
She added that the expo had enabled the company to create a virtuous cycle of "rooted in China, empowering the Asia-Pacific," allowing innovative products that integrate global technologies with local Chinese needs to benefit consumers across the Asia-Pacific region more effectively and quickly.
The development of the Asia-Pacific region has shown that openness and cooperation create mutual benefits. This year's CIIE brought together leading companies from across regional industrial chains, fostering partnerships to strengthen the stability of regional industrial and supply chains.
The Canada International Trade Promotion Society (CITPS) has brought Canadian companies to the expo for nine consecutive years.
Jeannie Cheng, president of the CITPS, said the CIIE serves as a trade and economic bridge connecting businesses and markets, and that behind a product's journey into Chinese households lies a cooperation network spanning multiple APEC economies.
She cited Canadian seafood and fresh fruit as examples, explaining that Canadian companies handle production and quality control, while Chinese partners are responsible for imports, distribution, and sales, and economies such as Singapore and South Korea provide financial, logistics, and testing services.
By leveraging their respective strengths at different stages, economies across the region are strengthening economic ties and deepening cooperation, she said.
Zhang Daijun, executive vice president of Samsung China, said the CIIE offers a vivid illustration of China's commitment to expanding high-standard opening-up, and that the expo is underpinned by China's vast domestic market, well-developed industrial chain support system, and vibrant innovation ecosystem.
China has become a global manufacturing hub, a major center for research and development, and a key hub in global supply chains, he said.
The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting is scheduled to take place in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong province, from November 18 to 19.
Business negotiations, technology launches, and investment projects at the CIIE have offered concrete examples of Asia-Pacific cooperation.
Under the summit's theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," the shared vision of openness, innovation, and cooperation is being translated into practical action across the region, injecting fresh momentum into common development.
original_payload.original_summary: As the Asia-Pacific region embraces deeper economic integration, the recent China International Import Expo has served as a vital platform for APEC economies to foster growth, innovation, and shared prosperity.
original_payload.author: Alwihda Info

items.title: Canada denies Russian team entry for ice hockey tournament

original_payload.original_title: Canada denies Russian team entry for ice hockey tournament
original_payload.original_body:
Russia’s hopes of returning to international sport have suffered another setback after Canada announced plans to deny Russian athletes entry to the 2026 Junior Ice Hockey World Championships.
The Canadian government’s decision effectively bars Russia’s Under-20 national team from participating in the tournament, which is scheduled to hold from December 26, 2026, to January 5, 2027, in Edmonton and Red Deer.
As reported by BBC Sport on Monday, the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) confirmed Russia’s exclusion in a statement, citing restrictions communicated by the Canadian government.
“Due to the position and restrictions formally communicated by the Canadian government, the Russian Under-20 national team is unable to participate in the World Junior Championship,” the IIHF said.

Organisers  of the Abuja City International Half Marathon are targeting World Athletics Silver Label status after the third edition of the race produced a reported Nigerian national record on Saturday.

items.title: JABU alumni condemn INEC chair harassment in UK

original_payload.original_title: JABU alumni condemn INEC chair harassment in UK
original_payload.original_body:
The President of the Joseph Ayo Babalola University Alumni Association, Akinkunmi Akintayo, has condemned the harassment and public intimidation of the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, Professor Joash Amupitan (SAN), during his recent visit to London, United Kingdom.
Akintayo described the incident, in which protesters reportedly surrounded the vehicle conveying the INEC chairman outside Chatham House and hurled insults at him, as an unfortunate development that falls short of the standards of civility and responsible public engagement expected in a democratic society.
Protesters targeted the INEC chairman on Thursday in London, where he went to deliver an address on Nigeria’s 2027 general elections and democratic trajectory at Chatham House, hosted in partnership with the Kimpact Development Initiative.
He stressed that while Nigerians have every right to question public institutions, demand accountability and express concerns about the electoral process, such engagements should be conducted through lawful, constructive and respectful channels rather than personal harassment or intimidation.
Akintayo emphasised the importance of protecting the dignity of public officeholders and preserving the institutional integrity of organisations entrusted with critical national responsibilities.
He noted that Amupitan’s position as INEC chairman comes with enormous national responsibility, particularly as Nigeria prepares for the 2027 general elections. Consequently, he urged Nigerians to allow the electoral body to discharge its constitutional responsibilities without unnecessary intimidation, while continuing to hold it accountable through legitimate democratic processes.
Akintayo’s intervention also reflects a longstanding institutional relationship between Amupitan and JABU.
Before he was appointed INEC chairman in October 2025, Amupitan served as the Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council of JABU, where he contributed to the university’s governance and administration.
A Nigerian based in the United Kingdom and a member of Chatham House, Tunmise Ajiboye, also condemned protesters’ harassment of the INEC chair.
In a statement on Saturday, Ajiboye called on United Kingdom authorities to investigate the incident thoroughly and ensure that anyone involved in the dastardly act is held accountable under the law.
He explained that Chatham House remained one of the world’s most respected platforms for policy dialogue, international affairs and democratic engagement.
He expressed deep disappointment that such a prestigious event was marred by an ambush outside the venue and near the UK Parliament area.
The Convener of Arewa Think Tank, Muhammad Alhaji Yakubu, also frowned on the alleged harassment of Amupitan.
He described the incident as a plot by disgruntled politicians to undermine Nigeria’s democracy ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Yakubu noted that those allegedly threatening to truncate the 2027 elections through sponsored protests, intimidation, and political blackmail would fail.
According to him, Nigerians would not allow the country’s democratic process to be sacrificed to selfish political interests.    Related News      Morning recap: State police bill may reach Tinubu Friday, IG redeploys 15 officers, other stories

items.title: 2027: Atiku vows to restore fuel, electricity subsidies

original_payload.original_title: 2027: Atiku vows to restore fuel, electricity subsidies
original_payload.original_body:
Former Vice-President and African Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has vowed to restore fuel and electricity subsidies if elected president in the 2027 general election.
Atiku made the pledge on Sunday during a political rally at Dabo Aliyu Stadium in Potiskum Local Government Area of Yobe State, where thousands of supporters gathered to receive him.
The former Vice-President said his administration would reverse the removal of petrol and electricity subsidies, arguing that the measures would provide relief to Nigerians grappling with rising living costs.
Addressing the crowd, Atiku said, “Let me assure you that once I am elected president in 2027, I will bring back the fuel subsidy. As I have said in other places, let me reiterate that I swear I will bring back the fuel subsidy once I am elected president.
“I swear I will also bring back the subsidy on electricity.”
He also pledged to tackle insecurity in Yobe State and other parts of the country, promising that his administration would take decisive measures to restore peace and prevent criminal elements from operating freely.
“Let me assure you that I will ensure that peace returns to Yobe State and the country at large. Criminal elements will have no haven once I am elected president,” he said.
On youth unemployment, Atiku promised to create job opportunities for young Nigerians, saying his administration would prioritise employment and economic empowerment.
He expressed concern over the number of unemployed youths in the country, insisting that deliberate policies would be introduced to improve their livelihoods.
“Let me assure you that I will ensure that our youths are fully employed in Nigeria. We will not have jobless youths once I am elected,” the ADC presidential candidate said.
Atiku urged Nigerians to support the ADC in the 2027 general election, describing the party as a platform through which the country could address its economic and security challenges.
“ADC will bring a better life to you. We are here to shape your future,” he told the supporters.
He called on the people of Yobe to sustain their support for the party ahead of the polls, maintaining that his campaign promises on subsidies, security and employment would be implemented if the ADC secured victory.    Related News      Akpabio dares Amaechi as NDDC funds row escalates

Le président du Botswana, Duma Gideon Boko, est arrivé dimanche 15 novembre 2026 à Abidjan pour une visite d’État de quatre jours consacrée notamment à la coopération minière, énergétique et industrielle. Alassane Ouattara doit le recevoir lundi 16 novembre au palais présidentiel, où la signature de nouveaux accords bilatéraux figure au programme.
À son arrivée à l’aéroport international Félix-Houphouët-Boigny, le chef de l’État botswanais a été accueilli par le vice-président ivoirien, Tiémoko Meyliet Koné, en présence du Premier ministre Robert Beugré Mambé et de plusieurs membres du gouvernement. La visite se poursuivra jusqu’au mercredi 18 novembre.
La rencontre entre les deux présidents doit être suivie d’un point de presse conjoint et d’un déjeuner officiel. Elle s’inscrit dans une série de rendez-vous associant responsables politiques, entreprises et institutions financières des deux pays.
Abidjan et Gaborone disposent déjà d’un cadre de coopération dans les industries extractives. Le 30 juillet, à Gaborone, les deux pays ont conclu un  premier accord dans les mines et l’énergie , après une rencontre entre Duma Boko et le ministre ivoirien Mamadou Sangafowa-Coulibaly. Le  gouvernement ivoirien avait alors annoncé  la participation du Botswana au Salon international des ressources extractives et énergétiques d’Abidjan.
Le programme du séjour prévoit des visites à la Société pour le développement minier de la Côte d’Ivoire (SODEMI) et à la Société ivoirienne de raffinage (SIR). Ces deux étapes portent sur l’activité minière et la transformation des produits pétroliers, deux secteurs visés par le rapprochement entre les gouvernements.
Mardi 17 novembre, un forum économique Côte d’Ivoire–Botswana est prévu au siège de la Confédération générale des entreprises de Côte d’Ivoire (CGECI). Le président botswanais doit également découvrir une unité ivoirienne de transformation du cacao, autre activité industrielle inscrite à son agenda.
Mercredi 18 novembre, Duma Boko doit rencontrer le président de la Banque africaine de développement, puis participer à l’ouverture du Salon international des ressources extractives et énergétiques (SIREXE 2026), organisé à Abidjan avec le Botswana comme pays invité d’honneur.

SOMMAIRE
Un modèle conçu pour les tâches professionnelles
Google a lancé le 12 novembre 2026 le déploiement mondial de Gemini 4 Hydrogen, un modèle d’intelligence artificielle intégré à son moteur de recherche et à l’application Gemini. Conçu pour exécuter rapidement des tâches en plusieurs étapes, il est également proposé aux développeurs par Google AI Studio et l’API Gemini.
Dans Google Search, la nouveauté concerne notamment les questions complexes. Une demande comportant plusieurs volets, une formulation imprécise ou des fautes de frappe peut être décomposée en recherches complémentaires. Google annonce ainsi un éventail plus large de liens pertinents et des réponses davantage adaptées à une présentation visuelle.
L’accès varie selon le service utilisé. Dans l’application Gemini, les utilisateurs de la formule gratuite peuvent bénéficier automatiquement d’Hydrogen lorsque le système le juge adapté à leur demande. Le modèle est aussi proposé dans l’interface de sélection de Gemini, tandis que son intégration au moteur de recherche fait l’objet d’un déploiement mondial.
Un modèle conçu pour les tâches professionnelles
Hydrogen s’adresse aussi aux équipes qui développent des logiciels. Il peut intervenir dans la rédaction de code, les tests, la correction d’erreurs et l’examen de dépôts informatiques. Google le distingue de Gemini 4 Carbon et Argon, réservés notamment aux problèmes qui nécessitent des raisonnements plus approfondis.
Dans les évaluations communiquées lors de son annonce du 12 novembre, le groupe affirme qu’Hydrogen achève certaines tâches deux fois et demie plus vite que Gemini 3.8 Flash, à son niveau de raisonnement élevé par défaut. Ce résultat correspond aux essais présentés par Google. Dans son environnement Antigravity, un orchestrateur peut également répartir le travail entre Hydrogen et Carbon.
Pour les développeurs utilisant l’API, Google fixe le prix à 1,50 dollar par million de jetons traités en entrée et à 7,50 dollars par million en sortie. Le tarif est identique sur l’ensemble de la fenêtre de contexte d’un million de jetons, une capacité destinée notamment au traitement de longs documents et de projets informatiques volumineux.
Le modèle est disponible dans Android Studio et dans les offres Gemini destinées aux entreprises. Google prévoit aussi son emploi dans Sheets pour les abonnements professionnels éligibles. L’utilisation d’Hydrogen dans Antigravity dépend, elle, d’un abonnement payant Google AI Pro ou Ultra.
Quatre niveaux de raisonnement sont prévus, du réglage « low » au niveau « xhigh », avec « high » sélectionné par défaut. Les développeurs peuvent ainsi adapter le temps et les ressources consacrés aux demandes selon la complexité des opérations à exécuter.

Le Maroc, la Côte d’Ivoire, le Mali et la RD Congo peuvent décrocher leur qualification pour la Coupe d’Afrique des nations 2027 dès mardi 17 novembre. Chacune compte neuf points après trois victoires. Un quatrième succès lui garantirait une place en phase finale, sans attendre les deux dernières journées.
Ces quatre sélections jouent dans des groupes où les deux premières places donnent directement accès au tournoi. Le Kenya, la Tanzanie et l’Ouganda, pays organisateurs, sont déjà qualifiés d’office. Dans les groupes comprenant l’un de ces trois pays, une seule autre équipe pourra obtenir son billet.
Le Maroc se déplace face au Niger mardi à 20 heures GMT, soit 21 heures au Bénin. Les Lions de l’Atlas ont remporté le premier duel 5-1 et dominent le groupe A. Une quatrième victoire consécutive leur assurerait la qualification.
La Côte d’Ivoire jouera en Gambie à 16 heures GMT, soit 17 heures à Cotonou. Les Éléphants avaient gagné 2-1 à Bouaké. Les Gambiens comptent six points dans le groupe C, tandis que le Ghana affronte lundi la Somalie.
Dans le groupe K, le Mali retrouve le Rwanda mardi à 19 heures GMT, soit 20 heures à Cotonou. Les Aigles se sont imposés 3-2 lors de leur dernière rencontre. Une nouvelle victoire leur garantirait la qualification avant mars.
La RD Congo affronte la Sierra Leone mardi à 16 heures GMT. Les Léopards ont gagné leurs trois matchs, dont le dernier 3-1 face au même adversaire. Le Zimbabwe et la Guinée équatoriale doivent aussi s’affronter lundi dans ce groupe E.
Le Bénin et le Burkina Faso, tous deux à sept points dans le groupe F, dépendent également des résultats de leurs rivaux. Une victoire béninoise contre la Centrafrique lundi, suivie d’un succès burkinabè en Mauritanie mardi, qualifierait les deux équipes. Les cinquième et sixième journées des éliminatoires se joueront du 22 au 30 mars 2027.

items.title: Mozambique: Millennium bim strengthens long-standing support for Casa do Gaiato with donation of essential food supplies

original_payload.original_title: Mozambique: Millennium bim strengthens long-standing support for Casa do Gaiato with donation of essential food supplies
original_payload.original_body:
Photo: Millennium bim Millennium bim has donated essential food supplies to Casa do Gaiato to help ensure meals for the children and young people cared for by the institution. The donation includes rice, maize flour, spaghetti, cooking oil, sugar and beans.
Located in Boane district, Maputo province, Casa do Gaiato provides care for vulnerable children and young people and supports their education and training. The institution serves more than 300 meals every day to residents, pupils at its school and staff.
“Casa do Gaiato carries out extremely important work with children and young people who need support, stability and opportunities to build their future. We recognise the value of this mission and, through this support, seek to make a practical contribution to the institution’s needs. It is also a way of thanking those who dedicate themselves to caring for these children and young people every day,” said Rui Pedro, Chairperson of Millennium bim’s Executive Committee.
In addition to addressing food needs, Casa do Gaiato seeks to provide children and young people with an environment of stability, learning and personal development, combining daily care with education and preparation for independent living.
In 2021, Millennium bim donated an irrigation system to Casa do Gaiato for use on the institution’s farm. The equipment was intended to strengthen agricultural production and contribute to providing food for the children and young people in its care.
Representatives of Casa do Gaiato thanked Millennium bim for its support and highlighted the importance of this collaboration to the institution’s day-to-day operations and the continuation of its work with children and young people.
The initiative is part of the bank’s corporate social responsibility programme, “Mais Moçambique Pra Mim”, which covers projects in education, health, the environment, financial literacy, youth sport and social solidarity. The programme seeks to address concrete needs and help improve living conditions in the communities where the bank operates.
Source:  Millennium bim / Press Release

items.title: Mozambique: Civil society at Mondlane trial; analysis of Chapo strategy — By Joseph Hanlon

original_payload.original_title: Mozambique: Civil society at Mondlane trial; analysis of Chapo strategy — By Joseph Hanlon
original_payload.original_body:
File photo: VOA   In this issue
Civil society at Mondlane trial Tuesday
Extended analysis of Chapo strategy: Frelimo backs juggler Chapo – names him next candidate
Civil society to be present at Mondlane trial
The Supreme Court treason trial of opposition leader Venâncio Mondlane starting Tuesday will have a guaranteed presence of press and civil society, Supreme Court (TS) judge Pedro Nhatitima told a press conference Friday. The courtroom seats only 45 people, so most seats have been assigned. Seats are guaranteed to the two most important civil society organisations, CIP (Centre for Public Integrity) and the CDD (Centre for Democracy and Human Rights). (LUSA, 13Nov)
Ten media organisations have permanently reserved seats including the Portuguese agency LUSA; five more press sets will rotate on a daily basis. The defendant, Mondlane, has 15 seats. The Bar Association will have two reserved seats. Only 10 seats will be available to the general public, rotating and subject to prior registration. Nhatitima said “we will be using a new recording and transcription system. Image and sound recording, followed by transcription into a written document. This helps to significantly reduce the length of the trial.” Previous big trials were written by hand and the text read out.
The trial will not be broadcast live; press and public will not be permitted to record or photograph the trial.
An extended analysis to pull together recent events to show how President Chapo has created a programme that has won party support
Frelimo backs juggler Chapo to keep the party in control, curb greed, and gain international support
President Daniel Chapo will be the Frelimo’s presidential candidate in 2029, Frelimo has announced. The very early announcement gives unexpected party backing to Chapo. But the announcement itself was only made by Frelimo Secretary General Chakil Aboobacar on 18 October (O Pais, MediaFax 19 Oct). It had been decided by the Central Committee at its meeting in Chimoio on 26 August, he said. But there had been no announcement, and Aboobacar’s press conference appears to come only after a meeting of the Frelimo Political Commission. The PC is composed of 17 of the most powerful people in Frelimo, who with the former presidents – Chissano, Guebuza and Nyusi – control Frelimo and thus to a great extent rule Mozambique.
Armando Guebuza (president 2005-15), a party oligarch, gained substantial personal power as president and his government was responsible for the secret debt. The Political Commission responded by delaying the choice of the next presidents until the last minute, just a few months before the election. And the PC selected relatively unknown middle level officials, Filipe Nyusi (2015-25) and Daniel Chapo (2025-present), who the party expected to control. But the unexpected demonstrations after the 2024 elections shocked Frelimo. Suddenly Chapo, who had only ever been a provincial governor, had the task of resolving the ongoing crisis. His very early nomination for 2029 shows he has proved adept at tackling some of the most glaring problems without unduly upsetting the Frelimo oligarchs and factions, who have now given their approval after delaying the announcement.
Chapo has three interconnected tasks. First keeping Frelimo in political control. Second, giving Frelimo increasing control of the economy while curbing the greed and corruption that caused the demonstrations. And third to gain the international support that will keep a bankrupt Mozambique functioning. Finally we point to a fourth issue that appears to be off the agenda by agreement – the war in Cabo Delgado.
Political control
The 2024 election was a blatant fraud, as shown by the Public Integrity Centre (CIP) and its 500 correspondents. There was only token criticism from the international community, so Frelimo is convinced it can do that again in 2029 – or delay the election. The two traditional opposition parties, Renamo and Podemos, and both collapsing because of internal fights.
The new opposition figure, Venâncio Mondlane, is charismatic and good with social media, but he goes on trial Tuesday (17 Nov) by the Supreme Court for treason for the demonstrations. Speaking at the Berlin Freedom Conference on 10 November, he said he would return to Mozambique for the trial. Frelimo’s hope is that he will stay away, flee the country or be jailed.
The accurate and trusted tabulator of political violence  Platforma Decide published  its latest report Thursday (12 Nov). It reports 914 people are currently detained without trial by police, many since the post-election demonstrations two years ago. In the period March-October this year, there were 50 incidents of political violence, many by police and security services. There were 8 deaths and 13 injuries, some by fire arms, and 18 arrests. Of the 50 people affected by violence, 44 are members of Anamola, Venâncio Mondlane’s party, Decide reports.
Frelimo is worried about the reaction to the trial. In some places police officers’ holidays have been cancelled. The prison service ordered its highest level of combat readiness across all prisons from Monday. The directive gives particular attention to prisons affected by incursions and prisoner releases during the 2024 unrest. Guards will be redeployed from administrative duties and patrols strengthened (Zitamar 22 Oct). OMR (Rural Observatory) which did some of the best reporting on the post-election demonstrations, has made a documentary using social media videos: ‘Isn’t this our country?’ (Não é nosso pais este aqui?) Political pressure recently stopped two showings in the downtown Cinema Scala, but OMR is arranging other local showings with discussions – if allowed.
Economic control
The imposition of the so-called ‘free market’ over the past 25 years gave transnational companies control of most natural resources while allowing a Frelimo elite control of large parts of the local economy, and permitted widespread corruption. This has been an important cause of the war in Cabo Delgado and the post-election demonstrations. Demands for bribes, fraud, and badly done and uncompleted building contacts have all caused discontent. Chapo is moving to curb the most egregious problems, while increasing Frelimo power and ensuring continued foreign earnings. Difficult for any juggler, because different interests clash.
An early move was against massive looting of two state companies, airline LAM and telecommunication company TMcel. LAM was put under control of three large state companies: Hidroeléctrica de Cahora Bassa (HCB), Empresa Moçambicana de Seguros (EMOSE, insurance) and Caminhos de Ferro de Moçambique (CFM, railways). All three are well run and skilled at dealing with Frelimo demands without destroying the company.
A key problem is a population growing faster than the economy, despite the huge mineral resources. Ordinary young people want jobs and a share of the resource wealth, which is the basis of the Cabo Delgado war and the post-election demonstrations. Oligarch’s extended families are growing and more Frelimo people want jobs, contracts and commissions, which puts pressure on the party. These two overlap.
Artisanal gold mining in Manica province is uncontrolled and destroying water supplies and farming zones. The biggest mining zone is ‘seis carros’ (6 cars). The mines are controlled by the local Frelimo elite and have 12,000 artisanal miners (garimpeiros). Gold is sold outside Mozambique, so the country gains little. Chapo tried to halt and regularise the gold mining by first banning it. The result is that mining simply moved to nighttime when it could not be controlled. Chapo did not have the power to control the local party elite, and the number of jobs is too great for local people to lose.
As with LAM, his alternative was to find things he could control. First is changes to mineral laws to force mining and gas companies to sign more contracts with local companies. Second is to centralise government import and purchase contracts, and make them more transparent so they can be monitored. The hope is to encourage Felimo-elite owned companies which create jobs and meet higher standards. Control of grain imports has had a bad start, involving pushing out a foreign owned company with a long and good history in Mozambique, which brought protests from the local business community.
The party is backing Chapo, but will it allow him the space to force party elite contractors to do a better job?
International support?
Faced with a major fiscal crisis at home and diminished foreign support after the stolen election, Chapo has opted for globetrotting and high level politics, personally meeting as many senior people possible. This has created some good will and promises of support, but little actual money so far.
Frelimo has a long history of gaining diverse support. During the independence war it was one of the few liberation movements to have support from both China and Soviet Union. After independence it joined the British, Portuguese and Islamic commonwealths. Chapo is now trying to play off China, Russia and the United States against each other. A visit to China in April led to an easing of debt repayments. He visited Russia in October. Soon after, on 5 November, US AFRICOM deputy commander Lt Gen John Brennan Jr. visited Maputo and met President Chapo. Brennan called Mozambique a “strategic partner” and pressed for more US military involvement, especially in Cabo Delgado. Accompanied by Peter Vrooman, US ambassador to Mozambique until last year and who is now AFRICOM’s civil-military deputy, Brennan met Mozambique’s Defence Minister, Cristóvão Chume. AFRICOM is the US military command for Africa.
On the day Chapo met Brennan, a US private security company Sincerus announced that it has been given $4mn for the US State Department to train and equip police to protect the N1 and N380 main north-south roads in Cabo Delgado, which are now subject to attacks and ransom kidnappings. (Mozambique Times 6 Nov)
Three visits to Portugal in the past year and meetings with Portuguese President António José Seguro and Prime Minister Luís Montenegro have generated promises of support and investment. Most recently, Chapo was in Turkey giving a speech Wednesday (11 Nov) to the COP31 to say Mozambique needs $37 billion for climate resilience; he also talked to Turkish investors. On his return he went to Abu Dhabi Friday (14 Nov) for a meeting the President Sheikh Mohamed looking for investments in agriculture, tourism, and energy.
Chapo has made the IMF a high profile issue. Under President Nyusi, and probably under Frelimo pressure, Mozambique made impossible commitments to the IMF in order to obtain a loan. Just when Chapo was taking office, the IMF threatened to cancel its Mozambique programme. The first move under Chapo was to convince the IMF in April 2025 to suspend but not cancel the programme.
Chapo’s moves started early this year. In March 2026 the government unexpectedly (and unnecessarily) fully paid its $630mn debt to the IMF. At the IMF Spring meetings in Washington in April, Finance Minister Carla Loveira met senior IMF officials and it was agreed that the IMF would send missions to Mozambique. In September Chapo met with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly annual high level meeting in New York. On 14 October Loveira, met with the IMF Deputy Managing Director, Bo Li, at the annual IMF meeting in Bangkok, Thailand. Bo Li encouraged Mozambique to maintain dialogue and engagement with the IMF. Olamide Harrisson, IMF’s Resident Representative in Mozambique, said on Wednesday (11 Nov) in Maputo that rising international fuel prices, foreign currency shortages and difficulties in managing public finances are increasing the vulnerabilities of Mozambique’s economy. The economy will grow by only 1% this year, less than population growth, he said. But, unlike a year ago, the IMF is talking to Mozambique, in part due to Chapo talking to top people.
Ignoring the war
The civil war in Cabo Delgado started and expanded during the Nyusi presidency. Rwandan troops were brought in, but the war continued to grow and spread across the province. Frelimo’s underlying policy has simply been to ignore the war. For five years the war stopped development of the gas. The agreement which allowed the recent restart of the gas was to construct a fortress around the gas liquification zone on the Afungi peninsula at Palma. The fortress has no land access and has Mozambican and Rwandan troops inside for protection. President Chapo told the UN General Assembly three weeks ago that “in Cabo Delgado, we have made progress in fighting terrorism and strengthening security.” Few observers would agree, and insurgents have free movement around nearly all of Cabo Delgado province and many local people support them.
In particular ignoring the war means claiming the there are no local grievances behind the war, and that it is all due to a “foreign hand” – which is increasingly rejected by domestic research and foreign observers. Indeed the local grievances of the young people fighting the are about no jobs or benefit from the mineral wealth, and a lack of power. These were a key part of the grievances of the post-election protesters. So far the two protests have not joined, and Frelimo assumes they will always be separate. Frelimo tries to keep researchers and journalists away from the war, but it has not worked.
Government confirmed last week that the gas bonanza is a decade away. Minister of State Administration Inocêncio Impissa told parliament Thursday (12 Nov) that the main source of gas revenue, corporate income tax, will only start being paid in 2035 and will reach $2.6bn per year only in 2042. That means there will be little to share between the oligarchs and young people demanding jobs not just for a second Chapo term, but for some years after – unless money can be raised from the IMF and foreign lenders, investors and donors.
Frelimo is betting that Chapo’s mix of using force on the opposition, trying to curb the oligarchs, looking for money abroad, and ignoring the war will keep Frelimo in control. But for how long? Can Chapo survive a second term? And after that?
By  Joseph Hanlon
Source: Mozambique News, reports and clippings

items.title: Abu Dhabi Fund for Development signs US$500 million agreement with Mozambique

original_payload.original_title: Abu Dhabi Fund for Development signs US$500 million agreement with Mozambique
original_payload.original_body:
Photo: Emirates News Agency (WAM) Abu Dhabi Fund for Development (ADFD) has signed its first cooperation agreement with the Government of the Republic of Mozambique, valued at approximately AED1.84 billion (US$500 million), to support the country’s national development priorities, strengthen key sectors and advance its economic growth agenda.
The agreement was formalised at Emirates Palace on the sidelines of the high-level UAE–Mozambique Business Roundtable, held in conjunction with the conclusion of negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) between the two countries.
The signing was attended by Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique, and Dr. Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi, Minister of Foreign Trade of the United Arab Emirates.
Mohammed Saif Al Suwaidi, Director-General of ADFD and Basílio Zefanias Muhate, Minister of Economy of the Republic of Mozambique, signed the agreement in the presence of senior officials and representatives from both countries.
Al Suwaidi said, “This agreement reflects ADFD’s commitment to building strategic development partnerships that translate national priorities into tangible outcomes. It also marks an important step in expanding the Fund’s global reach and strengthening its contribution to sustainable development. The addition of the Republic of Mozambique as the 109th country in ADFD’s global network of development partnerships reflects our continued commitment to extending the impact of development financing across regions.”
He added, “Development financing plays a vital role in enabling economic growth and advancing national development agendas. Through this agreement, ADFD will provide financing to support Mozambique’s priorities, strengthen key sectors and enhance the country’s capacity to pursue long-term economic and social development.”
Basílio Zefanias Muhate expressed his appreciation for the strategic relations between Mozambique and the UAE, highlighting ADFD’s role in supporting economic development and strengthening the growth prospects of its partner countries.
He noted that the agreement represents an important milestone in bilateral cooperation, creating new opportunities to draw on the Fund’s expertise and financing capabilities to advance national priorities and deliver development projects. These efforts will contribute to strengthening Mozambique’s economy and achieving its broader development objectives.
ADFD continue to expand its international development partnerships, directing financing towards priority projects identified by partner governments. Through this approach, the Fund seeks to support resilient economies, advance sustainable development and contribute to a more stable and prosperous future for communities and generations to come.
Source:  Emirates News Agency (WAM)

More than 77,000 pupils in Gauteng are still awaiting school placements for the 2027 academic year, despite over 267,000 learners already being placed,  reports   EWN   . Education MEC Lebogang Maile said 278 schools have reached capacity, with space shortages affecting parts of Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni. Parents with outstanding documents have until 4 December to submit them. Late applications will open on 17 December. Meanwhile, the department has said that it will pay the second tranche of school funding in instalments until March next year, subject to available funds. It has confirmed that scholar transport disputes over outstanding payments have been resolved.

items.title: Africa: Reaching Isolated Areas Crucial To Stopping Ebola

original_payload.original_title: Africa: Reaching Isolated Areas Crucial To Stopping Ebola
original_payload.original_body:
Six months into the Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, significant progress has been made in bringing lifesaving services closer to affected communities, despite immense challenges. However, fuelled by ongoing conflict, displacement and humanitarian needs, the outbreak continues to expand, particularly in affected areas.
Since the start of the outbreak, more than 11 000 cases and 5400 deaths have been reported. Children account for more than a quarter of confirmed cases and one third of deaths. Seven in 10 children under five with confirmed Ebola have died. While the response has slowed transmission in the initial epicentres, 400 to 500 new cases continue to be reported each week, and the outbreak has expanded to 67 health zones in eight provinces.
Contact follow-up remains below target. The high number of deaths occurring in communities, which account for two-thirds of confirmed deaths, show that infections are still being identified too late. Recent imported cases in Kenya and Nigeria underscore the continuing risk of spread beyond national borders. Delays in paying frontline health workers and responders create tension and slow the response.
Six months of collective action
The United Nations, Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, regional economic bodies and humanitarian partners are fully mobilized behind government leadership. WHO is directing the technical health response, and the wider humanitarian system is helping enable access, logistics, protection, and continuity of essential services. Nearly 100 health and humanitarian partners are present across the affected areas, providing essential health services, including treatment for acute malnutrition.
Africa CDC and WHO co-lead the joint continental Incident Management Support Team, which supports the technical health response and coordinates health and development partners across affected and at-risk countries in response, preparedness and readiness.
Most of the early epicentres of this outbreak have been successfully brought under control and rapid transmission has been halted, including Mongbwalu, Nyankunde, Nizi, Rwampara and Butembo. Even in Bunia, one of the larger, early epicentres, though there is still significant transmission, the number of new cases has halved, and treatment centres are reporting low occupancy.
Diagnostic capacity has grown from two laboratories to more than two dozen, while close to 2000 treatment beds are now available in 104 treatment and transit centres. Around 3000 people have recovered from Ebola, and a quarter of those have enrolled in the survivor programme.
Over 17 000 community health workers and 46 000 community actors have been trained and provided with supplies to safely do their jobs. Health teams are implementing targeted strategies to support women and children, including by keeping maternal health services running. Nearly one million hot meals across 59 treatment, isolation and transit facilities have been delivered to more than 180,000 people affected by the outbreak and to support containment efforts.

However, fuelled by ongoing conflict, displacement and humanitarian needs, the outbreak continues to expand, particularly in affected areas.

items.title: Malawi: Malawi Brewer Castel Faces 100 Job Cuts As Union Seeks Help

original_payload.original_title: Malawi: Malawi Brewer Castel Faces 100 Job Cuts As Union Seeks Help
original_payload.original_body:
Castel Malawi, the country's second-largest taxpayer, is on the verge of retrenching 100 employees, citing a challenging business operating environment that management says has continued to affect the company's operations and sustainability.
The planned retrenchment, which was initially scheduled for the second week of November, has temporarily been put on hold following engagements between management and the Castel Malawi Workers Union (CAMAWU).
The two parties agreed to suspend the decision for three weeks, giving the union an opportunity to engage government policymakers and push for interventions that could help address the challenges facing the industry and potentially avert the planned job losses.

items.title: West Africa: Ecowas - Community Court to Hold 2026 Judicial Retreat

original_payload.original_title: West Africa: Ecowas - Community Court to Hold 2026 Judicial Retreat
original_payload.original_body:
The Community Court of Justice, ECOWAS, will hold its 2026 Judicial Retreat from 16 to 20 November 2026 at Zuma Rock Resort, Niger State, Nigeria, under the theme: Consolidating Judicial Excellence: Strengthening Institutional Standards and Working Procedures for Timely and Quality Justice Delivery.
The judicial retreat is an annual activity of the Court, which affords the judges and judicial support staff the opportunity to review judicial practice and procedure, and adopt guidelines for the efficient administration of justice, in line with international best practice.
The five-day retreat comes at a significant phase in the Court's institutional development, following the assumption of office of the new College of Judges on 13 October 2026, the operationalisation of the harmonised legal framework under Supplementary Act SA.1/12/25 relating to the Court, and the deployment of the Electronic Case Management System (ECMS).
