items.title: Francophonie summit postpones new leader vote amid DR Congo-Rwanda dispute

original_payload.original_title: Francophonie summit postpones new leader vote amid DR Congo-Rwanda dispute
original_payload.original_body:
A summit of French-speaking nations attended by  France 's  Emmanuel Macron  postponed the election of a new chief Monday after a row between African neighbours the  Democratic Republic of Congo  and  Rwanda .
The Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie ( OIF ) – a post-colonial entity resembling the Commonwealth, comprising 53 members and dozens more associates – had intended to choose a new secretary general during talks in Phnom Penh.
DR Congo, Rwanda clash over Francophonie leadership as Macron seeks compromise
But amid a walkout threat by DR Congo, delegates decided to postpone the election for a year, sources close to the matter said.
The current secretary general,  Rwanda 's  Louise Mushikiwabo , will remain in the post but at the next election, her country will not field a candidate, the sources said.
DR Congo had threatened to quit the OIF if Mushikiwabo was chosen for a third successive term on Monday, and had put forward its own candidate.
Kinshasa accuses Rwanda of supporting  the M23 armed group's activities inside DR Congo , which Kigali denies.
The departure of DR Congo – the second most Francophone country after France with 57.3 million speakers, according to the OIF – would have been a major blow to the organisation.
Last year,  Mali ,  Niger  and  Burkina Faso  withdrew after successive coups that saw Paris-friendly governments replaced by pro-Russian juntas.
Macron, who attended the summit alongside DR Congo President  Felix Tshisekedi  and Rwanda's  Paul Kagame , had  earlier called for unity.
But Macron's efforts to defuse the row had sparked anger in Rwanda, and revived debate over the influence of former colonial power France in the organisation.
A source in Macron's office welcomed the postponement of the vote Monday, saying it would allow time for reforms of the appointment process.
"This solution makes it possible to overcome divisions and preserve consensus within the Francophone family," the source said, hailing members' "sense of responsibility".
DR Congo's Foreign Minister Therese Kayikwamba Wagner welcomed a "wise compromise" that would help "preserve the unity of the Francophonie", in a post on X.
But former Romanian prime minister Dacian Ciolos, one of the four candidates for election, deplored a "very sad day" for the organisation.
"If we want the Francophonie to remain relevant, our absolute priority must be to rebuild trust among ourselves," he said in a statement.
(FRANCE 24 with AFP)
original_payload.original_summary: The Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie (OIF) on Monday had been set to choose its new secretary general during talks in the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh. But delegates decided to postpone the election for a year after a walkout threat by the Democratic Republic of Congo amid an ongoing dispute between Kinshasa and Kigali.
original_payload.author: FRANCE 24

items.title: Five EU nations set to announce migrant deportation centre deal with Rwanda

original_payload.original_title: Five EU nations set to announce migrant deportation centre deal with Rwanda
original_payload.original_body:
Five  EU  countries including  Germany  and  Denmark  are set to announce Monday a deal to establish a migrant deportation centre in  Rwanda  -- the first such facility outside the bloc.
The group, also comprising  Austria ,  Greece  and the  Netherlands , has been gunning to open a so-called "return-hub" despite rights groups' concerns, after the European Union cleared the way with a  recent toughening of migration rules.
EU tightens migration rules with plan for offshore ‘return hubs’
The five have kept the location under wraps as they negotiated with potential hosts, but European diplomats and other people briefed on the talks have indicated  Rwanda  as the chosen country.
The African Great Lakes nation had confirmed in August it had begun "preliminary discussions" with several European states.
And it is sending a delegation to a migration conference in Vienna, where several sources said the agreement would be unveiled at a press conference on Monday.
"We shall see next week in Vienna," Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker told reporters Friday, when asked about the matter.
'Suffering and harm'
The announcement is to mark the culmination of an EU push to boost  deportations  launched in 2024, on the back of a souring of public opinion on migration.
EU's new rules on migration and asylum come into effect
original_payload.original_summary: Five EU countries on Monday are set to announce a deal to establish a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda – the first such facility outside the bloc. The move comes after the EU toughened its migration rules in late 2025.

items.title: Report of the Regional Immunization Technical Advisory Group meeting, Addis Ababa, July 2026
items.source: WHO AFRO（WHO 非洲区域办事处）

original_payload.source_name: WHO AFRO（WHO 非洲区域办事处）
original_payload.original_title: Report of the Regional Immunization Technical Advisory Group meeting, Addis Ababa, July 2026
original_payload.original_body:
The Regional Immunization Technical Advisory Group (RITAG) provides strategic guidance on vaccines and immunization to the WHO Regional Director and the WHO Regional Office for Africa. The July 2026 meeting of the RITAG for the WHO African Region was held against the backdrop of the ongoing Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda, and the release in mid-July of the WHO and UNICEF Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC) for 2025. The meeting facilities were provided by the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. It was attended by RITAG members, the technical secretariat from the WHO Regional Office for Africa, colleagues from Africa CDC, and the Chair of the Ethiopian National Immunization Technical Advisory Group (NITAG).
The meeting included updates on global and regional immunization progress; key vaccine-preventable diseases (polio, measles, yellow fever and meningitis); the Bundibugyo virus outbreak; and vaccine manufacturing in Africa.

items.title: Diffa : Le DREN appelle à une meilleure scolarisation des enfants en situation de handicap

original_payload.original_title: Diffa : Le DREN appelle à une meilleure scolarisation des enfants en situation de handicap
original_payload.original_body:
Diffa, 16 Nov (ANP) – Le Directeur régional de l’Éducation nationale (DREN) de Diffa, M. Noufou Hassan Diori, a appelé, ce lundi 16 Novembre 2026, les parents d’élèves à favoriser la scolarisation des enfants en situation de handicap, notamment les malvoyants et les malentendants, afin de leur garantir un accès équitable à l’éducation et de promouvoir leur pleine inclusion dans le système éducatif.
Cet appel a été lancé en marge de la cérémonie de montée des couleurs organisée au niveau du bloc scolaire regroupant les écoles primaires Boukari Sabo et Fanna Grima, dans le cadre de l’initiative nationale « Une semaine, une école ».
Ce bloc scolaire abrite quatre écoles qui accueillent au total 1 442 élèves, encadrés par une cinquantaine d’enseignants.
À l’issue de la montée des couleurs, l’Inspecteur de l’enseignement primaire de Diffa 1, l’Inspecteur de l’enseignement secondaire ainsi que les directeurs des quatre établissements ont successivement pris la parole.
À travers leurs interventions, chacun dans son domaine de compétence, ils ont mis l’accent sur les objectifs de l’initiative « Une semaine, une école », notamment le renforcement du suivi pédagogique, l’amélioration de la qualité des enseignements et des apprentissages, ainsi que la responsabilisation des acteurs de la communauté éducative autour du bon fonctionnement des établissements scolaires.
Prenant la parole à son tour, le DREN de Diffa, M. Noufou Hassan Diori, a rappelé l’importance de cette initiative dans le suivi régulier des établissements et la recherche de solutions aux difficultés qui entravent le bon déroulement des activités pédagogiques. Il a également insisté sur la nécessité de promouvoir une école accessible à tous les enfants, sans distinction liée à leur situation physique ou à leurs capacités.
À la suite de cette cérémonie, le responsable régional de l’éducation s’est rendu à l’école Fanna Grima, où il a visité la classe intégratrice accueillant des élèves malvoyants.
Cette visite lui a permis de s’enquérir des conditions d’apprentissage des élèves, du dispositif pédagogique mis en place et des difficultés rencontrées par les enseignants dans l’accomplissement de leur mission.
Cette classe intégratrice a pour vocation de faciliter l’accès à l’éducation des enfants malvoyants, de favoriser leur apprentissage dans un environnement adapté et de préparer progressivement leur intégration dans les classes ordinaires. Les élèves y suivent une année d’initiation et de familiarisation avec les matériels spécifiques avant de pouvoir accéder à la classe de niveau 1.
Deux enseignants assurent leur encadrement, dont M. Maaroufi, lui-même malvoyant, qui met son expérience au service de l’apprentissage des enfants. Il a exprimé sa satisfaction de pouvoir enseigner à des élèves confrontés aux mêmes difficultés visuelles que lui, tout en soulignant l’importance de l’apprentissage du braille, système d’écriture et de lecture destiné aux personnes déficientes visuelles.
Il a toutefois relevé que le transport des élèves constitue l’une des principales difficultés auxquelles la classe est confrontée. Ces dernières années, grâce aux efforts de la direction de l’établissement et de son partenaire, un tricycle a été mis à la disposition des élèves pour faciliter leur déplacement entre leurs domiciles et l’école.
Pour sa part, Mme Kiari Djalo, enseignante dans cette même classe depuis sept ans, a indiqué avoir bénéficié d’une formation spécialisée en braille pour assurer l’encadrement pédagogique des enfants.
Elle a expliqué que les premiers moments de son expérience avaient été marqués par des difficultés d’adaptation à l’enseignement des élèves non-voyants, avant qu’elle ne développe progressivement les compétences nécessaires à cette tâche.
Elle a également salué la complémentarité professionnelle avec son collègue malvoyant, dont l’expérience constitue un apport important, particulièrement dans les aspects pratiques de l’apprentissage et de l’écriture en braille.
Évoquant les contraintes auxquelles ils font face, Mme Kiari Djalo a, à son tour, insisté sur la question du transport, qui affecte directement la régularité des enseignements. Selon elle, lorsque le tricycle tombe en panne ou devient indisponible, les déplacements des élèves ne peuvent plus être assurés, entraînant parfois l’interruption des activités pédagogiques.
Elle a regretté que, depuis les sept années de fonctionnement de cette classe, les élèves n’aient pas toujours pu bénéficier d’une année scolaire complète, contrairement à leurs camarades des autres établissements, en raison notamment de ces difficultés logistiques. Elle a ainsi plaidé pour un accompagnement financier et social plus conséquent en faveur des enfants en situation de handicap et de leurs familles.
Parmi les pistes de solutions évoquées figure la possibilité de mobiliser, en cas d’indisponibilité du tricycle, les véhicules de la Direction régionale de l’Éducation nationale pour assurer le transport des élèves et éviter les interruptions des cours.
Le DREN a, par ailleurs, rappelé que l’éducation inclusive est déjà une réalité dans plusieurs établissements de la région de Diffa. À titre illustratif, l’école primaire Rahamane Saadou dispose d’une classe intégratrice destinée aux enfants malentendants, tandis que d’autres établissements scolaires, dans les différents départements de la région, accueillent également des enfants malvoyants et malentendants.
En clôturant cette visite, M. Noufou Hassan Diori a lancé un appel aux parents et aux communautés à ne pas marginaliser les enfants en situation de handicap, mais plutôt à les accompagner et à les inscrire à l’école. Il a insisté sur la nécessité d’intensifier la sensibilisation des familles afin qu’aucun enfant ne soit privé de son droit à l’éducation en raison de son handicap.
À travers l’initiative « Une semaine, une école », les responsables éducatifs entendent ainsi renforcer la proximité avec les établissements scolaires, identifier les préoccupations des acteurs de l’éducation et promouvoir des réponses adaptées aux défis du système éducatif, notamment en matière d’inclusion et d’équité dans l’accès à l’école.

items.title: Beijing : l’expérience chinoise dans l’élimination de l’extrême pauvreté partagée avec médias nigériens

original_payload.original_title: Beijing : l’expérience chinoise dans l’élimination de l’extrême pauvreté partagée avec médias nigériens
original_payload.original_body:
Par Abdoulaye Issa Ounteini, envoyé spécial de l’ANP à Beijing (Chine)
Beijing, 15 Nov(ANP)-L’expérience chinoise en matière de l’élimination de l’extrême pauvreté a été partagée, le vendredi 13 novembre 2026 à Beijing, avec une délégation de journalistes nigériens en visite dans le pays.
Cette victoire de la chine sur l’extrême pauvreté ne s’est pas réalisée par un coup de bâton magique. C’est tout un processus qui a été mis en œuvre, a précisé Mme Yang Baozhen, ancienne responsable principale de l’Agence Canadienne de développement international au cours d’une conférence portant sur« Les politiques et pratiques de la lutte contre la pauvreté en Chine ».
Pour mettre en œuvre l’Agenda pour le développement durable à l’horizon 2030, adopté pendant le Sommet des dirigeants des Etats membres des Nations Unies en septembre 2015, Mme Yang Baozhen a expliqué que la Chine a travaillé sur plusieurs leviers stratégiques, il s’agit d’abord d’éliminer la famine ; réaliser la sécurité alimentaire et promouvoir le développement durable de l’agriculture ; Assurer un mode de vie saint ; garantir une éducation équitable et de bonne qualité pour tout le monde ; l’Égalité des sexes ; Un développement respectueux à l’environnement.
Dans cette dynamique de développement, la Chine a entrepris plusieurs réformes visant à stimuler son économie. La conférencière a souligné que le pays a mis en place un système socialiste de marché, entrepris des réformes dans les zones rurales, créé aussi des zones économiques spéciales, et introduit l’investissement étranger. Tout en créant des entreprises à capitaux mixtes et privés, la chine a libéralisé le commerce et les prix.
La pratique de la Chine en matière de réduction de la pauvreté
Le développement économique de la Chine a permis de réduire la pauvreté à grande échelle, tout en améliorant l’éducation et la santé, l’égalité des sexes et le renforcement de la protection de l’environnement.
Dans son combat pour éradiquer l’extrême pauvreté avant la fin 2020, la Chine a fait sortir de la pauvreté 30,46 millions de personnes (fin 2017) et 16,6 millions (fin 2018).
Ce résultat est le fruit d’une politique d’assistance ciblée, en permettant à toute la population d’avoir de la nourriture et des vêtements, de leur assurer les soins médicaux essentiels, de rendre obligatoire l’éducation et d’assurer la sécurité de logement.
Pour y arriver, le pays a enregistré tous ceux qui vivent dans la pauvreté. Cet enregistrement qui a commencé en 2014 avec 800 000 officiels envoyés dans la campagne, a par la suite permis de mobiliser 2 millions de personnes pour un nouvel enregistrement en 2016.
Il s’est agi au cours dudit enregistrement, la première de l’histoire de la Chine, de collecter les informations sur chaque village et chaque famille en pauvreté.
A cet effet, le pays a mobilisé 66,7 milliards de RMB du gouvernement central et 49,3 milliards de RMB de la part des gouvernements provinciaux en 2016.
Il y’a aussi environ 170,6 milliards de RMB de microcrédits et 283,3 milliards de RMB accordés aux 8,02 millions de familles pauvres.
Par ailleurs, le partenariat entre les provinces développées (Est) et régions pauvres (ouest) a pour objet l’assistance à 10 000 villages par 10 000 entreprises. Vers la fin de 2020, plus de 10 millions de paysans de 22 provinces ont été réinstallés.
L’objectif de l’éradication de la pauvreté absolue a été réalisé dans les délais prévus en 2020.
Lors d’un grand rassemblement organisé le 25 février 2021 pour marquer les réalisations de la Chine en matière de réduction de la pauvreté et honorer ses combattants modèles contre la pauvreté, le président Xi a déclaré : « La victoire dans la bataille contre la pauvreté est complète et la Chine a achevé la tâche difficile d’éliminer l’extrême pauvreté ».
Mme. Yang Baozhen a fait remarquer que la Chine a complètement éradiqué l’extrême pauvreté en 2020, la première cible du Programme de développement durable à l’horizon 2030 des Nations Unies, 10 ans plus tôt que prévu.
Les résultats de la Chine en matière de réduction de la pauvreté représentent 70% de la réduction de la pauvreté dans le monde, « c’est une contribution importante à la réduction de la pauvreté dans le monde », a-t-elle notifié.
Au terme de l’intervention de la conférencière, une séance d’échanges enrichissants s’est poursuivie, au cours de laquelle les participants ont soulevé la question de la transposition du modèle chinois au Niger ; le secret de la réussite chinoise et bien d’autres questions.
En réponse, Mme. Yang Baozhen a précisé que le Niger peut s’inspirer de ce modèle en l’adaptant à ses propres réalités.
De par les échanges, il ressort qu’il suffit d’une volonté politique et d’un engagement patriotique pour arriver à ce niveau. Le Niger qui est dans une dynamique de refondation, montera certainement les pas de la Chine dans l’élimination de l’extrême pauvreté.
Le Niger et la Chine entretiennent d’excellentes relations de coopération dans plusieurs domaines notamment le pétrole et les mines, la santé, les infrastructures, note-t-on.

items.title: Niger : Un nouveau directeur général à la tête de la DGPN

original_payload.original_title: Niger : Un nouveau directeur général à la tête de la DGPN
original_payload.original_body:
Niamey, 16 nov (ANP)- Le Président de la République, le Général d’Armée Abdourahamane Tiani a signé, le vendredi 13 novembre 2026, deux décrets portant nomination du nouveau directeur général et de son adjoint de la police nationale (DGPN).
Il s’agit du Commissaire Général de Police Aboubacar Issaka Oumarou, Mle 50 865 nommé à la tête de la Direction Générale de la Police Nationale (DGPN), et du Commissaire Divisionnaire de Police Abdoulaye Maman Mijinyawa, Mle 83 000/R, nommé Directeur Général adjoint de la Police Nationale.
A cet effet, rapportent les deux décrets, “le Ministre d’Etat, Ministre de l’Intérieur, de la Sécurité Publique et de l’Administration du Territoire et le Ministre de l’Economie et des Finances sont chargés, chacun en ce qui le concerne, de l’application du présent décret qui sera publié au Journal Officiel de la République du Niger”.
Notons que le nouveau Directeur Général de la police nationale était jusqu’à sa nomination directeur général de l’Office central de répression du trafic illicite des stupéfiants (OCRTIS) au Niger.

items.title: Initiative « Une semaine, une école » : la Ministre de l’Éducation nationale en visite au CES Lamordé

original_payload.original_title: Initiative « Une semaine, une école » : la Ministre de l’Éducation nationale en visite au CES Lamordé
original_payload.original_body:
Niamey, 16 nov(ANP) – La ministre de l’Éducation nationale, Elisabeth Shérif, a poursuivi ses visites dans les établissements scolaires dans le cadre de l’initiative « Une semaine, une école », en se rendant, ce lundi 16 novembre 2026, au Collège d’enseignement secondaire (CES) Lamordé, situé dans l’arrondissement communal Niamey 5.
Cette visite s’inscrit dans le cadre de la mission du ministère visant à améliorer les conditions d’apprentissage et d’encadrement des élèves, tout en renforçant la qualité de l’enseignement. Pour cette étape, l’accent a particulièrement été mis sur les classes d’examen.
À cette occasion, le proviseur de l’établissement a présenté la situation de l’école, notamment les résultats scolaires enregistrés lors de l’année précédente, les ressources humaines ainsi que l’effectif des élèves.
“Excellence Madame la Ministre, cette année, notre établissement a enregistré un taux d’admission de 54,5 % au BEPC 2026. Au second cycle, nous avons obtenu 46 % de réussite au baccalauréat 2026, dont 33 % pour la série D”, a-t-il indiqué.
S’agissant des ressources humaines, le proviseur a précisé que “le CES Lamordé compte au total 86 agents, dont 46 hommes et 40 femmes. Cet effectif comprend 74 enseignants en activité, trois censeurs, trois surveillants, trois bibliothécaires, deux agents auxiliaires et le proviseur. Concernant la population scolaire, l’établissement compte 1 484 élèves, dont 865 filles”.
Prenant la parole à son tour, l’administrateur délégué de l’arrondissement communal Niamey 5, le commissaire de police Boureima Kousso Abass, a salué les efforts et l’accompagnement de la ministre en faveur de la sécurisation de l’établissement, notamment à travers la réalisation de sa clôture et l’installation de lampadaires.
« Depuis votre arrivée à la tête du ministère, Madame la Ministre, nous avons constaté des changements. Aujourd’hui, le CES Lamordé est éclairé et sécurisé grâce à cette clôture. Partout, il y a des lampadaires. Nous ne pouvons que vous remercier pour tous les efforts que vous avez consentis et ceux que vous continuerez à consentir », a-t-il déclaré.
De son côté, le représentant des parents d’élèves s’est également réjoui des mesures prises pour renforcer la sécurité au sein de l’établissement. Au nom des parents d’élèves de l’arrondissement communal Niamey 5, il a exprimé sa reconnaissance à la ministre pour les efforts déployés en faveur de la protection des élèves.
« Depuis votre arrivée, l’école est sécurisée. Au nom de tous les parents d’élèves de la commune Niamey 5, nous vous disons merci, Madame la Ministre. Merci pour tout et continuez à assurer la sécurité de nos enfants », a-t-il lancé.
Après les différentes interventions, la ministre a effectué une visite des salles de classe, de la bibliothèque et du jardin scolaire afin de s’imprégner davantage des conditions d’apprentissage et de l’environnement de travail des élèves et du personnel enseignant.
Cette visite a permis à la ministre de s’enquérir des conditions d’apprentissage et d’encadrement des élèves, particulièrement ceux des classes d’examen, tout en réaffirmant l’engagement du ministère à améliorer la qualité de l’enseignement et à garantir un environnement scolaire sécurisé.

items.title: 10e réunion du parquet au titre de l’année 2026 : 334 procès verbaux traités au mois d’octobre mettant en cause 673 personnes

original_payload.original_title: 10e réunion du parquet au titre de l’année 2026 : 334 procès verbaux traités au mois d’octobre mettant en cause 673 personnes
original_payload.original_body:
Niamey, 16 nov (ANP)- La Procureure de la République adjointe, Mme Hadiza Manzo a présidé, le vendredi 13 novembre 2026 à son cabinet, la dixième réunion du Parquet au titre de l’année 2026 qui a fait ressortir qu’au mois d’octobre 2026 le parquet a reçu et traité 334 procès verbaux mettant en cause 673 personnes.
A cette occasion, les échanges ont porté sur deux points dont la présentation du bilan mensuel des activités du Parquet, notamment le nombre de procès-verbaux reçus et traités, les audiences tenues ainsi que les principaux motifs de renvoi des dossiers et l’examen de la situation carcérale, à travers le bilan des placements en détention et des mises en liberté enregistrés au cours du mois écoulé.
A cet effet, concernant le  bilan des audiences, au cours du mois de juin 2026, les juridictions relevant du Parquet ont enregistré plusieurs résultats  dont 112 dossiers jugés devant les juridictions de droit commun et  37 dossiers jugés devant les deux pôles spécialisés.
Pour le bilan des procédures transmises au parquet en octobre 2026, le Parquet a enregistré et traité 334 procès-verbaux, mettant en cause un total de 673 personnes déférées devant lui.
À l’issue de l’examen de ces procédures, les suites judiciaires  ont été enregistrées 453 personnes poursuivies devant les juridictions compétentes  et  220 personnes ayant bénéficié d’un classement sans suite.
Pour ce qui est de la typologie des personnes poursuivies, les 453 sont réparties en deux catégories  parmi lesquelles 259 personnes majeures, dont 237 hommes et 22 femmes  et 63 personnes mineures, dont 57 garçons et 6 filles.
Pour les principales infractions constatées, il s’agit notamment du vol, d’association de malfaiteurs en lien avec une entreprise terroriste, l’escroquerie, les coups et blessures volontaires, l’abus de confiance, le faux et l’usage de faux, les actes d’appui au terrorisme, le financement du terrorisme, le viol, le trafic, la cession, la détention et la consommation de drogues à haut risque.
Ces différentes infractions, “classées par ordre décroissant selon le nombre de cas enregistrés, traduisent la diversité des contentieux auxquels le Parquet est confronté et soulignent l’importance de la vigilance, de la prévention et de la réponse pénale dans la lutte contre la criminalité”, rapporte le Parquet.
Par conséquent, le parquet réaffirme son engagement “dans l’exercice de l’action publique, la protection de l’ordre public et la lutte contre toutes les formes de criminalité, dans le strict respect des lois et règlements en vigueur”.
DBZ/AS/ANP 0140 novembre 2026

items.title: Le quartier historique et culturel de Xizhijie : un patrimoine ancestral qui valorise l’histoire de la Chine

original_payload.original_title: Le quartier historique et culturel de Xizhijie : un patrimoine ancestral qui valorise l’histoire de la Chine
original_payload.original_body:
Accueil  ›  Monde & AES  ›  International
Le quartier historique et culturel de Xizhijie : un patrimoine ancestral qui valorise l’histoire de la Chine
16 novembre 2026  · ONEP NIGER
Vue d’une rue du quartier Xizhijie
Partager vers les réseaux
À l’allure calme, ancienne et négligée, les rues de ce quartier semblent inhabitées mais, l’atmosphère est tout autre. Lumières vives et colorées, chansons traditionnelles, danses anciennes, décoration attrayante, street-food, tout y est pour se sentir dans un cadre qui raconte l’histoire du peuple. Derrière chaque maison se cache une histoire et chaque spectacle relate un récit attachant et émouvant lié à cette rue symbolique.
À l’entrée, un spectacle est présenté chaque soir. La musique forte attire les passants et un groupe de danseurs s’adonne à une chorégraphie magnifique. Le regard ébloui et plein d’admiration, hommes, femmes, enfants et seniors sont concentrés sur le spectacle. Un jeu de lumière et de la fumée sont utilisés pour rendre encore plus attrayante la fête. Cette rue était autrefois un lieu consacré au commerce. Ce quartier, appelé « Baoqing de fer », qui est resté intact au fil du temps avec des murs qui ont résisté à tout, rappelle la forme de la ville ancienne.  On y trouve des restaurants, des boutiques, des maisons de thé et des bijouteries. La particularité du quartier fait de cet espace le lieu idéal pour se retrouver, manger des nouilles de riz ou du tofu mariné et admirer cette ville ancienne qui reste encore vivante.
Le plan en arête de poisson offre une vue incroyable. Les passants lèvent les yeux vers le ciel pour contempler les lanternes qui forment un dragon de lumière au-dessus de la rue. Elles symbolisent le dragon qui protège la ville ancienne, offrant un paysage magnifique et lumineux. On y trouve également plusieurs emplacements qui se trouvent au même endroit dont les boutiques, les habitations et le temple ancestral Zhangjia ; ce qui fait de ce quartier un espace de vie, de prière et de détente avec des constructions qui résistent et qui racontent l’histoire de la Chine. Mais, ce qui donne tout le charme à ce lieu, c’est le spectacle qui attire des milliers de touristes. Tous les soirs sont animés et chaque soirée est particulière car, entre les parades immersives qui s’enchaînent, les jeux, les chants avec des instruments dont les cordes sont en soie, les concerts live, les danses des lanternes-poissons, tout y est pour rendre Xizhijie attrayant.
Chaque soir, les rues sont animées de spectacles captivants
Pour cette soirée, la fraîcheur caresse nos visages mais, le spectacle des danseurs Nuo Xi nous fait voyager. A l’origine, ce spectacle était un rituel d’exorcisme et les anciens de Wugang mettaient ces masques féroces pour chasser les mauvais esprits et les maladies. Aujourd’hui, c’est une parade immersive visant à divertir. Les danseurs portent des costumes noirs et rouges de la dynastie Ming. Ces tenues sont raffinées, modernes, tissées avec une soie fine et douce. La fumée par terre crée un effet mystérieux et lors des danses, les mains sont utilisées pour créer des formes ou des dessins. Les danseurs interagissent avec le public et ce dernier reste réceptif et admiratif. Aujourd’hui, il reste 7 unités de protection culturelle, 30 bâtiments historiques et un total de 15 sites protégés et 35 bâtiments historiques dans tout le quartier comme le Tang Family et le magasin Tongchun.

original_payload.original_title: Hunan : de Changsha à Shibadong, un voyage au cœur de la Chine centrale
original_payload.original_body:
Accueil  ›  Monde & AES  ›  International
Hunan : de Changsha à Shibadong, un voyage au cœur de la Chine centrale
16 novembre 2026  · ONEP NIGER
Partager vers les réseaux
Cap sur le centre de la Chine. Après Beijing, les journalistes participant au séminaire bilatéral ont pris, la direction de Hunan, une province au carrefour de l’histoire, de la culture et des transformations contemporaines de la Chine. Du 16 au 21 novembre 2026, le programme les conduira de Changsha à Yueyang, jusqu’au village Miao de Shibadong.
Située dans le cours moyen du fleuve Yangtsé, la province du Hunan occupe une place centrale en Chine. Sa capitale, Changsha, en est l’un des pôles majeurs, sur le plan économique, culturel et scientifique. Ville industrielle importante, base majeure de l’enseignement supérieur et de la recherche, Changsha est aussi un important carrefour de transport. Mais c’est surtout son histoire qui frappe. Souvent surnommée « la célèbre ville du royaume de Chu et de la dynastie des Han », elle conserve les traces d’un passé millénaire. L’Académie Yuelu, l’îlot de Juzizhou et le Musée provincial du Hunan en témoignent : Changsha est une ville où la culture traditionnelle est encore très vivante.
La deuxième étape du voyage des journalistes est Yueyang, autrefois appelée Baling. Située au point de rencontre du lac Dongting et du fleuve Yangtsé, la ville est célèbre dans toute la Chine pour sa Tour Yueyang, l’une des trois grandes tours historiques du sud du fleuve Yangtsé. Sa renommée, elle la doit aussi à la littérature. Le célèbre texte de Fan Zhongyan, « Le Pavillon de Yueyang », a fait de ce lieu un symbole important de la culture du Hunan, et plus largement de la culture chinoise.
Shibadong, village Miao et symbole de la lutte contre la pauvreté
Dernière étape, et sans doute la plus emblématique : le village de Shibadong, dans le district de Huayuan, au sein de la préfecture autonome Tujia et Miao de Xiangxi. Habité principalement par l’ethnie Miao, le village tire son nom des dix-huit grottes naturelles qui s’y trouvent. Shibadong signifie littéralement « les dix-huit grottes ». Mais Shibadong est surtout connu comme le lieu où a été formulé pour la première fois le concept de « réduction ciblée de la pauvreté ». En 2024, le village a reçu le titre de « Meilleur village touristique » décerné par ONU Tourisme. Sur place, les journalistes pourront découvrir une culture Miao particulièrement riche : broderie Miao, chants traditionnels, danses du tambour Miao et autres éléments du patrimoine culturel immatériel constituent les principales attractions du village. Une salle d’exposition consacrée à la lutte contre la pauvreté sera également visitée.

items.title: «Une fois mon diplôme obtenu, je ne resterai pas»: au Tigré, les étudiants traumatisés par la guerre

original_payload.original_title: «Une fois mon diplôme obtenu, je ne resterai pas»: au Tigré, les étudiants traumatisés par la guerre
original_payload.original_body:
«Une fois mon diplôme obtenu, je ne resterai pas»: au Tigré, les étudiants traumatisés par la guerre
Un peu plus d’un mois après la reprise par l’armée fédérale de Mekele, la capitale régionale du Tigré, les étudiants ont repris le chemin des cours à l’université. Mais ailleurs dans la région, les combats entre les troupes éthiopiennes et les forces du Front de libération du peuple du Tigré se poursuivent. Comment ces jeunes Tigréens ont-ils vécu la reprise de la guerre ? Et comment envisagent-ils l’avenir ?
Publié le :  16/11/2026 - 11:42
2 min     Temps de lecture
Écouter - 01:19
L'université de Mekele a rouvert ses portes fin octobre, après des semaines de fermeture et la reprise de la guerre au Tigré. Ici, l'entrée de l'université, le 28 octobre 2026.        © Marlène Panara / RFI
Par :
RFI
Publicité
Avec notre correspondante de retour de Mekele ,  Marlène Panara
Les drapeaux   éthiopiens  , symbole du retour du gouvernement fédéral à Mekele, flottent aux côtés de quelques bannières tigréennes à l’entrée de l’université.
Mariam, 24 ans, est soulagée de la reprise des cours, après des semaines d’angoisse. «  Pendant cette guerre, j’étais avec ma famille, c’était difficile. Surtout qu’après le conflit précédent, on commençait tout juste à retrouver un peu d’espoir. Et voilà que tout a été de nouveau remis en question  », témoigne-t-elle.
La guerre «  anéantit les capacités économiques du Tigré  »
Le retour de l’armée fédérale   dans la ville   soulage peu l’étudiante en droit, encore traumatisée par la guerre de 2020 qui a fait plus de 600 000 morts. «  Nous gardons en mémoire ce qu’ils ont fait. Nous ne pouvons donc faire confiance à personne , ajoute-t-elle.  Alors nous plaçons tout notre espoir en Dieu, et en sa miséricorde  ».
Son amie Betelhem, à la silhouette filiforme, partage ce sentiment. L’instabilité permanente a nourri chez elle des envies d’ailleurs : «  La guerre au Tigré tue les gens, mais elle anéantit aussi les capacités économiques du Tigré. Honnêtement, une fois mon diplôme obtenu ici, je ne resterai pas. Je ne veux pas que mes enfants vivent ce que je vis, je ne veux pas leur enfance soit détruite. Je veux qu’ils aient des perspectives d’avenir, qu’ils voient des choses que je n’ai jamais vues.  »
L’année prochaine, les deux amies prévoient de demander une bourse d’études pour un pays européen.
À lire aussi  Éthiopie: «les choses s’améliorent» dans la capitale du Tigré, veulent croire des habitants usés par la guerre

items.title: Mali: quatrième semaine de grève des enseignants-chercheurs, les autorités commencent à réagir

original_payload.original_title: Mali: quatrième semaine de grève des enseignants-chercheurs, les autorités commencent à réagir
original_payload.original_body:
Mali: quatrième semaine de grève des enseignants-chercheurs, les autorités commencent à réagir
Les enseignants-chercheurs maliens entament ce 16 novembre leur quatrième semaine de grève. Le Syndicat national de l'enseignement supérieur et de la recherche scientifique (Snesup) exige que la prime de recherche, prévue par un décret présidentiel datant de 2017, il y a presque dix ans, soit enfin calculée et versée. Les autorités de transition tolèrent ce mouvement social car la revendication portée par les grévistes n'est ni politique, ni démocratique. Toutefois, sa durée commence à gêner et suscite un début de réaction.
Publié le :  16/11/2026 - 14:18
2 min     Temps de lecture
Un bâtiment de l'université des sciences juridiques et politiques de Bamako, le 21 septembre 2021.        © Wikimedia Commons CC BY SA 4.0 USJPB
Par :
David Baché
Publicité
«  Les plus hautes autorités  » du   Mali   ont enfin reçu les dirigeants du Snesup au cours des derniers jours. C'est ce qu'a indiqué le syndicat des enseignants-chercheurs dimanche 15 novembre dans un communiqué, sans donner davantage de précisions, mais en appelant à poursuivre la grève. Sollicité par RFI, le ministère de l'Enseignement supérieur n'a pas commenté.
Selon des enseignants-chercheurs impliqués dans le mouvement, le syndicat aurait été reçu au ministère et même à la présidence. «  Mais il n'y a eu aucune proposition concrète pour le moment , explique l'un d'eux.  En attendant, on durcit le mouvement en suspendant même les encadrements de master et de thèse  ».
À lire aussi  Mali: après deux semaines de grève, les enseignants-chercheurs poursuivent le mouvement de manière illimitée
Les autorités de transition n'ont pas l'habitude de laisser s'exprimer la contestation. D'autres mouvements ont été violemment réprimés ou étouffés par le passé, comme les manifestations de mai 2025 contre la suspension des partis politiques, finalement dissous dans la foulée. Si les autorités de transition tolèrent cette grève, c'est que les revendications ne sont ni politiques, ni démocratiques : les enseignants-chercheurs ne réclament pas d'élections, mais la simple application d'une prime, déjà prévue par un décret présidentiel de 2017.
Usure et fragilisation
Pour autant, la longévité du mouvement commence à gêner les autorités de transition qui, après avoir superbement ignoré les grévistes pendant près de trois semaines, ont fini par les recevoir. Oumar Berté, avocat et politologue malien, chercheur associé à l'Université de Rouen souligne : «  Cela pourrait conduire à une fragilisation, encore plus, du gouvernement, dans la mesure où il n'y a plus l'euphorie qui était derrière la transition il y a quelques années. L'usure atteint le pouvoir. Le risque est aussi que d'autres syndicats reviennent avec leurs propres revendications.  »
Depuis le 26 octobre, la quasi-totalité des universités et des établissements d'enseignement supérieur du Mali sont paralysés par la grève.

items.title: Germany to join other EU states in announcing Rwanda deportation hub

original_payload.original_title: Germany to join other EU states in announcing Rwanda deportation hub
original_payload.original_body:
Migration    Germany
Germany to join other EU states in announcing Rwanda deportation hub
Alex Berry   with Reuters, AFP
11/16/2026  November 16, 2026    The move follows approval of EU regulations that ease deportations and allow hubs to be set up outside the bloc. A similar scheme by the UK government fell apart over legal issues.
https://p.dw.com/p/5PV1q
Prefer DW on Google
The European Union has struggled to find a migration policy that satisfies all member states Image: Daniel Kubirski/IMAGO       Advertisement
A group of five EU member states, including Germany, was set to announce a new scheme on Monday to deport rejected  asylum seekers  to Rwanda.
A plan to set up so-called return hubs in a non-EU country had been announced by the group — which also includes Austria, the Netherlands, Greece and Denmark — had been  announced back in September .
Monday's expected announcement comes after the  EU introduced new regulations  to speed up deportations and allow the establishment of hubs outside of the bloc.
What do we know about the EU deportation hub scheme?
Rwanda was  not officially named as the chosen country , but people who had been briefed on the ongoing negotiations spoke to Reuters and AFP news agencies.
The central African country had also acknowledged being in "preliminary discussions" with the group of states.
Rwanda had also been the intended destination for a similar plan set up under the UK's former Conservative government that  subsequently collapsed in UK courts .
'Migration paradox': How borders, aid drive human movement
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that  supports HTML5 video
However, the new EU scheme differs from the British one in that it is only intended for migrants who have exhausted all other legal avenues within the European Union.
Migration hubs have been seen by governments as a means to visibly show that they are taking action on migration amid surging anti-migrant sentiment and rising support for the far right.
What are the criticisms of the deportation hub plans?
While the leaders of the five countries said the scheme would comply with EU law, that has not protected them from criticism, especially over the plan to send migrants to a country with which they have no connection.
The Council of Europe, a pan-European human rights body, said in July that return hubs posed "considerable human rights risks."
Claims that the scheme is meant as a deterrence have been rejected by researchers who say there is no evidence that deterrence works.
"Enforcement changes how people travel, not whether they travel. Some pause or ⁠change ​route, and smugglers adapt and raise their prices," said Roberto Forin of the Mixed Migration Centre, a ​research institute that collects data along migration routes.
The choice to pick Rwanda has also been controversial, with the government President Paul Kagame in particular being accused of suppressing dissent and supporting the M23 rebel group in the neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo.
"Paying Kigali to host a deportation program would not only cause suffering and harm to those deported, it would finance and provide political leverage to a government responsible for serious human rights abuses at home and abroad," said Human Rights Watch's senior Africa researcher, Clementine de Montjoye.
Rwanda unscathed in failed UK migration deal

original_payload.original_title: South Africa: 17 killed in separate mass shooting incidents
original_payload.original_body:
Crime    South Africa
South Africa: 17 killed in separate mass shooting incidents
Kieran Burke   with AFP
11/16/2026  November 16, 2026    Police are investigating two mass shooting incidents in Gauteng and KwaZulu-Natal provinces. There has been a growing trend of mass shooting incidents making headlines in recent years.
https://p.dw.com/p/5PUSU
Prefer DW on Google
Around 60 people are killed in the country on average a day, according to police statistics Image: Emmanuel Croset/AFP       Advertisement
At least 17 people have been killed in two separate shooting incidents in  South Africa , police said on Monday.
South Africa is battling extremely  high levels of violent crime with around 60 people killed every day .
In one of the incidents, 9 people were found with gunshot wounds in an informal settlement near Pretoria Image: Emmanuel Croset/AFP
What we know about the latest incidents
The South African Police Service (SAPS) said in a statement that nine bodies were found early on Monday in an informal settlement outside of the capital Pretoria in Gauteng province.
A police spokeswoman said that officers were alerted to the scene at 07:30 a.m. (0530 UTC/GMT) and on arrival found six dead males and three dead females inside a shack, all with gunshot wounds.
Police said a motive for the shooting had not yet been established and that no arrests had been made.
In the second incident, police said that a bullet-riddled vehicle was found in a semi-rural area outside the city of Pietermaritzburg in the eastern province of KwaZulu-Natal.
"Inside the vehicle police found eight men who had multiple gunshot wounds and were certified dead at the scene," a police statement said.
Police said they were also still trying to determine a motive and were working to identify the victims.
"We have seen these kinds of shootings before and there have been different motives from stock theft-related, to drugs-related to taxi violence," KwaZulu-Natal province police spokesman, Colonel Robert Netshiunda, told local broadcaster Newzroom Afrika.
Gunmen kill 27 in two shootings in South Africa

South Africa's high rates of crime
In September, at least 28 people were gunned down in  mass shootings in Gauteng and the Western Cape  in two of the most recent incidents.
Over the years, South Africa has consistently ranked among the countries with the world's highest murder rates, recording between 36 and 45 murders per 100,000 people annually.
The country also continues to grapple with  high levels of gender-based violence , sexual violence and other contact crimes while police battle with large case loads, contributing to low convictions rates.

items.title: Oborevwori presents N1.23trn 2027 appropriation bill, earmarks N320bn for roads

original_payload.original_title: Oborevwori presents N1.23trn 2027 appropriation bill, earmarks N320bn for roads
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Oborevwori presents N1.23trn 2027 appropriation bill, earmarks N320bn for roads
By  Funmilayo Adeyemi   ·   31 seconds ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Mercy Neme
Gov. Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta on Monday, presented a N1.23 trillion 2027 Appropriation Bill before the State House of Assembly, earmarking 65 per cent for capital expenditure, with N320 billion allocated to road infrastructure.
Presenting the bill to the state assembly during plenary in Asaba, Oborevwori said the budget was tagged “Budget of Sustained Prosperity and Enhanced Growth”.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the proposal comprised N806.8 billion for capital expenditure and N430 billion for recurrent expenditure.
The governor also said the proposed budget represented a 28.5 per cent reduction from the N1.729 trillion approved for the 2026 fiscal year.
According to him, the budget will prioritise the completion of ongoing civil and industrial projects, initiation of new high-impact programmes and consolidation of development achievements recorded over the past three years.
He explained that infrastructure development, economic growth and improved public service delivery remained central to his administration’s priorities.
He also explained that the two Ministries of Works would receive N320 billion for road infrastructure, while N50 billion and N74 billion were allocated to the health and education sectors respectively.
He noted that government would also prioritise electricity reforms, agriculture, youth empowerment and social intervention programmes to improve residents’ living conditions.
“My administration remain committed to inclusive development, particularly addressing the needs of vulnerable and disadvantaged groups, irrespective of ethnicity, gender or social background.
“Infrastructure like roads, bridges and flyovers are also critical to my administration as they are drivers of economic development, community integration and improved access to markets,” he said.
The governor added that functional road networks were essential for connecting rural communities to urban centres, facilitating transportation and expanding economic opportunities.
“Without roads, there are no transport routes. Roads connect people, communities and markets,” he said.
According to him, feedback from town hall meetings and community engagements has consistently identified road infrastructure as a major priority among residents.
He said that improved connectivity would facilitate the movement of agricultural produce, reduce transportation difficulties and stimulate commercial activities across rural and urban communities.
Oborevwori emphasised that his administration would intensify efforts to complete ongoing infrastructure projects while commencing new ones in the 2027 fiscal year.
On revenue generation, he identified statutory allocations, internally generated revenue, mineral resources, Value Added Tax (VAT), capital receipts and proceeds from approved asset sales as major sources of funding.
He further said that the budget was anchored on realistic revenue expectations, prudent financial management and effective implementation of priority projects.
He reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to consolidating previous achievements, expanding economic opportunities and ensuring that development benefits reached communities across Delta.
Responding, the Speaker of the House, Mr Dennis Guwor, assured the governor that the Assembly would give the proposed budget thorough, objective and timely consideration.
Guwor said the consideration would be guided by the approved 2027–2029 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework and Fiscal Strategy Paper, with emphasis on prudent resource allocation, accountability and projects that would positively impact residents.
He commended the governor’s performance in implementing the 2026 budget, particularly in road infrastructure, healthcare, education, social welfare and human capital development.
The speaker also praised the governor’s commitment to workers’ welfare, particularly his assent to the 13th Month Salary Law, describing it as a landmark initiative.(NAN)

items.title: FG captures 34m learners, 700,000 teachers on digital platform

original_payload.original_title: FG captures 34m learners, 700,000 teachers on digital platform
original_payload.original_body:
Education  FG captures 34m learners, 700,000 teachers on digital platform
By  Funmilayo Adeyemi   ·   31 minutes ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Funmilayo Adeyemi
The Federal Government says it has captured more than 34 million learners and 700,000 teachers on the Nigerian Education Data Infrastructure (NEDI) as part of efforts to digitalise the country’s education system.
Mr Adebayo Onigbanjo, National Project Coordinator, Special Programmes Operations and Implementation Unit, Office of the Minister of Education, disclosed this on Monday in Abuja.
He spoke at a news conference ahead of the launch of the National Educational Technology (EdTech) Strategy.
Onigbanjo said NEDI, which had also captured 340 schools, would serve as the data backbone of the education system, providing reliable information for planning, resource allocation and accountability.
He said the platform had replaced largely manual data collection processes, which often resulted in delays and outdated information, with digital systems that enabled schools to upload information directly to a central database.
“The Nigerian National EdTech Strategy represents the Federal Government of Nigeria’s commitment to building a unified, data-driven and future-ready education system.
“It provides a coherent national framework for integrating technology across teaching, learning, education management, teacher development, digital infrastructure and governance.
“It ensures that investments in education technology translate into improved learning outcomes and greater equity across the country,” he said.
He said the platform would also help government identify out-of-school children, monitor enrolment and target interventions at learners and communities that needed them most.
Onigbanjo identified five pillars of the strategy as data and interoperability, digital infrastructure, technology and procurement, teacher transformation, and governance and coordination.
He said the data component would establish common standards to enable existing education technology systems to share information while protecting personal records in line with the Nigerian Data Protection Act.
On infrastructure, he said the strategy would prioritise reliable electricity, broadband connectivity and access to digital devices, especially in rural and underserved communities.
He added that the teacher transformation pillar would establish standards for digital skills, certification and career progression through the National Teachers Digital Competency Framework (NTDCF).
According to him, a National Teacher Professional Development Portal would also provide online, offline and blended learning opportunities for teachers.
The strategy would further introduce AskFM, a digital assistant designed to provide parents, students, teachers, institutions and the public with information on the ministry’s programmes, policies and services.
Onigbanjo said artificial intelligence would be deployed responsibly, with emphasis on digital literacy, teacher development and controlled pilot programmes.
He stressed that privacy, child protection and human oversight would remain non-negotiable in the deployment of emerging technologies.
On implementation, he said the immediate priorities included strengthening NEDI, expanding its interfaces, identifying infrastructure gaps in schools, implementing the teachers’ digital competency framework and formalising partnerships with participating states.
“Our immediate priorities are clear: put the governance arrangements in place, strengthen NEDI and extend its priority interfaces, map school infrastructure gaps, launch NTDCF implementation, formalise arrangements with participating States, and mobilise our partners.
“Implementation will be phased. We will mobilise in late 2026 and 2027, scale up thereafter, and focus on optimisation and sustainability through 2030,” he said.
He said the strategy was developed in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, state governments, development partners, the private sector, academia and civil society.
He acknowledged the support of the Mastercard Foundation and the World Bank in developing the strategy. (NAN)

original_payload.original_title: 2027: Don’t allow opposition secure 25% votes in FCT – Wike charges campaign council
original_payload.original_body:
Politics  2027: Don’t allow opposition secure 25% votes in FCT – Wike charges campaign council
By  Philip Daniel Yatai   ·   15 minutes ago   ·  5 min read
✓
✓
By Philip Yatai
Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, has directed President Bola Tinubu’s campaign council in FCT to block opposition parties from securing 25 per cent of votes in the territory during the Jan. 16, 2027 general elections.
Wike gave the charge while inaugurating the 466-member All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council and Rainbow Coalition in FCT on Monday.
The minister specifically named the opposition parties as the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC).
He said the campaign team’s mandate goes beyond a simple victory to achieving an overwhelming margin for Tinubu and APC National Assembly candidates.
“We’re not talking about winning; we’re talking about winning overwhelmingly.
“We must not allow them to go with 25 per cent. They don’t deserve to get 25 per cent,” Wike told the gathering, which included council members, party supporters, and members of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).
Addressing claims by opposition figures regarding political dominance ahead of the 2027 polls, Wike dismissed assertions that the ADC held sway in northern states or stood a chance in the nation’s capital.
He singled out the ADC’s presidential candidate, noting his tenure as Vice President from 1999 to 2007, and argued that past administrations failed to deliver foundational policy reforms for the FCT.
Wike also challenged former Rivers governor, Rotimi Amaechi, whom he referenced in connection with opposition remarks about an APC rally in Port Harcourt, to test his party’s popularity in Rivers.
“The FCT is for no other party other than the APC,” Wike declared, warning council members that they would be held directly accountable for the election outcome in the territory.
To persuade voters, the minister urged the council to campaign on the current administration’s governance reforms and infrastructure record rather than mere promises.
According to him, Tinubu’s administration has introduced historic structural changes since 2023, including appointing an FCT representative to the Federal Executive Council for the first time since Abuja’s creation in 1976 and establishing dedicated Mandate Secretariats for Women and Youth.
He noted that the administration also created the FCT Civil Service Commission, appointed the first Head of Service for the FCT, and enabled career civil servants to rise to the rank of Permanent Secretary.
On financial autonomy and land administration, Wike said the removal of the FCT from the Treasury Single Account (TSA) allowed direct access to financial markets for capital projects, leading to the signing of over 20,000 Certificates of Occupancy (C of O) within three years, compared to roughly 8,000 issued between 1999 and 2023.
He added that traditional rulers had been elevated, while road networks, police stations, and educational projects, such as the proposed University of Science and Technology in Abaji, were expanded across satellite towns and rural communities.
Wike commended the leadership of the APC and PDP in the FCT for setting aside party rivalries to form the Rainbow Coalition in support of the president’s re-election and National Assembly candidates.
He identified the candidates as Sen. Philip Aduda, seeking election to represent FCT at the Senate, Mr John Gabaya for AMAC/Bwari Federal Constituency and Danladi Chiya for Abuja South Federal Constituency.
He urged other states to emulate the alliance model practiced in the FCT, Rivers and Akwa Ibom.
He instructed the council to establish local campaign committees across all FCT area councils and take their message directly to markets, suburbs, traditional rulers, indigenes, and non-indigene associations while maintaining peace and adherence to electoral laws.
In his remarks, the FCT Chairman of the APC, Ishaku Yamawo, commended the party leadership for fostering unity across political divides and specifically recognised members of the “Rambo Coalition,” a cross-party political structure associated with the FCT minister.
Yamawo said the coalition’s willingness to work alongside the APC demonstrated that the party’s strength lay in building partnerships and pursuing a common political objective, adding that the developmental projects executed under Tinubu’s “Renewed Hope” agenda served as the party’s primary campaign message.
“The people can see the transformation taking place,” Yamawo said.
He added that Wike’s appointment as the coordinator of the FCT Presidential Campaign Council was a strategic decision based on his capacity for grassroots mobilisation.
He pledged that the territory’s party structure was fully mobilised to deliver votes for Tinubu and all APC National Assembly candidates, urging members to remain disciplined and sustain the prevailing atmosphere of political cooperation across all wards and polling units.
Also speaking, the FCT Chairman of the PDP, Mohammed Dogara, praised Wike for what he described as unbiased leadership that had united rival political camps in the capital territory.
Using a local proverb, Dogara commended the minister for “bringing the cat and the rat to build the house and live in the house without any issues,” noting that such collaboration between APC and PDP leaders in the FCT was unprecedented.
Dogara assured the minister that local council chairmen and grassroots leaders in the territory were fully capable of mobilising voters even in his absence.
He expressed optimism that the coalition’s efforts would secure victory at the polls on Jan. 16, 2027, naming Aduda, Gabaya and Chiya as beneficiaries of the unified political front.
“Come 17th of January, we are going to rejoice and celebrate the resounding victory,” he said.(NAN)

By Ginika Okoye
Limited has won the non-interest bank of the year award at the 2026 BusinessDay Media Limited Banks and Other Financial Institutions (BAFI) Awards for the fifth consecutive time.
Mr Hamid Joda, the Founder and Managing Director of the bank, said in a statement on Monday in Abuja that the recognition reinforced the bank’s responsibility to widen access to non-interest banking.
He said the award was a renewed call toward deepening financial inclusion.
Joda said the award would also spur the bank into delivering transparent and customer-focused financial services that meet the needs of individuals, businesses and underserved communities.
“This recognition belongs to our Board of Directors, management, dedicated staff and most importantly, our valued customers, whose confidence continues to inspire us.
”We are deeply honoured to receive the Non-Interest Bank of the Year Award at the 2026 BAFI Awards.
”We see this award not merely as a celebration of our achievements, but as a renewed call to strengthen our commitment to ethical banking and develop innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers,” Joda said.
The statement quoted Mr Sheriff Idi, the Co-Founder/Executive Director of the bank, as saying that the award reflected the bank’s progress in building a distinctive identity in the country’s financial services industry.
He noted that TAJBank had continued to strengthen its market position through customer-focused solutions, operational innovation and a business model designed to meet the diverse financial needs of its growing clientele.
Idi said the award would also spur the bank to consolidate its gains, explore new growth opportunities and deliver greater value to customers while reinforcing its position in the nation’s non-interest banking sector.
The statement said the Publisher/CEO of BusinessDay Media Ltd, Frank Ahigbogun,  noted that to be recognised as Non-Interest Bank of the Year, meant to be acknowledged as an institution which had demonstrated that banking could simultaneously deliver profitability, trust, and responsible financial stewardship.
Aigbogun said that TAJBank had distinguished itself as one of Nigeria’s most dynamic and credible non-interest financial institutions in a financial landscape increasingly shaped by questions of sustainability, ethics and long-term trust. ( NAN )

original_payload.original_body:
Agriculture  Okomu ​‌‌‍‍​​‍⁠⁠‍‍‌⁠⁠​‍‌‍‌​Oil honours 65 staff at 2026 long service awards
By  Nefisetu Yakubu   ·   2 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Monday Ajogun
The Okomu Oil Palm Company Plc has honoured 65 employees for their long-standing commitment and meritorious service to the company.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Monday in Benin reports that the employees were recognised at the company’s 2026 Long Service Award ceremony for serving the organisation for bdtween 15, 20 and 25 years respectively.
The Managing Director of the company, Dr Graham Hefer, said employees remained a critical component of the organisation’s growth and success.
Hefer maintained that the award ceremony was part of the company’s efforts to recognise and appreciate employees who had contributed significantly to its growth and development over the years
Hefer said the workers played vital roles in aligning the company with its business goals, driving performance and ensuring its long-term sustainability.
He said management recognised that appreciating workers’ commitment boosted dedication and morale, leading to increased productivity.
Hefer explained that the annual long service award was instituted to recognise employees who attained significant milestones in their years of service.
According to him, 65 employees drawn from various departments were beneficiaries of the 2026 award.
He encouraged the award recipients to serve as role models to newly recruited employees and remain good ambassadors of the company even after disengaging from its services.
The managing director also specially recognised the company’s Smallholder Superintendent, Rev. Sam Aisien, for 20 years of dedicated service.
In his remarks, the Chairman of the Nigerian Union of Agriculture and Allied Employees (NUAAE), Mr Clifford Ewansiha, commended the management for consistently rewarding excellence.
Ewansiha said the gesture had encouraged workers to remain committed and dedicated to the service of the company.
He urged the award recipients to continue to be good ambassadors of Okomu, assuring them that the union would continue to represent their interests.
Ewansiha also presented an award plaque to Hefer on behalf of the workers in appreciation of his visionary leadership and contributions to the growth of the company.
Responding on behalf of the beneficiaries, Mr Mike Okhilua, Mrs Philomena Nwoko and Mr Osarodion Imasekhomwan appreciated the management for recognising and celebrating their long years of service.
They said the recognition not only honoured their dedication and hard work but also reinforced the value of loyalty and commitment within the organisation.
The beneficiaries said the gesture had inspired them to continue giving their best, noting that it demonstrated that their contributions were seen and appreciated.
They commended the company for fostering a culture where perseverance was rewarded and employees’ milestones were celebrated.
At the ceremony, 30 junior staff who had served for 15 years received a medium-sized Thermocool freezer each.
Also, 21 junior staff who had put in 20 years of service received a 21-inch LG colour television each, while four senior staff who had served for 20 years received a 5 KVA generating set each.
Similarly, seven junior staff who had completed 25 years received a settee and four-chair dining table set each.
Three senior staff who had served for 25 years received complete sets of fully upholstered sitting-room furniture, queen- and king-sized beds, and wardrobes.
Mr Wisdom Idemudia of Workshop department received 25 years award from Hefer. (NAN)

items.title: Lagos J30: Ogunsakin claims maiden singles title as Manneni defeat Aina

original_payload.original_title: Lagos J30: Ogunsakin claims maiden singles title as Manneni defeat Aina
original_payload.original_body:
Sports  Lagos J30: Ogunsakin claims maiden singles title as Manneni defeat Aina
By  Folashade Adeniran   ·   39 minutes ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
​‌‌⁠⁠‌​‍⁠⁠‍‍‌‍⁠⁠‍⁠⁠‌​ By Vivian Ahanmisi
Nigeria’s Seyi Ogunsakin on Saturday defeated David Edward to win his maiden boys’ singles title in the second leg of the International Tennis Federation World Tennis Tour Juniors J30 tournament in Lagos.
Ogunsakin, the top seed, had lost to Edward in the first-leg final but bounced back to claim the second-leg title.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the two-leg tournament was held at Lagos Country Club, Ikeja.
In the girls’ singles final, India’s Tejaswi Manneni defeated Nigeria’s second seed, Goodnews Aina, 6-3, 7-5 to win the title.
Manneni dominated the opening set before Aina fought back in the second, but the Indian maintained her composure to secure the victory.
In the girls’ doubles final, top seeds Goodnews Aina and Gloria Samuel defeated second seeds Oluwalashe Agunbiade and Chimezurum Ogualu 3-6, 6-2, 10-4 to lift the title.
In the boy’s doubles final, Elisha Kwange and Gbolahan Olawale beat Oliwier Kowzan and Ivo Sampayo 6-4, 6-4 to claim the title
Speaking after his victory, Ogunsakin, from Ekiti, described the triumph as a major boost to his career.
“I am very happy because it is a big tournament. I wanted revenge after losing in the first leg, and I am glad I did it,” he said.
He said his experience from previous competitions gave him the confidence to win.
“This is not my first tournament. If I can win other tournaments, I can win this one too,” he said.
Manneni expressed satisfaction with her victory, having reached the semi-finals in the first leg.
“It feels really good. I am happy that I was able to pull through,” she said.
She said she approached the final with an open mind, focusing on giving her best rather than putting herself under pressure.
“My mindset was to go and play. If I give my best and lose, that is fine. I am happy as long as I give my best,” she said.
Also, Saidu Musa, Technical Director of the Nigeria Tennis Federation, said Nigerian players had recorded significant improvement since the introduction of the J30 tournament in Abuja in 2018.
He said the increasing number of Nigerian finalists and winners showed that local players were becoming more competitive at the international level.
“There has been quite a lot of improvement in the performance of our Nigerian players. Most of them are now reaching finals and winning tournaments,” he said.
Musa commended Moses for investing in junior tennis development and urged more partnerships to sustain the progress.
“We owe him a lot of gratitude for what he is doing. We look forward to more partnerships with him for the development of tennis in Nigeria,” he said.
Tochukwu Adino, President of Mainland Tennis Club, described the standard of competition as impressive and called for greater sponsorship of junior tennis.
“The tournament standard is high. I never expected to see this level of quality tennis being displayed by upcoming players,” he said.
Adino praised Moses for sponsoring the competition, noting that such investments were important for the growth of the sport.
“I can only say thank you so much for sponsoring this tournament. It is not easy. May God bless him and replenish his pocket to do more,” he said.
Meanwhile, Paul Moses, founder of Tiger Tennis Foundation and tournament director, described the competition as successful, citing increased participation among junior players.
He said the qualifying draw was fully subscribed, with several players placed on the waiting list.
“The competition was incredible. For the first time, we had a full qualifying draw and a long alternate list,” he said.
Moses singled out 13-year-old Mofifunoluwa Atilola, who won the first-leg girls’ singles title and reached the semi-finals in the second leg, for praise.
He said hosting more J30 tournaments in Nigeria would help local players earn international ranking points without spending heavily on overseas competitions.
“When we host more tournaments at home, players can improve their rankings, secure college scholarships and build professional careers,” he said. (NAN)

Hassan Mohamed, Chairman, Local Organising Committee (LOC) of the maiden General Assembly of the African Asset Recovery Practitioners’ Forum (AARP-F), gave the assurance during a pre-conference media briefing in Abuja on Saturday.

He spoke during a question-and-answer session ahead of the assembly, scheduled to hold from November 17 to November 20 in Abuja.

items.title: MDN defende maior envolvimento dos cidadãos na segurança nacional

original_payload.original_title: MDN defende maior envolvimento dos cidadãos na segurança nacional
original_payload.original_body:
O Ministro da Defesa Nacional, Cristóvão Chume, defende o envolvimento dos cidadãos e de diferentes sectores da sociedade nas acções de defesa e segurança, considerando que a preservação da paz e da estabilidade exige uma responsabilidade partilhada.
Cristóvão Chume falava esta sexta-feira, 13 de Novembro, em Maputo, na abertura da I Jornada de Cooperação de Defesa, subordinada ao lema “Segurança Cooperativa: O Cidadão no Centro da Estratégia de Defesa”.
Na ocasião, o governante afirmou que a segurança não deve ser entendida como responsabilidade exclusiva das instituições de defesa, defendendo maior articulação entre o Estado, a sociedade civil, a academia, o sector privado e os parceiros internacionais.
Segundo explicou, a participação dos cidadãos é fundamental para fortalecer a resiliência nacional, promover a consciência patriótica e garantir a protecção das pessoas, das comunidades e dos seus direitos.
O Ministro apontou a cooperação internacional e intersectorial, as mudanças climáticas, a cibersegurança e as ameaças híbridas entre os assuntos que exigem reflexão e respostas coordenadas, tendo em conta a complexidade dos actuais desafios à segurança.
A I Jornada de Cooperação de Defesa reúne representantes de instituições do Estado, das Forças Armadas de Defesa de Moçambique, do corpo diplomático, de organizações internacionais, da academia e da sociedade civil, com o objectivo de promover a partilha de experiências e formular recomendações para o fortalecimento da defesa e segurança nacional.

items.title: Who will develop the north?

original_payload.original_title: Who will develop the north?
original_payload.original_body:
Good afternoon and welcome to Friday's newsletter. Nampula governor Eduardo Mariamo Abdula wants Mozambique’s three northern provinces to stop working in isolation. Opening the first Northern Regional Forum, he argued that Niassa, Cabo Delgado and Nampula should develop as a single economic region, with the Northern Integrated Development Agency (ADIN) at its centre.
The economic case is clear. Niassa has agricultural land, Cabo Delgado has gas, while Nampula, the country’s most populous province, has the commercial networks, port of Nacala and railway corridor connecting the region to wider markets. The harder question is who has the authority and resources to bring these assets together.
The full Daily Briefing continues below for Pro subscribers. Subscribers to the  Zitamar News  tier can read the top half, including the full leader article, here.
The latest from    Zitamar News   :
Vulcan targets February start for coal-waste power plant as it pursues 2,000MW expansion
The $300m plant will burn mineral-rich rejects from coal processing, raising pollution questions alongside promised savings from replacing diesel
Zitamar News  Zitamar News
Subscribe from just $12 a month
Poverty remains widespread across all three provinces. According to the 2015 multidimensional poverty index, 65% of Nampula’s population was poor, compared with 67% in Niassa and 53% in Cabo Delgado. Yet the gas economy has done little to change conditions across the region. The onshore LNG project, suspended in 2021, is only now being revived, while Coral South operates offshore with few links to the local economy. How investment in one province can create jobs and opportunities in its neighbours remains an unresolved question.
Abdula’s own examples illustrate the problem. He complained that cotton leaves Nampula without being processed locally. Mozambique gins its cotton but exports the lint rather than developing a domestic textile industry. Cashew is an even clearer example. Nampula was once the centre of the country’s processing industry, but much of that capacity has disappeared. A large share of the crop now leaves through Nacala unprocessed or is sent elsewhere for processing. A study by Eduardo Mondlane University and IIED linked the industry's decline to the removal of export surcharges on raw nuts, which deprived local factories of supplies. That decision was made in Maputo. No forum of provincial governors could have prevented it.

items.title: Western Equatoria seeks NPA support to boost farming

original_payload.original_title: Western Equatoria seeks NPA support to boost farming
original_payload.original_body:
The Azande Kingdom and Western Equatoria State government have called for stronger cooperation with Norwegian People’s Aid (NPA) to modernise agriculture, increase food production and improve food security.
The call came on Friday during a visit by a high-level NPA delegation to the Azande Kingdom in Bazungua, Yambio, as the organisation marked 40 years of operations in Sudan and South Sudan.
The delegation was led by NPA Secretary-General Raymond Johansen.
Abel Sudan, Western Equatoria State minister of local government and law enforcement, commended NPA for its continued support to the state and the Azande Kingdom, particularly in agriculture and community development.
He urged the organisation to expand its support for agricultural modernisation, saying increased local production was essential to improving livelihoods and strengthening food security.
“I urge NPA to continue supporting the government and the kingdom. The government, the Azande Kingdom and NPA should work together to explore ways of modernising agriculture to improve food production and support our communities,” Sudan said.
He said South Sudan should aim to produce enough food to meet domestic demand and supply neighbouring countries.
Prince Tadeo Mario Sasa, prime minister of the Azande Kingdom, welcomed the delegation and called for closer cooperation in agriculture, investment and community development.
Johansen reaffirmed NPA’s commitment to supporting agricultural transformation and community development. He also recalled the organisation’s previous engagement in the region nearly 25 years ago.
The meeting was held under the theme “Cultivating Resilience, Empowering Communities, Driving Growth” and focused on food security and nutrition, climate change, women’s and youth empowerment, peacebuilding and community resilience.
Western Equatoria has fertile soils and favourable rainfall, making it one of South Sudan’s key agricultural regions, with potential to produce cassava, maize, sorghum and groundnuts.

items.title: 13 civilians killed in airstrike in West Kordofan, witnesses say

original_payload.original_title: 13 civilians killed in airstrike in West Kordofan, witnesses say
original_payload.original_body:
At least 13 civilians, including women and children, were killed in an airstrike on the Abu Galb area of Abu Zabad Locality in Sudan’s West Kordofan State on Sunday, according to eyewitnesses and a local lawyers’ group.
The attack, allegedly carried out by a Sudanese military aircraft, also destroyed homes and shops, causing extensive damage to civilian property.
Speaking to Radio Tamazuj, eyewitness Salih Yousif said the airstrike struck civilians, killing several people and leaving some bodies dismembered. He said three shops were completely destroyed.
Yousif identified two of those killed as Ibrahim Naheed and Ezzeldin Mohamed Naheed. He said other victims included children of Yousif Al-Haj, who were reportedly struck by three bombs while on their way to fetch water for their household.
Another eyewitness, Juma Zakaria, described the bombing as a devastating tragedy, saying it killed civilians, left some bodies badly mutilated and caused extensive damage to property.
In a statement issued on Monday, the Emergency Lawyers group condemned the attack, alleging that a Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) warplane had carried out the strike.
The group said its preliminary monitoring indicated that 13 civilians, including women and children, had been killed and several homes destroyed.
Emergency Lawyers warned against continued airstrikes on residential areas, saying indiscriminate attacks endangered civilian lives and violated international humanitarian law.
The group called for an immediate halt to airstrikes on populated areas, an independent and transparent investigation into the incident, and accountability for those responsible.
It also urged the authorities to ensure unhindered access to humanitarian and medical assistance for those affected and allow relevant organisations to establish the full number of casualties and document the alleged violations.
The Sudanese army could not immediately be reached for comment.
Fighting has intensified in the Kordofan region between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF). The army and allied forces recaptured Al-Khuway in West Kordofan last week and advanced into surrounding areas as they seek to regain territory from the RSF.
