items.title: Mozambique: Chapo meets ExxonMobil and Eni executives to review Rovuma Basin gas projects

original_payload.original_title: Mozambique: Chapo meets ExxonMobil and Eni executives to review Rovuma Basin gas projects
original_payload.original_body:
Photo: AIM Mozambique’s President Daniel Chapo met executives from US energy giant ExxonMobil and Italian energy company Eni in Maputo on Monday to review the development of natural gas projects in the Rovuma Basin, with a focus on Rovuma LNG, which could reach a final investment decision by the end of this year.
During separate meetings at the President’s Office, the two companies presented progress on the strategic restructuring of their stakes in the natural gas projects, as well as their development plans and the expansion of operations in Cabo Delgado province.
Speaking to the press after the meeting, ExxonMobil Upstream President Dan Ammann said the restructuring, carried out through a transaction with Eni, would allow the US multinational to increase its stake in the Rovuma LNG project to 50%, reinforcing its commitment to Mozambique.
According to Ammann, the project could generate more than US$100 billion in value for the country and create over 7,000 jobs if it proceeds according to the announced plans.
ExxonMobil expects to reach a final investment decision by December 2026, paving the way for the project’s implementation phase.
For his part, Eni Chief Operating Officer Guido Brusco explained that the strategic restructuring establishes a 50% stake for the company in the Coral Sul and Coral Norte projects, as well as in the other floating liquefied natural gas (FLNG) initiatives in Area 4.
READ:  Eni anticipates final investment decision on Mozambique FLNG expansion by 2027
According to Brusco, the new structure is intended to make operating models more efficient and accelerate the development of natural gas resources in the Rovuma Basin.
Regarding Coral Sul, which is already producing, Brusco said the project had created 1,400 jobs and awarded contracts worth more than US$1 billion to Mozambican companies.
The initiative had also mobilised US$19 million for sustainability programmes, with an estimated 650,000 people benefiting.
As for Coral Norte, Brusco said the project was 70% complete, with operations expected to begin in 2028.
Over its lifetime, the project is expected to generate more than US$3 billion in contract awards for national companies and mobilise US$60 million for sustainability initiatives, with an estimated one million people benefiting.
Brusco also announced that Eni expects to take an investment decision in 2027 on a third floating liquefied natural gas production unit, known as Mamba East. With this unit, alongside Coral Sul and Coral Norte, total production capacity is expected to reach three million tonnes per year.
In the energy sector, Eni also expects to take an investment decision in the second quarter of 2027 on the construction of a power plant, which is projected to begin operating in 2029.
Brusco further revealed that the multinational had already invested US$60 million in the energy transition and planned to invest a further US$200 million in agribusiness, clean cooking, reforestation and sustainable agriculture initiatives.
The investments are expected to benefit 100,000 farmers by 2030 and provide two million people with access to clean cooking solutions.
Both multinationals expressed their willingness to continue working with Mozambique on the development of natural gas projects and other related economic initiatives.
Brusco reiterated Eni’s commitment to “creating lasting value and a sustainable economy for the benefit of the country and the Mozambican people”, while ExxonMobil reaffirmed its commitment to advancing the Rovuma LNG project and preparing for the next phase of its implementation.
Source:  AIM Moçambique

items.title: Mozambique: Mondlane “steadfast and in good spirits”

original_payload.original_title: Mozambique: Mondlane “steadfast and in good spirits”
original_payload.original_body:
FILE – For illustration purposes only. [File photo: Lusa] Mozambican politician Venâncio Mondlane said yesterday that he was “steadfast and in good spirits” ahead of the trial beginning on Tuesday, saying the proceedings were intended to put on trial “the audacity” of a generation that had accepted “shedding its blood” in defence of the truth.
“I am steadfast, I am in good spirits, I am aware that this is a great cause, something that is far bigger than my shoulders, and I am certain that I am being sustained by the prayers of the Mozambican people,” Venâncio Mondlane said during a live broadcast on his Facebook page.
The Supreme Court begins the trial of former Mozambican presidential candidate Venâncio Mondlane in Maputo on Tuesday. He faces five criminal charges, including incitement to terrorism, in connection with the post-election demonstrations.
For the Mozambican politician, the proceedings target an “entire generation” that decided to defend the truth, justice and “what was placed in the ballot box”. He described himself as merely the “tip of the iceberg” and the “point of contact” for that movement.
“What is being put on trial is the audacity of a generation that accepted shedding its blood but continued to defend the truth, and that generation’s ability, knowledge and conviction that our country can change,” he said.
Mondlane also said he was willing, “with great pleasure”, to be the “guinea pig” who would stand in the dock, arguing that the trial was intended to serve as an example to an entire generation.
“I gladly accept being precisely that guinea pig [test subject] who will be sitting in the dock tomorrow and used as an example of the message they want to send to an entire generation, to an entire people. But I accept this challenge, I accept this sacrifice, I accept serving as a shield and as an example because I have a conviction,” he said, adding that no regime or dictatorship could prevail against the truth.
Venâncio Mondlane also called for all Mozambicans to unite and thanked them for contributing to what he called “the people’s trial”, saying that more than 920,000 meticais (around €13,000) had been raised to cover legal costs.
The Public Prosecution is presenting videos, telephone recordings, bank data and documentation concerning Venâncio Mondlane’s movements as evidence in court. He has never recognised the results of the 9 October 2024 elections and is accused of plunging Mozambique into “chaos”.
The prosecution case is based on Venâncio’s calls for challenges to the election results, strikes, shutdowns and protests, made on social media during the electoral contestation.
The politician faces charges of public glorification of crime, incitement to collective disobedience, public instigation to commit a crime, instigation of terrorism and incitement to terrorism.
According to the Public Prosecution, the defendant used social media “to facilitate the dissemination of his radical ideas, which he called a revolution”, an accusation he has rejected: “On the contrary, I rendered a great service to this nation.”
According to previously published data from the Decide platform, around 7,200 people were detained during the five months of protests, which resulted in 411 deaths in clashes with the police and the destruction of hundreds of businesses and public institutions.
Regarding the protests, which continued until March 2025, the Public Prosecution says Venâncio Mondlane acted “with the aim, which he achieved, of inciting acts of violence and social unrest, as well as developing a process of radicalisation, spreading radical ideas and promoting acts of violence”.
“By ordering young people and other followers to block roads, preventing the passage and movement of people and goods, and by coercing citizens into staying at home, he acted with the aim of causing them fear and intimidation (…), aware that these actions were capable of causing panic and terror, as they effectively did,” the prosecution alleges.
The police General Command has appealed to the public to follow the trial with “calm”, calling for respect for public order and reaffirming its “commitment to protecting people and public and private property”, while acting “preventively and proportionately”.
The trial will take place in the Criminal Section of the Supreme Court, from 10:00 to 15:30 local time, before a panel of five Supreme Court judges. The Public Prosecution will be represented by two deputy attorneys-general. The courtroom has a capacity of 45 people, including 17 journalists.
The case will involve 12 prosecution witnesses, 20 defence witnesses, four witnesses for the assisting party and two experts from mobile operators Vodacom and Tmcel. It will also be the first trial in the country to feature audio and video recording and automatic transcription of hearings.
The case is being heard by the Supreme Court because Venâncio Mondlane is, by virtue of his position as the second most-voted presidential candidate, a member of the Council of State, following the lifting of his immunity.
Source:  Lusa

Neste contexto, o Presidente Chapo destaca a importância da  continuidade do diálogo e da concertação entre os dois países,  tendo em vista a valorização dos laços históricos e culturais que  unem os seus povos e a promoção de posições comuns sobre  matérias de interesse mútuo na agenda regional e internacional.

items.title: Venâncio Mondlane já se encontra no Tribunal Supremo onde vai ser julgado

original_payload.original_title: Venâncio Mondlane já se encontra no Tribunal Supremo onde vai ser julgado
original_payload.original_body:
O presidente do partido Anamola, Venâncio Mondlane, chegou ao Tribunal Supremo, na Cidade de Maputo, por volta das 10h10, onde era aguardado pelos juízes responsáveis pelo seu julgamento. Eram dez minutos depois da hora prevista para o arranque da sessão.
Logo à chegada, a viatura que o transportava ficou rodeada de jornalistas de órgãos de comunicação social, tanto nacionais como internacionais, que pretendiam captar as suas declarações. Perante o cenário, o político saiu do veículo e dirigiu-se à imprensa.
Na sua primeira e breve intervenção, Venâncio Mondlane criticou a actuação da imprensa por não ter recorrido à justiça para contestar as restrições impostas à cobertura do processo, à luz do exercício da liberdade de imprensa e do direito à informação.
Na ocasião, o líder do recém-criado partido Anamola defendeu que os órgãos de comunicação social não se deveriam limitar à produção de reportagens e artigos de opinião, mas sim adoptar medidas com eficácia jurídica para defender os seus direitos.
No entender do político, os jornalistas foram impedidos de exercer a liberdade de imprensa, o que, consequentemente, condicionou o direito dos cidadãos ao acesso à informação.
“Era obrigação da imprensa nacional tomar uma acção concertada para fazer valer os seus próprios direitos”, afirmou Mondlane. Para o político, a responsabilidade pela ausência de uma contestação judicial não deve ser atribuída ao tribunal, mas aos próprios jornalistas.
Venâncio Mondlane falava à comunicação social momentos antes de entrar no edifício do Tribunal Supremo, no centro da Cidade de Maputo. De seguida, escoltado, dirigiu-se ao interior da instituição para o início do julgamento, cuja sessão poderá terminar às 15h30.

items.title: CDD pede independência dos juízes no julgamento de Venâncio Mondlane

original_payload.original_title: CDD pede independência dos juízes no julgamento de Venâncio Mondlane
original_payload.original_body:
Centro para Democracia e Direitos Humanos (CDD) espera que os juízes responsáveis pelo julgamento de Venâncio Mondlane não tomem decisões influenciadas por interesses ou encomendas políticas. A posição foi manifestada por André Mulungo, minutos antes do início do julgamento, ao defender que os magistrados tenham em consideração as consequências da sua decisão para o futuro do país.
Segundo André Mulundo, uma eventual decisão que coloque Venâncio Mondlane numa situação de inelegibilidade poderá deixá-lo fora da corrida política, fazendo com que o Presidente da República, Daniel Chapo, siga praticamente sozinho, num cenário em que, na sua interpretação, a oposição está fragilizada.
“Os juízes devem ter em mente que têm o futuro da nação nas suas mãos”, afirmou André Mulungo, sublinhando a expectativa de que o julgamento decorra com independência e sem interferências políticas.
O pronunciamento foi feito momentos antes do início da sessão de julgamento de Venâncio Mondlane.

original_payload.original_body:
A Primeira-Dama, Gueta Chapo, orienta,hoje, a cerimónia central alusiva ao Dia Mundial do Prematuro, no Centro de Saúde de Moamba, na província de Maputo. A iniciativa pretende sensibilizar as famílias e comunidades para a prevenção dos partos prematuros e a melhoria dos cuidados aos recém-nascidos.
A cerimónia, marcada para as 09h00, vai centrar-se na importância do início atempado das consultas pré-natais, na identificação precoce dos factores de risco associados ao parto prematuro e na prestação de cuidados adequados aos bebés que nascem antes do tempo previsto.
A iniciativa destaca igualmente a promoção do Método Mãe Canguru, uma prática de cuidados aos recém-nascidos prematuros e de baixo peso.
Celebrado anualmente a 17 de Novembro, o Dia Mundial do Prematuro chama a atenção para os desafios enfrentados pelos bebés que nascem prematuramente e para a necessidade de garantir o acesso a cuidados neonatais de qualidade, essenciais à sua sobrevivência e desenvolvimento saudável.
A participação da Primeira-Dama enquadra-se no compromisso com a promoção da saúde materno-infantil, a protecção da criança e o bem-estar das famílias moçambicanas.

items.title: Ethiopia Wins Int’l Award for Institutionalizing Climate-Responsive Auditing

original_payload.original_title: Ethiopia Wins Int’l Award for Institutionalizing Climate-Responsive Auditing
original_payload.original_body:
Addis Ababa, November 17, 2026--The Office of the Federal Auditor General has won international recognition for its efforts to institutionalize climate-responsive auditing at the 2026 ClimateScanner Impact Awards held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
The award recognizes OFAG’s efforts to integrate climate change considerations into its institutional structures, strategic planning and auditing practices, according to the ClimateScanner initiative.
In particular, the initiative commended the Office for establishing a dedicated Environmental Performance Audit Department, integrating climate-responsive auditing into its Strategic Plan for 2026–2031.
The achievements demonstrate OFAG’s efforts to make climate-related auditing an integral part of its institutional operations and long-term strategic direction, it stated.
The winners of the 2026 ClimateScanner Impact Awards were selected by an international panel of judges comprising representatives of Supreme Audit Institutions (SAIs) and partner organizations.
The awards were announced during a special ceremony held as part of the ClimateScanner Summit 2026 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on November 5–6.
ClimateScanner is a global collaborative initiative led by Supreme Audit Institutions from more than 100 countries to assess government responses to climate change.
The initiative provides a framework for evaluating government actions on climate change and strengthening accountability through independent public-sector auditing.

items.title: Mozambique opposition leader faces trial over deadly 2024 election unrest

original_payload.original_title: Mozambique opposition leader faces trial over deadly 2024 election unrest
original_payload.original_body:
Mozambique opposition leader faces trial over deadly 2024 election unrest
Image source,  AFP via Getty Images
Image caption,    Venâncio Mondlane was the runner-up in the 2024 presidential election
By   Jose Tembe   ,   Reporting from Maputo       and    Wycliffe Muia
Published
17 November 2026, 08:22 GMT
Updated 1 hour ago
Tensions are running high in Mozambique's capital, Maputo, with a heavy police deployment as a prominent opposition leader goes on trial over deadly protests that followed the country's disputed 2024 elections.
Venâncio Mondlane faces several charges, including incitement to terrorism and civil disobedience, over protests that left hundreds of people dead. He denies any wrongdoing.
Security has been tightened around the Supreme Court, where Mondlane is due to appear on Tuesday, with authorities fearing a fresh wave of demonstrations by his supporters.
Police have appealed to citizens to follow the proceedings calmly and avoid actions that could threaten public order.
The trial is widely seen as a major test of Mozambique's political stability, nearly two years after disputed elections triggered some of the country's deadliest political unrest in decades.
"The trial is a real test for Mozambique. It is is an important opportunity to demonstrate that the rule of law applies equally to everyone," said Luis Nhachote, a political analyst.
Mondlane, who challenged the presidential election results that declared Daniel Chapo of the ruling Frelimo party the winner, accused the authorities of widespread electoral fraud and called for nationwide protests and work stoppages.
Children shot dead after joining pot-banging protests in Mozambique
Published
23 November 2024
The demonstrations continued for months, with rights groups accusing security forces of using excessive force against protesters.
Amnesty International, citing local civil society organisations, said more than 300 people were killed during the unrest, which was one of the country's worst post-election crises since independence.
Mozambican police put the death toll at 96, including 17 police officers.
European Union election observers also reported irregularities in the October 2024 vote, raising questions about the credibility of the results.
Image source,  AFP via Getty Images
Image caption,    About 96 people died during the 2024 protests, according to police
Prosecutors accuse Mondlane of encouraging demonstrations that disrupted public services, damaged property and threatened public security.
The charges include publicly glorifying criminal acts, incitement to collective disobedience, public instigation to commit crimes and offences linked to terrorism.
He could face up to 24 years in prison if convicted of the most serious charge.
Mondlane has rejected the accusations, insisting that his calls for demonstrations were aimed at demanding electoral transparency rather than encouraging violence.
His party, the National Alliance for a Free and Autonomous Mozambique (Anamola), has described the prosecution as politically motivated.
The Supreme Court has denied allegations of political interference in the proceedings.
A heavy deployment of police has been seen patrolling around the Supreme Court and major streets in Maputo ahead of the trial.
In a statement issued on Monday, Mozambique's police appealed to citizens to  "preserve tolerance and peaceful coexistence," adding that the right to demonstrate must be exercised strictly within the limits of the law.
Police also pledged to protect people and property while acting preventively and proportionately in accordance with the rule of law.
The court has only granted access to selected media organisations, sparking criticism from journalists and press freedom campaigners.
Court officials say the restrictions are necessary because of limited seating capacity in the courtroom, but critics argue they undermine transparency in a case of significant public interest.
The proceedings are expected to be heard by five judges, with witnesses called by both the prosecution and defence.
Political observers warn that the trial could reignite tensions in a country still struggling to recover from the violence and deep political divisions that followed the 2024 elections.

items.title: BBC launches programme for children forced from school by bandits and poverty in West Africa

original_payload.original_title: BBC launches programme for children forced from school by bandits and poverty in West Africa
original_payload.original_body:
BBC launches programme for children forced from school by bandits and poverty in West Africa
Image source,  Ifiokabasi Ettang/BBC
Image caption,    Hadiza left school at 13 to get married and now spends her time doing housework
By  Madina Maishanu   BBC Africa   ,   Reporting from Goronyo
Published
17 November 2026, 00:08 GMT
As she pounds millet, 15-year-old Hadiza sings the English alphabet. It is a reminder of something that she desperately misses - going to school.
"Sometimes I write on the ground to practise and see if I'm still writing correctly," she says.
One night, about two years ago, a group of armed men raided her village.
"They scared our cattle away and abducted a girl. We had to run away. We walked barefoot all the way here," she says.
Since then she has lived in a displaced persons camp in Goronyo, a few kilometres from her home. For a short while she went to school here, but soon met a young man and, at the age of 13, stopped going to classes and got married.
"It's tradition here that once a girl is married, her education ends," she explains.
Now she lives with her in-laws and helps look after the home.
Although Nigerian law prohibits marriage under the age of 18, it is not always enforced.
Image source,  Ifiokabasi Ettang/BBC
Image caption,    Hadiza practises writing on the ground to make sure she doesn't forget the English alphabet
Hadiza is one of nearly 19 million children in Nigeria who are missing out on an education, according to estimates shared by Unesco in 2024. That's about one in four of the country's school-age children.
Against this backdrop, the BBC World Service has launched Dars Hausa, an educational programme in the main language spoken in northern Nigeria, as well as neighbouring Niger, Cameroon and elsewhere in West Africa.
It brings English, maths and science lessons to children across West Africa, via social media, local television partnerships and radio. Many people in the region get their news from the radio and nearly half of households in Nigeria have one, according to the charity Save the Children.
Dars means "lesson" in Pashto and Dari, and it was first launched in those languages in 2023 for Afghan children barred from attending school. An Arabic version followed in February 2025.
The reasons why so many Nigerian children are out of school are numerous and complex. Like Hadiza, 12-year-old Rukayya also lives in the displacement camp in Goronyo.
Image source,  Ifiokabasi Ettang/BBC
Image caption,    After Rukayya's father was killed, she gave up school to earn money instead
"It pains me to see other children studying and going to school while I cannot," she says.
As the eldest child, each day Rukayya goes out to gather firewood to sell and to beg so that her younger siblings can have something to eat.
"If my father was alive, I wouldn't have to go out and beg," she explains, saying some people mock her "but it doesn't stop me because it is our only way to survive."
Bandits killed her father about a year ago in front of her, she says, and her family fled from their home to the camp.
She and Hadiza are among 670,000 people in north-west and central Nigeria who have been forced from their homes by armed robbery and kidnappings, according to the International Organization for Migration.
Three Girls: Lessons in Limbo features the stories of Hadiza and Rukayya - you can    watch the full film on YouTube  ,  external
Some attacks have been carried out by militant Islamist groups, but the majority in this region are by criminal gangs, known in Nigeria as bandits, who steal, kill and kidnap.
The school that Hadiza once attended in Goronyo is the only one serving children in the camp and typically has about 50 students in each class.
One of the teachers, Kamilu Sulaiman Jakada, says that even though lessons are free, only a tiny portion of the children attend, and even then sporadically, because parents tell him that "it is the children that are the breadwinners" and they need to earn money to eat.
Image source,  Ifiokabasi Ettang/BBC
Image caption,    Armed gangs, poverty and lack of funding all have a huge impact on children's education, says teacher Kamilu Sulaiman Jakada
He says the school does not have enough teachers or classrooms, explaining that funding is inconsistent and often comes from individuals or organisations rather than the government.
The other challenge is the bandits. A gang once came to the school on motorbikes, shooting in the air, he says, and although no-one was hurt, many parents were scared and withdrew their children. That has been parents' reaction to attacks in some other parts of the country too.
Every Nigerian child is meant to get nine years of free, compulsory education - six in primary and three in secondary school. Responsibility is shared between federal, state and local governments.
But many schools are facing shortages and poorer families who cannot afford private education can struggle to pay for uniforms, books and transport.
The crisis has built up over decades, with successive governments struggling to address chronic underfunding and poor oversight of resources.
In addition, many children in the traditional Almajiri system, which provides Islamic education, are not taught subjects such as maths and science, and are considered by Unicef to be out of school.
Image source,  Ifiokabasi Ettang/BBC
Image caption,    Many of Nigeria's schools face shortages of teachers, classrooms and learning materials after years of underfunding and lack of oversight
Minister of State for Education Prof Suwaiba Sa'id believes the number of children out of school is lower than has been reported, but admits that with Nigeria's growing population "the proper investment, the proper oversight, has not been done… I will not mention the names, but we know of two states that did not recruit a single teacher for eight years".
She says that education is the government's "number-one priority" and initiatives such as Lumina are designed to help address "decades of neglect". Lumina aims to support one million girls by 2030, providing an accelerated learning programme for older girls who have missed years of formal education.
She also says that "the government is doing everything possible" to deal with bandits and that "we have seen children that should be at school but are engaged in this banditry".
In the meantime, it is children like Hadiza and Rukayya that the BBC World Service Dars Hausa programmes aim to help. Hadiza says she still has a dream to one day become a doctor "to help my fellow women".
Dars Hausa will air on BBC News Hausa radio on Sundays at 06:45 West Africa Time, with a repeat at 20:45. The programme will also be available via BBC News Hausa's digital platforms, including YouTube, Facebook, X and Instagram.

items.title: Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate

original_payload.original_title: Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate
original_payload.original_body:
Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate
Image source,  Peel Regional Police
Image caption,    Canadian authorities say organised vehicle theft is a serious crime threatening the security of communities
By  Basillioh Rukanga
Published
2 hours ago
Canadian police have arrested 12 suspects, including eight Nigerians, in an investigation into an alleged car theft syndicate.
They are accused of stealing luxury vehicles and shipping them to West Africa.
Police in Peel, Ontario said they had recovered 96 high-value vehicles concealed in shipping containers. The vehicles, valued at $4.5m (£3.4m) were destined for export via Canadian ports.
The trafficking of vehicles from North America and Europe to African countries has been a long-standing concern for law enforcement agencies.
The suspects face 231 charges, with arrest warrants issued for others. Police say some of the accused may face deportation after their criminal proceedings are concluded.
The arrests followed months of what police described as an "extensive auto theft investigation".
The investigations began in March in partnership with Canada's border agency after police identified a warehouse allegedly being used to store stolen vehicles.
Investigators believe the network was led by five people who coordinated the theft, transportation and export of the stolen vehicles, with the others playing supporting roles.
"Together, investigators linked the network to loading sites, container movements and the transportation of stolen re-VINed vehicles," the police said in a statement.
Re-VINing is the illegal practice of altering the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) to conceal its identity and make it harder to trace.
Canadian authorities have described organised vehicle theft as a growing threat, saying it was linked to wider criminal networks.
"Organised auto theft is a predatory business model run by transnational syndicates that terrorise families and fund broader criminal enterprises," Peel Regional Police Deputy Chief Nick Milinovich said.
Last year, Interpol said more than 100 luxury vehicles stolen from Canada and European countries had been recovered, exposing a network involved in trafficking stolen cars to West Africa.
In a separate operation the same year, Ghanaian security authorities recovered 43 luxury vehicles stolen from Europe and North America.
They attributed the success of the operation to improved cooperation between national and international law enforcement agencies.

items.title: 'Is that not match-fixing?' - Erasmus questions officiating

original_payload.original_title: 'Is that not match-fixing?' - Erasmus questions officiating
original_payload.original_body:
'Is that not match-fixing?' - Erasmus questions officiating
Image source,  Getty Images
Image caption,    Rassie Erasmus questioned standards in officiating before South Africa's game with Ireland on Saturday
By  Andy Gray   BBC Sport NI Journalist
Published
16 November 2026
South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has predicted Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast will not face a ban after being cited, and questioned what he perceived as double standards in officiating to the point where he asked: "is that not match-fixing?"
Prendergast became the first player to be cited under World Rugby's new regulations for a hip-drop tackle against Fiji and could be banned for Saturday's Nations Championship match.
Speaking at a media conference on Monday, Erasmus said the 23-year-old's tackle was "terrible", but he believes Prendergast will be free to play against the Springboks in Dublin because of a "technicality".
The 54-year-old also added that he thought it was an "immediate red card" when he saw the tackle occur in the first half of Ireland's 43-15 win, but it was not penalised in-game by referee Angus Gardner or by the television match official Mike Adamson.
"I must say the right words now. We are in the northern hemisphere. I think there is going to be a technicality and he is going to play," Erasmus said when asked about Prendergast being cited.
When he was asked to elaborate on what he meant by a "technicality", Erasmus said that, while he is "not a legal guy", "it never seems to go our way".
"I'm not saying anybody's doing anything wrong. I'm just not expecting him to get [suspended] - I think he'll play on Saturday," Erasmus said.
World Rugby has been approached for comment by BBC Sport.
Erasmus, who said "I swear I'm not moaning", also pointed to how Ireland prop  Tadhg Furlong avoided punishment  for an alleged groin grab in Leinster's United Rugby Championship win over Munster in October.
Last year, South Africa prop  Jan-Hendrik Wessels was handed a nine-match ban  for a similar offence and missed November's matches for the Springboks.
"Tadhg got off free for the same thing Jan-Hendrik did. I don't want to go into details because I'm not a legal person, but from a South African point of view, that hurt," added Erasmus.
"I'm telling you now for any neutral - and I'm not saying the neutrals are right - but for anybody that looks at that situation on exactly the same two things that happened, one guy's word was taken, and another guy's word was not taken.
"One guy got nine weeks. He didn't play for the Springboks, and the other guy played the next weekend. That's all I'm saying."
In 2021, when he was South Africa's director of rugby, Erasmus was banned for two months by World Rugby for an hour-long video criticising the refereeing in the Springboks' first-Test defeat by the British and Irish Lions.
World Rugby found the video contained "multiple abusive and insulting comments and attacks on the officials".
The following year, he received a two-match ban for a series of tweets criticising officials in a defeat by France.
Prendergast cited and could miss South Africa game
Published
20 hours ago
'Not an accusation'
Erasmus said there had been a meeting with World Rugby over the implementation of new laws surrounding the hip-drop and knee-drop tackle for November's internationals, which Ireland and France coaches didn't attend.
Hip and knee-drop tackles are when the tackling player drops their body weight on the legs of the ball carrier, and Fiji captain Peceli Yato was eventually forced off with an injury against Ireland after initially continuing following Prendergast's tackle.
South Africa head into this weekend's game in Dublin off the back of a 21-19 defeat by France at the Stade de France on Saturday.
After saying he would get in trouble if he showed video evidence, Erasmus said that 17 hip-drop or knee-drop tackles by French players were not penalised by match referee Andrea Piardi or the TMO Matteo Liperini in Paris - 11 of which he thought were penalties and three which he felt should have been yellow cards.
To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser.
This video can not be played
Figure caption,    Highlights: France narrowly beat South Africa in thriller in Paris
Erasmus said his comments were "not an accusation" about the officials, and questioned World Rugby's prerogative to limit interruptions from the TMO.
"I'm saying if he didn't see it, it must be a technology problem. If he saw it and decided not to act on it, is that not match-fixing?" Erasmus added.
"Is that not interfering with the outcome of a game if you see this injury that happened there, a knee-drop tackle happened there, and it's been decided that knee-drop tackles are out?"
Erasmus said his players spoke to Piardi and the officials about the number of knee-drop tackles, and he doubled down on his views over the lack of intervention from the TMO.
"They happened 17 in our games. Not one was penalised even," Erasmus said.
"If the TMO didn't see it, maybe then technology must be better. If he saw it and he ignored it, what does that boil down to? Manipulation of the game or the result or injured players getting injured.
"So all I'm asking, don't take TMOs out and discourage them to get involved. Then the wrong team will win and players will get injured. That's all I'm saying."

items.title: Ouverture à Agadez d’un atelier de planification du Projet de renforcement de la stabilité et du relèvement socio-économique

original_payload.original_title: Ouverture à Agadez d’un atelier de planification du Projet de renforcement de la stabilité et du relèvement socio-économique
original_payload.original_body:
Agadez, 17 novembre 2026 (ANP) – Le Secrétaire Général du Gouvernorat d’Agadez, M. Souleymane Saïdou Boulhassan a présidé, ce Mardi 17 Novembre 2026 dans la salle de réunion du Gouvernorat, la cérémonie d’ouverture de l’atelier régional de planification du Projet « Renforcement de la stabilité et du relèvement socio-économique (2026-2030) ».
Durant trois jours, les participants échangeront sur la mise en place d’un dispositif régional de suivi opérationnel, comprenant un comité régional de suivi dont les responsabilités seront clairement définies. Ils travailleront également à l’identification des priorités régionales hiérarchisées à partir des besoins exprimés par les communes et les communautés, notamment les femmes, les jeunes et les populations des localités les plus éloignées. Les travaux porteront aussi sur l’élaboration d’une programmation réaliste pour 2026 et 2027, qui précise les activités, les responsabilités et un calendrier compatible avec les ressources disponibles. Il s’agira enfin de définir des modalités claires de coordination, de gestion des risques et de redevabilité, en tenant compte des initiatives en cours et des tensions locales.
En ouvrant les travaux, le secrétaire général du gouvernorat d’Agadez a d’abord fait observer que « la région d’Agadez, à l’instar de celles de Tahoua et de Tillabéri, rencontre presque les mêmes défis en matière de sécurité, d’accès à certains services sociaux de base, de bon fonctionnement des institutions locales, de bonne gouvernance et de perspectives de développement ». Face à ces défis, il a indiqué que « la réponse de l’État doit être à la fois cohérente, territorialisée et durable. Elle doit permettre de renforcer la présence et l’efficacité de l’administration, de consolider la confiance entre les populations et les institutions et de créer les conditions d’un retour progressif à la stabilité ».
Il a également fait savoir que « la stabilité de nos communautés ne saurait être envisagée sans une administration territoriale forte, des institutions de proximité fonctionnelles et une participation active des communautés aux décisions qui les concernent », soulignant qu’au-delà de ses interventions en matière de cohésion sociale, d’accès aux services essentiels et de relèvement économique, « ce projet constitue une opportunité stratégique pour renforcer la gouvernance territoriale, améliorer la coordination des interventions et consolider le rôle des Autorités Administratives dans la prévention des conflits et la stabilité des Communautés ».
À cet égard, M. Souleymane Saïdou Boulhassan a insisté sur trois impératifs majeurs qui doivent guider les travaux de cet atelier. Le premier impératif est celui de l’appropriation et de la responsabilité institutionnelle. Les autorités régionales, départementales et communales, en collaboration avec les services techniques et les acteurs communautaires, doivent pleinement assumer leur rôle dans l’identification des besoins, la coordination des interventions et le suivi des résultats. La mise en place du comité régional de suivi devra ainsi permettre de disposer d’un mécanisme de gouvernance fonctionnel, capable d’assurer une coordination efficace entre les différents acteurs et de garantir un suivi régulier des engagements pris.
Le deuxième impératif est celui de la cohérence territoriale et de la priorisation stratégique. Les interventions doivent répondre aux réalités spécifiques des communes et des communautés concernées, tout en s’inscrivant dans une vision régionale cohérente. À ce titre, il a invité les participants à privilégier des priorités consensuelles, réalistes et à fort impact, en tenant compte des besoins des populations, des contraintes sécuritaires et des capacités de mise en œuvre. « Il ne s’agit pas de dresser un catalogue de besoins, mais de faire des choix stratégiques susceptibles de produire des résultats concrets et durables », a-t-il déclaré.
Enfin, le troisième impératif est celui de la coordination, de la redevabilité et de la durabilité. Les autorités compétentes doivent veiller à la complémentarité des interventions, à la mobilisation des services compétents et à la participation effective des communautés, notamment des femmes, des jeunes et des groupes vulnérables.
Le Secrétaire Général du Gouvernorat d’Agadez a enfin rappelé l’engagement du Ministère en charge de l’Intérieur à accompagner, à travers ses structures centrales et territoriales, la mise en œuvre de cette initiative. Il a également rassuré les participants quant à l’ambition dudit Ministère de faire de ce partenariat un instrument concret de renforcement de la gouvernance territoriale, de consolidation de la présence de l’État et de promotion d’une stabilité durable.
« Au-delà des ressources mobilisées et des activités programmées, notre véritable réussite sera de bâtir des territoires mieux gouvernés, des institutions plus efficaces et des communautés durablement résilientes », a-t-il conclu.

items.title: Niger : Nomination des nouveaux SG aux ministères de la défense et de l’intérieur

items.title: Décès d’Abdou Tidiane Diop et d’Adama Diallo : le Sénégal attend les résultats des autopsies

original_payload.original_title: Décès d’Abdou Tidiane Diop et d’Adama Diallo : le Sénégal attend les résultats des autopsies
original_payload.original_body:
DAKAR, Sénégal, 17 novembre 2026  – Un dîner entre proches, puis deux familles en deuil. À Dakar, la mort d’Abdou Tidiane Diop, petit-fils de l’ancien président Abdou Diouf, et celle d’Adama Salif Diallo, fils de l’ancien député Mamadou Lamine Diallo, tient la capitale sénégalaise en haleine. Les deux amis avaient partagé un repas, et d’autres convives se trouvent toujours à l’hôpital. Lundi soir, personne n’avait encore expliqué ces décès.
Un repas, trois scénarios
L’affaire est sortie dimanche, grâce au site Dakarposte. D’après lui, Abdou Tidiane Diop est mort samedi 14 novembre à la clinique Urgence Cardio, dans le quartier de Mermoz. Il avait enduré trois jours de crampes d’estomac intenses et de vomissements répétés. Né aux États-Unis, ce fils de Yacine Diouf et d’Ibrahima Diop dirigeait une société dans la capitale. Aucune source ne précise la date du décès d’Adama Salif Diallo.

items.title: Guinea jails 200 in wildcat gold mining crackdown

original_payload.original_title: Guinea jails 200 in wildcat gold mining crackdown
original_payload.original_body:
Politics   Guinea
Guinea jails 200 in wildcat gold mining crackdown
Mark Hallam   with AFP, AP
11/17/2026  November 17, 2026    A Conakry court has jailed 22 former local officials from the gold-rich northeastern Siguiri region, as well as 200 people accused of illegal mining. It's part of a wider crackdown that sent thousands fleeing into Mali.
https://p.dw.com/p/5PXXU
Prefer DW on Google
More than 1,000 alleged artisanal gold miners are being tried in Conakry courts in various sessions, such as this one on November 11 Image: Adrien Marotte/AFP       Advertisement
Guinea  on Tuesday jailed 22 former regional administrators and 202 others accused of illegal  gold  mining in the northeastern Siguiri region near the border to  Mali .
This comes as part of a wider crackdown on wildcat mining that has led to violent clashes and forced thousands of people to flee into Mali .
According to the UN Environment Program, unauthorized gold mining is a source of income for more than 300,000 people in Guinea. The country's rich gold mines pull in workers from across West Africa.
Conakry's economic and financial crimes court issued the sentences on Tuesday Image: Adrien Marotte/AFP
What happened in the gold mining trial in Conakry?
Conakry's Court for the Repression of Economic and Financial Offenses sentenced 22 former officials from Siguiri to two years each in prison for complicity in environmental degradation, destruction and water pollution. They were each fined 10 million Guinean francs (around €1,025 or $1,125).
The court also sentenced 202 alleged illegal miners — several of them foreign nationals — to three-year prison sentences. They faced the same charges plus an additional count of mining illegally.
They were ordered to pay a combined fine of 10 billion Guinean francs.
Beyond that, the foreign nationals were banned from Guinean territory for a period of 10 years.
Many miners fled this month's crackdown into neighboring Mali, where they crowded to wait for transportation home to Burkina Faso Image: AFP
Why is Guinea cracking down on illegal mining?
Guinea's government announced a bid to stamp out illegal gold mining earlier this month, saying it wanted to prevent damages to farmland and rivers and other environmental destruction.
These efforts turned violent last week as protesters and security forces clashed in the northeast, with 10 people killed and 13 injured.
More than 1,200 artisanal miners were arrested in Siguiri in November.
Many more fled across the border to nearby Mali, often then having to await transportation to their homes in  Burkina Faso .
Malian authorities say that a total of around 160,000 people have flooded into the country after being driven out of Guinea's gold-rich border regions Image: AFP
Mark Hallam   News and current affairs writer and editor with DW since 2006.          @marks_hallam

items.title: Galaxy Backbone govt email service hits 150,000 accounts

original_payload.original_title: Galaxy Backbone govt email service hits 150,000 accounts
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Galaxy Backbone govt email service hits 150,000 accounts
By  Abdulrahman Kadiri   ·   46 seconds ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Jessica Dogo
Galaxy Backbone (GBB) Ltd. says its Government Email Service, GOVMAIL, has recorded over 150,000 accounts, strengthening secure digital communication across Nigeria’s public sector.
The Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of GBB, Prof. Ibrahim Adeyanju, said this in a statement signed by the Head, Corporate Communications and Marketing, Mr Chidi Okpala, on Tuesday in Abuja.
Adeyanju said that the growing adoption reflected increasing confidence among public institutions in locally developed and supported digital services.
He said that GOVMAIL was more than an email platform, describing it as part of the company’s commitment to strengthening Nigeria’s digital sovereignty and securing critical government communication infrastructure.
He said the service was designed to support the operational needs of government institutions while providing a locally managed platform for official correspondence and information exchange.
According to him, the increasing reliance on digital communication globally makes it imperative for governments to prioritise the security, reliability and resilience of their communication infrastructure.
“GBB is leveraging its local digital capabilities to provide government institutions with secure communication services and responsive technical support.
“A major strength of GOVMAIL is the technology infrastructure and security ecosystem supporting its operations,” he said.
He explained that GBB operated a 24-hour Security Operations Centre (SOC), which provided continuous security monitoring and incident response capabilities.
He added that the company also operates multiple world-class data centres supporting hosting, cloud services, backup and disaster recovery.
He said that the facilities contribute to service resilience, business continuity and the sustainability of critical government digital operations.
Adeyanju said that the company’s proximity to its customers and stakeholders enabled it to respond more quickly to their needs, understand operational challenges and provide appropriate support.
He said that although global technology platforms remained important to the digital ecosystem, governments needed to invest in complementary local capabilities to maintain greater control over critical digital infrastructure.
He said that locally supported platforms offered institutional understanding, responsive customer engagement and the technical capacity required to sustain government digital services.
He said the continued growth of GOVMAIL demonstrated GBB’s commitment to providing dependable shared Information and Communication Technology services to improve communication and collaboration among government institutions.
“The initiative also aligns with the company’s broader mandate of providing digital infrastructure to accelerate public sector transformation,” he said.
He said GBB would continue to strengthen the platform, improve customer experience and ensure that the service delivered value to government institutions and public servants.
Adeyanju reaffirmed the company’s commitment to building local digital competencies and providing secure, reliable infrastructure to support Nigeria’s evolving public sector digital needs. (NAN)
Edited by Uche Anunne

items.title: AfCFTA: Conference seeks removal of barriers to boost intra-African trade

original_payload.original_title: AfCFTA: Conference seeks removal of barriers to boost intra-African trade
original_payload.original_body:
Economy/Business  AfCFTA: Conference seeks removal of barriers to boost intra-African trade
By  Tosin Kolade   ·   52 minutes ago   ·  2 min read
✓
✓
​‌‌‍‌‌⁠‍⁠⁠‍‍‍​By Lucy Ogalue
An international conference on the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) and the geoeconomics of African states has urged governments to remove trade barriers and simplify customs procedures to boost intra-African trade.
The call is contained in a communiqué issued by Prof. Ngozi Egbuna, Director of ICRITR, Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka, on Tuesday.
The communiqué was jointly signed by Dr Justin Amase, Chairman of the Conference Communiqué Drafting Committee, and Dr Manfred Kouty, Coordinator of the Africa Trade Group (ATG) and Co-Chair representing Cameroon.
The conference identified tariff and non-tariff barriers, fragmented customs procedures and inadequate infrastructure as major constraints to continental trade.
It called for a shift “from formal agreements and protocols towards practical measures” to facilitate the movement of goods, services, capital and people across African markets.
The conference urged governments to accelerate the implementation of AfCFTA protocols and commitments to strengthen trade integration across the continent.
It also emphasised the need to promote regional industrialisation, local value addition, technology transfer and stronger African participation in regional and global value chains.
On Africa’s global trade position, the communiqué called for coordinated strategies to protect the continent’s economic interests amid changing geopolitical and international trade relations.
It further urged investment in transport, energy, logistics and digital infrastructure to reduce business costs and facilitate regional trade.
The conference described AfCFTA as more than a trade liberalisation initiative, noting that it represented a strategic instrument for Africa’s economic transformation and industrial development.
It said the success of the agreement would depend on political will, institutional capacity, policy coordination and sustained investments to translate commitments into tangible economic outcomes.
The conference reaffirmed that AfCFTA represented more than a trade liberalisation initiative.
“It is a strategic instrument for Africa’s economic transformation, industrial development, regional integration and enhanced participation in global economic governance.
“The success of the AfCFTA will depend not merely on the commitments contained in its founding agreement and protocols, but on the political will.
“It will also depend on institutional capacity, policy coordination and sustained investments required to translate these commitments into tangible economic outcomes,” the communiqué stated.
The conference, organised by the African Trade Group under the WTO Chairs Programme, held from Nov. 9 to Nov. 10.
It brought together policymakers, trade experts, academics, regional organisations, private-sector representatives and development institutions to deliberate on Africa’s trade and economic prospects. (NAN)
Edited by Abiemwense Moru

items.title: 2027: Tinubu has no formidable opposition – Kalu

original_payload.original_title: 2027: Tinubu has no formidable opposition – Kalu
original_payload.original_body:
Politics  2027: Tinubu has no formidable opposition – Kalu
By  Nefisetu Yakubu   ·   1 hour ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Nefishetu Yakubu
The Senator representing Abia North Senatorial District, Sen. Orji Kalu, has said that President Bola Tinubu has no formidable opposition in the 2027 presidential election.
Kalu stated this while receiving the ‘Best Impactful Representation’ award from the Senate Press Corps on Tuesday in Abuja.
The former governor of Abia, who noted that opposition parties had started their political calculations too late, added that their inability to agree on leadership had weakened their chances.
“If they had sincerely come together, it would have given APC a headache, but not a win. The game is already too late,” he said.
According to him, the opposition parties may struggle to agree on a consensus presidential candidate capable of challenging the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).
He maintained that APC enjoyed massive grassroots support nationwide and remained firmly positioned to retain power in 2027.
“We are not afraid of any party. APC is the ruling party and we have massive grassroots support,” he declared.
Kalu, however, condemned the use of thugs, intimidation and physical attacks during campaigns, urging politicians to embrace peaceful democratic engagement.
He said that elections should be determined by candidates’ records, achievements and capacity to deliver good governance rather than violence and intimidation.
“Nobody has asked anybody to go and fight or engage in violence. Campaigns should be fought based on what candidates have done,” he stated.
He added that political disagreements should not destroy personal relationships among leaders or undermine national unity.
“Tinubu, Atiku, Obi, Makinde and others are all friends who eat at the same table. Nigeria needs unity. We don’t need fighting,” he said.
On allegations that Abia deputy governor was sponsoring thugs against Tinubu’s supporters, Kalu cautioned public office holders against involvement in political violence.
He, however, said he had no verified evidence linking the deputy governor to the allegation and did not personally believe the claims.
The senator urged Gov. Alex Otti to counsel his deputy on conduct that would promote democratic stability, while calling security agencies to investigate the allegation.
He also denied the allegation that he was supplying weapons to the proscribed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB), insisting that he had never supplied arms.
Kalu clarified that international arms transactions were legitimate only when conducted by licensed entities and in compliance with relevant regulatory requirements.
Reacting to a prophecy that he would become Nigeria’s president before he clocks 70, Kalu said he currently had no presidential ambition.
“The will of God is always the will of God, and nobody can stop it. I am capable, but for now, I have no ambition,” he said.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Kalu had earlier been presented the award for his constituency development initiatives since his election into the senate in 2019.
The award citation highlighted projects across the five local government areas that make up Abia North senatorial district, particularly infrastructure, education, healthcare and economic empowerment.
It credited the senator with constructing and rehabilitating more than 160 rural and agricultural access roads across the senatorial district.
The citation also highlighted educational interventions, including classroom construction, scholarships, learning materials and payment of examination fees for beneficiaries.
It further listed healthcare facilities, solar-powered streetlights, boreholes, agricultural support programmes and empowerment initiatives among his constituency projects.
In his acceptance speech, Kalu dedicated the award to the late President Muhammadu Buhari and President Bola Tinubu for their support for his senatorial district, and to the people of Abia North for their continued support.
He disclosed that more than 49 additional roads were under construction across the district, subject to the release of relevant budgetary funds.
“If the budget has been released, there are more than 49 new roads currently being constructed in the district,” he said.
Kalu said his responsibility as an elected representative was to serve the people and ensure that citizens benefitted from public resources.
“What is meant for the public is for the public. My duty is to serve the people,” he stated.
The former governor explained that infrastructure and education investments offered more sustainable economic benefits than conventional empowerment programmes involving periodic distribution of material items.
“I don’t mostly do empowerment because empowerment is not the way to save the economy. We have to go back to providing roads,” he stated.
He urged Nigerians to embrace punctuality, discipline and commitment to their professional responsibilities, stressing that hard work remained essential for national development.(NAN)
NY/WAS

original_payload.original_body:
Metro  Wike approves promotion of 7,714 FCT workers
By  Philip Daniel Yatai   ·   2 hours ago   ·  2 min read
✓
✓
By Philip Yatai
The  Minister   of   the   Federal   Capital   Territory   (FCT),   Mr   Nyesom   Wike,   has   approved   the   promotion   of   4,220   teachers   and   3,494   other   civil   servants   in   the   territory.
The Chairman of the FCT Civil Service Commission (CSC), Mr Emeka Ezeh, announced this in a statement in Abuja on Tuesday, saying the approval followed the conclusion of the commission’s 2025 and 2026 promotion exercises.
Ezeh described the development as part of the administration’s efforts to boost workers’ morale, noting that Wike had directed the commission to clear all inherited promotion backlogs.
“You will also recall that the minister approved that education officers who disrupted the 2025 promotion exercise be pardoned and allowed to participate in the 2026 exercise.
“The commission subsequently invited all 2025 and 2026 eligible education officers to participate in the just-concluded exercise,” Ezeh said.
He congratulated the successful candidates and urged them to reciprocate the gesture through the diligent discharge of their duties.
Ezeh also said that the commission would conduct its second pre-retirement workshop on Dec. 16, 2026, for 116 FCT Administration workers scheduled to retire between Jan. 1 and March 31, 2027.
He explained that the workshop was designed to prepare the outgoing workers for life after public service.
The  News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)  reports that the minister approved the promotion of 3,592 civil servants in July following the completion of the 2025 promotion exercise.  ( NAN )

items.title: Rhythm spirit idol winner urges youths to shun peer pressure, pursue dreams

original_payload.original_title: Rhythm spirit idol winner urges youths to shun peer pressure, pursue dreams
original_payload.original_body:
Culture & Tourism  Rhythm spirit idol winner urges youths to shun peer pressure, pursue dreams
By  Folashade Adeniran   ·   2 hours ago   ·  Updated  9 seconds ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Glory ​‌⁠⁠⁠⁠‍⁠⁠‍‍‍​‌​⁠⁠‍‌​Akpan
Festus Ovuede , winner of Rhythm Spirit Idol Season 2, has urged youths to remain committed to their dreams and shun peer pressure and quick-money schemes.
Ovuede made this known in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) after emerging winner of the music competition in Lagos.
The event took place on Sunday.
Ovuede, who works with a technical company, attributed his victory to determination, saying he returned for the second season after failing to win in the previous edition.
“Self-determination brought me this far because after I couldn’t make it in Season 1, I didn’t lose hope but decided to return a second time in the competition.
“I really didn’t see myself winning this contest because the talents I met were amazing, but I was determined to fight for a win.
“My message to youths is that they should always pursue their dreams positively.
“I want to be somebody that history would remember, so I decided to come back and fight for a win,” he said.
Testimony Otume, who emerged second, said she felt honoured by her position but was challenged by the impressive performances of other contestants.
“I really feel honoured with this position but at first, I really felt challenged with the efforts of the other contestants because I came across real music talents in this competition.
“My experience here as a youth teaches me and other youths out there never to look down on yourself.
“Always be determined and push up as long as you’re doing something positive,” she said.
She said the experience had taught her and other youths to believe in themselves, remain determined and pursue positive goals.
Stephanie Obute, third place winner of Rhythm Spirit Idol Season 2, and award winner for Best Artistic Creativity
Meanwhile, Stephanie Obute, an undergraduate who emerged third and won the award for Best Artistic Creativity, expressed gratitude to God and her family for their support.
Obute, the youngest contestant, said her first experience performing on a public stage had taught her valuable lessons about music competitions and exposed her to talented singers.
She called on the government to invest in music talents, describing the sector as an avenue for promoting Nigeria’s tourism and showcasing the country’s creativity internationally.
The organiser of the competition, Mr Stuff Mukoro, said his inspiration to develop young musical talents was partly drawn from the experience of late singer Mohbad.
Mukoro said he wanted to provide talented youths with platforms to showcase their abilities and avoid pressures that could lead them into negative influences.
Mukoro said he wanted to provide talented youths with platforms to showcase their abilities and avoid pressures that could lead them into negative influences.
According to him, the competition seeks to discover versatile singers with originality, creativity and stage presence.
He said the initiative was also aimed at reducing youth idleness and frustration by providing opportunities for aspiring musicians to develop their talents.
“The streets are not smiling, there’s so much frustration, no jobs and for many youths, music is just something that still makes meaning in their lives and we want to help them achieve their dreams,” he said.
Mukoro said the winner received N1 million, a one-year music ambassadorial appointment and an opportunity to record a track with a notable record label.
He added that the second-place contestant received N500,000, while the third-place winner received N200,000, alongside consolation prizes for outstanding performances.
NAN reports that the maiden edition winner, Joseph Chinonso, was also present at the event to witness the performances of emerging musical talents. (NAN)www.nannews.ng

FOLLOWING the remand of FIJ journalist Daniel Ojukwu over reports concerning projects linked to the Office of the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Sustainable Development Goals (OSSAP-SDGs), The ICIR revisits investigations by media organisations across five states between 2023 and 2026, which exposed questionable contracts running into billions of naira in public funds and projects that were either not executed, diverted from their intended locations or left unused under the office headed by presidential aide Adejoke Orelope-Adefulire.
At Hammadu-Kafi Primary School in Akko Local Government Area of Gombe State, 11-year-old Khalid Adam learnt to arrive early if he wanted a seat in class.
The Primary V pupil was among about 2,000 children attending a school with only seven classrooms and 22 teachers. Those who arrived late often had to sit on the bare floor.
“Most of us do not have seats. We sit on the floor because there are not enough seats in the school,” Khalid told WikkiTimes during a visit in May 2023.
Procurement irregularities linked to former OSSAP-SDGs Adejoke Orelope-Adefulire    Findings showed the school had been operating morning and afternoon shifts to accommodate its pupils, with some classrooms holding at least 160 children. While three or four pupils shared desks designed for two, more than half of the pupils in some classes sat on dusty floors.

items.title: 29ᵉ Conférence des GRH : Trois résultats attendus pour une gestion plus rigoureuse des agents de l'État

original_payload.original_title: 29ᵉ Conférence des GRH : Trois résultats attendus pour une gestion plus rigoureuse des agents de l'État
original_payload.original_body:
La 29ᵉ Conférence des Gestionnaires des Ressources Humaines s'est ouverte le mercredi 11 novembre 2026 à Kandi, dans le département de l'Alibori. Organisée par le Ministère de la Décentralisation et de la Gouvernance Locale (MDGL), cette rencontre de deux jours est consacrée à la gestion de la position administrative des agents de l'État élus au sein des conseils communaux. Cette question revêt une importance particulière pour la bonne gestion des carrières des agents concernés, le respect des dispositions réglementaires et le fonctionnement des administrations publiques.
Placée sous la coordination de la Direction de la Planification, de l'Administration et des Finances (DPAF), la Conférence réunit les Secrétaires généraux des douze départements et les responsables des ressources humaines des préfectures. Elle constitue un cadre de concertation et d'harmonisation des pratiques administratives.
À l'ouverture des travaux, le Préfet de l'Alibori, Monsieur Bello KY-SAMAH, a rappelé la nécessité de disposer d'une administration moderne, transparente, équitable et performante. Il a souligné l'importance d'une gestion rigoureuse de la situation administrative des agents de l'État qui exercent des mandats électifs au sein des communes, afin de prévenir toute ambiguïté concernant leurs droits et obligations.
Représentant le Ministre de la Décentralisation et de la Gouvernance Locale, la Directrice de cabinet, Madame Mireille GUEDOU MADODE, a insisté sur la responsabilité des gestionnaires des ressources humaines dans la sécurisation des carrières et la régularité des actes administratifs. « Le gestionnaire des ressources humaines n'est pas un simple exécutant de procédures. Il est le premier garant de la sécurité juridique des agents et le premier rempart contre l'irrégularité », a-t-elle déclaré.
Trois résultats concrets attendus.
Au-delà des échanges d'expériences, cette 29ᵉ session doit aboutir à trois résultats prioritaires :
1. Un état des lieux précis de la situation des agents de l'État élus dans les communes de chaque département ;
2. Une procédure harmonisée qui précise les étapes, les actes administratifs et les délais applicables ;
3. Un dispositif de suivi destiné à évaluer les progrès accomplis dès la prochaine session.
Les travaux ont également porté sur l'examen du rapport de la 28ᵉ Conférence, tenue à Parakou, et sur les dispositions administratives relatives à la situation des agents publics élus dans les communes.
À travers cette rencontre, le MDGL entend renforcer la coordination entre l'administration centrale et les préfectures, améliorer la gestion des ressources humaines et garantir une meilleure sécurité juridique aux agents concernés. L'objectif est de parvenir à des pratiques administratives cohérentes, conformes aux textes en vigueur et appliquées de manière uniforme sur l'ensemble du territoire national.

items.title: 48ᵉ Conférence ministérielle de la Francophonie : Le Bénin désigné pour accueillir la prochaine session en 2027

original_payload.original_title: 48ᵉ Conférence ministérielle de la Francophonie : Le Bénin désigné pour accueillir la prochaine session en 2027
original_payload.original_body:
Le Bénin vient d’être désigné pour abriter la prochaine session de la Conférence ministérielle de la Francophonie. La décision a été prise lors des travaux de la 48ème session de cette conférence qui se tient du 14 au 19 novembre 2026 à Phnom Penh, au Cambodge. La Ministre des Affaires étrangères, Madame Corinne AMORI BRUNET, prend part à cette rencontre consacrée aux grandes orientations de la coopération multilatérale dans l’espace francophone.
Placée sous le thème : « Réinvestir dans la paix pour une prospérité partagée et une stabilité durable », cette session réunit les représentants des États et gouvernements membres autour des enjeux de paix, de stabilité et de coopération. Les échanges ont notamment porté sur les priorités communes de l’espace francophone, ainsi que sur les préparatifs du 20ᵉ Sommet de la Francophonie, organisé dans la capitale cambodgienne.
Les travaux de cette 48ᵉ session ont également été consacrés à l’examen de textes destinés à renforcer l’action de l’organisation face aux défis politiques et sécuritaires. Ils devraient notamment aboutir à l’adoption de la Déclaration de Phnom Penh et d’une résolution relative aux situations de crise, de sortie de crise et de consolidation de la paix dans l’espace francophone. Ces orientations traduisent la volonté des membres de renforcer les mécanismes de dialogue et de coopération face aux tensions qui affectent plusieurs régions.
Le choix du Bénin pour abriter la prochaine session de la Conférence ministérielle de l’OIF en 2027, intervient dans un contexte marqué par les réflexions sur l’avenir de la Francophonie et la nécessité de consolider les valeurs de solidarité, de paix et de coopération entre ses membres. Cette désignation témoigne de la reconnaissance de l’engagement du Bénin en faveur du dialogue multilatéral et du rapprochement entre les peuples francophones. Elle offrira au pays une tribune privilégiée pour contribuer aux réflexions sur les défis auxquels est confrontée la Francophonie.
La rencontre de Phnom Penh se poursuit avec l’ouverture du 20ᵉ Sommet des Chefs d’État et de gouvernement de la Francophonie, prévue pour ce dimanche 15 novembre 2026. Une autre échéance importante figure à l’agenda de l’organisation : l’élection du prochain Secrétaire général de l’OIF, programmée pour le lundi 16 novembre. Ces travaux permettront aux dirigeants francophones d’aborder les orientations futures de l’organisation et les moyens de renforcer son action au service de la paix et d’une prospérité partagée.

items.title: UPMB : après une année d’interruption, la fête de Noël des enfants des professionnels des médias fait son grand retour

original_payload.original_title: UPMB : après une année d’interruption, la fête de Noël des enfants des professionnels des médias fait son grand retour
original_payload.original_body:
Suspendue l’année dernière pour des raisons de calendrier, la célébration emblématique de l’UPMB renaît en 2026 sous l’impulsion du Président Hervé Prudence HESSOU.
C’est le retour d’un événement cher à la corporation. Après une année d’interruption, l’Union des Professionnels des Médias du Bénin (UPMB) annonce la relance de la « Noël des enfants des professionnels des médias et des orphelins de la presse », qui signe cette année sa 21ème édition.
Pourquoi l’édition 2025 n’a pas eu lieu ?
Joint par notre rédaction, le Président de l’UPMB, Hervé Prudence HESSOU, a tenu à apporter des clarifications : « L’année dernière, nous n’avons pas pu organiser la fête. Nous avons été élus le 3 décembre, nous avons pris fonction le 8 décembre. Du 8 au 22-25 décembre, il n’y avait matériellement pas la possibilité d’organiser rapidement un événement d’une telle envergure. Nous avons donc fait l’impasse ».
Une décision responsable qui n’aura été qu’une parenthèse. Pour cette année 2026, le nouveau bureau a décidé de redonner vie à cette célébration, symbole de solidarité et de fraternité au sein de la presse béninoise.
Une 21ème édition décentralisée et inclusive
Forte de ses 20 éditions précédentes, cette fête vise à offrir un moment de joie aux enfants (05 à 10 ans) de ceux qui informent le peuple au quotidien, et à témoigner de la solidarité de la corporation envers les orphelins de confrères et consœurs disparus.
Pour marquer cette renaissance, l’UPMB décentralise l’événement dans six villes :
–  Cotonou  : 24 Décembre 2026 à 10h
–  Porto-Novo  : 23 Décembre 2026 à 15h
–  Abomey  : 27 Décembre 2026 à 16h
–  Parakou  : 24 Décembre 2026 à 16h
–  Lokossa  : 23 Décembre 2026 à 15h
–  Natitingou  : 24 Décembre 2026 à 10h
Les sites exacts seront communiqués ultérieurement par les coordinations régionales.
Modalités pratiques
Frais d’inscription : 4 000 FCFA à Cotonou et 3 500 FCFA en régions, pour 3 enfants maximum par professionnel.
Période d’inscription : Du 09 novembre au 14 décembre 2026 à 18h, délai de rigueur.
Le comité d’organisation sous la coupole du président HESSOU invite les consœurs et confrères à une mobilisation massive pour faire de cette 21ème édition, celle de la renaissance et du renouveau.
Contacts : Cotonou : Rosemonde TCHIAKPE (01 97 77 70 16) ,  Toussaint KINNINKPO (01 97 45 75 46) / Secrétariat UPMB (01 40 72 87 71) – Régions : Coordinations UPMB (voir communiqué N°007-11/2026).

items.title: Child protection team in W. Equatoria to free child soldiers

original_payload.original_title: Child protection team in W. Equatoria to free child soldiers
original_payload.original_body:
A four-member delegation from the Child Protection National Technical Committee has arrived in Western Equatoria State to assess police training centers, identify underage recruits, and facilitate the release of children found enlisted in violation of child protection policies.
The delegation is led by Mr. Oluku Andrew, National Coordinator for the Release of Children and Acting Director General for Programmes at the Disarmament, Demobilisation and Reintegration (DDR) Commission.
Other members include Major General William Deng Pok, SSPDF Director for Child Protection; Major General James Dak Karlo, Police Director for the Special Protection Unit; and Lilian Raphael Moga.
Speaking during a meeting with state authorities in Yambio, Oluku said the delegation comprised representatives from government institutions mandated to implement the Government Action Plan on Children Associated with Armed Conflict.
“Our mission is supported by UNICEF and the UN Country Task Force and is part of nationwide efforts to prevent the recruitment and use of children by armed forces and security institutions,” he said. “The purpose of our visit is to assess the police training centers, establish the actual situation, and verify the ages of those undergoing training. We have received reports that more than 50 children have been identified in police training centers across the country, and some have reportedly spent three to four months in training.”
“Any child found to be underage must be identified and released in accordance with child protection policies,” Oluku added.
He said the delegation had already conducted assessments in Western Bahr el Ghazal, Northern Bahr el Ghazal and Warrap states, with Lakes State also scheduled for assessment.
He added that the delegation would meet state security authorities, the state police commissioner, instructors and trainees before compiling a comprehensive report for submission to the Inspector General of Police (IGP) for further action.
Brial James Dak, an official working with the Child Protection National Technical Committee, said the committee was working with the police, the Ministry of Gender and the DDR Commission to identify and remove children from the army and police while preventing further recruitment.
“We are working together with the police, the Ministry of Gender and the DDR Commission to ensure that children are identified and removed from security institutions,” he said. “During our mission to Bor, children serving in the police were identified and their release facilitated. We intend to extend these efforts across all states and the three administrative areas to prevent further recruitment and protect children.”
He stressed that individuals responsible for recruiting children, whether within or outside security institutions, must be held accountable.
Meanwhile, Major General William Deng Pok of the SSPDF Child Protection Unit said his department was working with relevant institutions to address child recruitment, child trafficking, sexual and gender-based violence and other violations affecting vulnerable groups.
Rita Bampoo, Child Protection Officer with the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) in Western Equatoria, commended the state government for its continued support of child protection activities.
“The committee has developed a State Action Plan based on the national action plan, which was presented to the governor and subsequently endorsed,” she said. “However, limited financial resources have been a major challenge affecting the implementation of planned activities.”
For his part, Western Equatoria State Caretaker Governor Badagbu Daniel Rimbasa reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to preventing child recruitment and supporting the release, protection and reintegration of children formerly associated with armed groups.
He said the state government supported efforts to end child recruitment since 2018, when more than 1,040 children were released from armed groups in an event witnessed by the then Vice-President Taban Deng Gai.
“We have absolute political will in Western Equatoria to make sure that we implement the government policy that no child should be associated with armed groups,” Rimbasa said.
He said his administration continued to engage armed groups, including the SPLM-IO, to facilitate the release and reintegration of children.
Highlighting reintegration efforts, Governor Badagbu revealed that 71 released children had graduated after completing vocational skills training last week. He revealed that he awarded university scholarships to four of the graduates, two girls and two boys, to support their pursuit of higher education.
The governor also announced plans to establish two child protection centres in Yambio and Maridi to improve access to services across the state’s ten counties.
