items.title: Mozambique: Mondlane trial interrupted one hour ahead of schedule after defence submits 223-page challenge

original_payload.original_title: Mozambique: Mondlane trial interrupted one hour ahead of schedule after defence submits 223-page challenge
original_payload.original_body:
FILE – For illustration purposes only. [File photo: Facebook/Tribunal Supremo de Moçambique] The first hearing in the trial of Mozambican politician Venâncio Mondlane was interrupted today, an hour earlier than scheduled, after the judge criticised the late submission of a 223-page written challenge by the defence and called for “responsibility on the part of lawyers”.
The hearing took place at the Supreme Court and was nearing its conclusion when the defence announced that it had prepared a written challenge comprising 223 pages, requesting that copies of the document be provided to the other parties to the proceedings the following day.
The request prompted an intervention by presiding judge Luís Mondlane, who questioned the defence about why a document of that length had not been made available earlier.
“The indictment was presented months ago,” the judge observed, questioning why a 223-page challenge was being submitted at that stage and arguing that a document of such length should have been made available to the other parties in the proceedings in good time.
Before the panel of judges, the defence said it intended to distribute copies of the legal challenge to the other parties so that they could familiarise themselves with its contents, but acknowledged that it did not have the copies available at that point.
“There has to be responsibility on the part of lawyers,” the judge added, pointing out that a challenge of that length should have been submitted to the other parties in advance.
In view of the situation, the judge decided to suspend proceedings shortly before 14:30 local time, approximately one hour before the first hearing was originally scheduled to end. Proceedings are due to resume on Wednesday at 10:00.
The interruption followed a hearing marked by several procedural debates, including the reading of the 107 points contained in the 44-page indictment by the Public Prosecutor’s Office, presented by Deputy Attorney-General Amabélia Chuquela, and a subsequent tense exchange during the intervention of the assisting party, represented by the Mozambique Road Network (Revimo).
Mondlane’s defence challenged the reading of the position submitted by the assisting party – the Revimo concessionaire, which claims to have suffered losses due to the destruction of toll plazas and the failure to collect road-use fees during the protests – arguing that the private prosecution had not been submitted within the legally prescribed deadlines and that its contents had not previously been made known to the other parties to the proceedings. Assisting party Revimo, meanwhile, said it supported the Public Prosecutor’s Office indictment, arguing that there were grounds for criminal proceedings to continue in relation to the two terrorism-related offences.
According to the indictment, the politician used various public appearances to call for strikes, work stoppages, demonstrations, marches and other protest actions, which the Public Prosecutor’s Office links to episodes of violence, infrastructure destruction and disruption of public order recorded in the country during the post-election period.
In the reading of the indictment, which began today, the Public Prosecutor’s Office argued that Mondlane sought to create an atmosphere of “fear and instability”, encouraging groups and individuals to commit acts considered “hostile to the rule of law”. The indictment also states that the defendant allegedly arranged for his family to be moved to a safe location and planned his own departure from the country in anticipation of an escalation in the incidents.
According to the prosecution, the allegations against the former presidential candidate are supported by documentary, audiovisual and witness evidence, including videos published between October and December 2024. Mondlane faces charges of public advocacy of crime, incitement to collective disobedience, public instigation to commit a crime, instigation of terrorism and incitement to terrorism.
Source:  Lusa

items.title: Mozambique: Chapo holds separate meetings with Mitrelli and Huatong representatives

original_payload.original_title: Mozambique: Chapo holds separate meetings with Mitrelli and Huatong representatives
original_payload.original_body:
Photo: Presidency of the Republic Mozambique’s President, Daniel Francisco Chapo, held separate meetings on Monday, 16 November, with representatives of the Mitrelli and Huatong groups, who expressed interest in expanding their investments in Mozambique, particularly in strategic sectors for the country’s economic and social development, including infrastructure, energy, industry, agriculture, education and health.
Following the meeting, Mitrelli Group President and Founder Haim Taib said the discussions focused on cooperation between the business group and the Mozambican State, particularly investments under way at the Port of Nacala Terminal in Nampula province.
According to Haim Taib, Mitrelli Group has invested approximately US$40 million in the port infrastructure and expressed its intention to continue investing in the Port of Nacala and expand the group’s presence into other areas of the national economy.
The businessman explained that the expansion plans cover sectors such as education, health and agriculture, as well as initiatives aimed at creating employment opportunities for young people. He added that the identification of areas for intervention should also take into account the priorities established by the Mozambican State.
“We intend to inaugurate this terminal in mid-December and we plan to continue investing, both in the Port of Nacala and in other areas, to develop education and health, create jobs for young people in the country, and invest in agriculture and any other areas that the Mozambican State may decide,” he said.
Haim Taib added that Mitrelli Group has experience implementing projects in several African countries, including Angola, Côte d’Ivoire and Senegal, and expressed its willingness to strengthen cooperation with Mozambique, in coordination with the Government and the private sector.
Mitrelli Group is an international Swiss-based business group founded in 2012 that develops and implements large-scale, sustainable turnkey infrastructure and socio-economic development projects across Africa. It works in partnership with governments, public institutions, investors and private companies in sectors considered strategic to the development of African countries.
Meanwhile, the meeting with representatives of Huatong Group was part of contacts with international investors interested in sectors relevant to the national economy.
The business conglomerate operates in the production of wires, electrical cables and industrial equipment, and also has investments in various fields and an international expansion strategy, particularly on the African continent.
Huatong Group’s activities are concentrated in four main areas: energy and electricity, oil and gas, the aluminium industry and geophysical services. These sectors have potential links with investment opportunities and infrastructure development in Mozambique.
The meetings form part of efforts to promote private investment and identify partnerships with international business groups, with the aim of stimulating strategic sectors, expanding productive capacity and creating opportunities for economic and social development in Mozambique.
Source:  Presidency of the Republic of Mozambique / Press Release

items.title: Mozambique: Mondlane’s defence seeks annulment of indictment over procedural discrepancies

original_payload.original_title: Mozambique: Mondlane’s defence seeks annulment of indictment over procedural discrepancies
original_payload.original_body:
Photo: Facebook/Juvêncio Albino Cumbe The defence team of Mozambican politician Venâncio Mondlane on Tuesday requested the annulment of the indictment in the trial concerning the post-election demonstrations, citing “formal discrepancies” between the document included in the case file and the one delivered to the defendant.
“If you compare the indictment contained in the case file with the one delivered to the defendant, you will find discrepancies in terms of formalities, but not in the content. The indictment delivered to the defendant was in the form of a transcript and did not identify the person who conducted the investigation, nor did it bear the signature of the person who issued the indictment order. Therefore, the requirements for an indictment have been violated,” argued Shamir Mendes, a member of Venâncio Mondlane’s defence team.
The request was submitted by Mondlane’s defence as a preliminary matter in the ongoing trial at the Supreme Court. The lawyers allege procedural discrepancies and argue that the Public Prosecutor’s Office violated legal procedures by retaining the indictment order instead of formally forwarding it to the Maputo City Judicial Court, where the case began before being transferred to the Supreme Court.
According to the defence, the indictment was missing “mandatory requirements” and contained what it described as “serious” discrepancies. It stressed that some elements included in the case file were absent from the indictment order delivered to the defendant, with the prosecution retaining information that should also have been provided alongside the indictment. This prevented the defendant from preparing his defence more effectively and from requesting a preliminary hearing as soon as he received the indictment, as provided for by law, the lawyers added.
“The defendant did not have a real, effective opportunity to propose and request a preliminary hearing when he received the indictment order, because the Public Prosecutor’s Office retained the case file,” the defence argued.
“If it retained the file and did not submit it to the criminal investigating judge [at the Supreme Court], then the defendant’s right to a defence was violated,” it added.
For its part, the prosecution, represented by Deputy Attorney-General Amabélia Chuquela, argued that this matter did not fall within the scope of preliminary issues and that the points raised by the defence were out of time, since they should have been brought within a maximum of three days, as stipulated by law.
“The case file also contains proof of due notification to the defendant and his legal representative, together with a warning that they could request a preliminary hearing. However, no request was submitted, and the proceedings therefore continued,” she argued.
Also among the preliminary matters, the prosecution asked the Supreme Court to prevent Shamir Mendes from joining Mondlane’s defence team, arguing that he did not meet the requirements to do so because he was not a lawyer recognised by the Mozambican Bar Association.
Before the judge, Mondlane said he was comfortable with Shamir Mendes representing him, adding that the lawyer knew the case and had been working with him for months.
“I think the court wants a trial in which the defendant feels comfortable. If that is the case, I express my wish to have Shamir as my defence counsel. I feel comfortable with him; he is the best defence for me,” Mondlane said.
Presiding judge Luís Mondlane granted the request, allowing Mendes to remain on the defence team, arguing that this was in “the interests of the defendant”, who felt comfortable with the defence already in place.
The politician is accused of being the material and moral perpetrator, in concurrence of offences, of public apology for a crime, incitement to collective disobedience, public instigation to commit a crime, instigation to terrorism and incitement to terrorism.
The Mozambican Public Prosecutor’s Office has submitted videos, telephone intercepts and banking information as evidence against Venâncio Mondlane, who has never recognised the official results of the general elections held on 9 October 2024 and whom it holds responsible for plunging Mozambique into “chaos”.

items.title: Mozambique: Media outlets should have adopted legal measures to defend their rights – Mondlane

original_payload.original_title: Mozambique: Media outlets should have adopted legal measures to defend their rights – Mondlane
original_payload.original_body:
Photo: TV Sucesso Moz Venâncio Mondlane, former presidential candidate and leader of the National Alliance for a Free and Autonomous Mozambique (Anamola), believes that media outlets should have adopted legal measures to defend their rights after the country’s Supreme Court has limited the number of media companies authorized to cover his trial, which started this Tuesday.
“It was the national press’s obligation to take concerted action to assert its own rights. The responsibility for the lack of a legal challenge should not be attributed to the court, but to the journalists themselves”, Mondlane said, minutes after arriving at Supreme Court premises in Maputo.
Upon his arrival, Mondlane had a vehicle surrounded by journalists from both domestic and international media outlets, all eager to capture his statements, marking the first day of his trial.
Mondlane added that media outlets should not limit themselves to producing reports and opinion pieces, but should instead “adopt measures with legal standing to defend their rights.”
The Supreme Court spokesperson, Pedro Nhatitima, had announced the availability of only 45 special seats for media companies, adding that “other national media outlets will have to compete for four rotating spots by registering via an electronic platform.” However, Nhatitima did not reveal the criteria for the appointment of companies in question, most of which are state-owned.
Mozambique’s Network of Human Rights Defenders (RMDDH) also condemned restrictions on press coverage of Mondlane’s trial and advocated “for equal access for media outlets.”
“The Supreme Court should review its criteria regarding the allocation of seats, ensuring equal access for the coverage of the trial. It should also provide transparent criteria for the accreditation and selection of journalists, and consider moving the trial to a larger venue to accommodate media coverage. Furthermore, the Court should adopt additional measures to guarantee public access to information about the progress of the trial. Security measures must respect the principles of legality and proportionality”, reads the RMDDH statement.
Mondlane is accused of five criminal charges related to post-election mass demonstrations. The mass demonstration he called to protest against the alleged fraudulent results of the general elections held in October 2024 started peacefully but then degenerated into rioting.
He is accused of having committed the following crimes: public apology for a crime; incitement to collective disobedience; public instigation to crime; instigation and incitement to terrorism.
Source:  AIM

items.title: Mozambique: Almost 40,000 cyber incidents reported in 2025

original_payload.original_title: Mozambique: Almost 40,000 cyber incidents reported in 2025
original_payload.original_body:
FILE – For illustration purposes only. [File photo: AIM] Almost 40,000 cyber incidents have been reported in 2025, mainly involving computer fraud and electronic payment scams, according to Mozambique’s National Institute of Information and Communication Technologies (INTIC).
According Lourino Chemane, INTIC chairperson – speaking at the opening of the second edition of the International Cybersecurity Week, which runs in Maputo from 16 to 20 November, bringing together around 250 participants – the country must shift from a reactive to a preventive approach to Cybersecurity, based on continuous monitoring, early threat detection and coordinated responses, in order to strengthen the protection of critical infrastructure, government systems and citizens’ data.
He also highlighted the country’s progress in the International Telecommunication Union’s Global Cybersecurity Index, in which it moved from level five to level three.
Speaking at the same event, Communications and Digital Transformation Minister, Américo Muchanga, described Cybersecurity as a matter of national sovereignty, state security and the protection of collective interests.
He explained that the country’s score in the Global Cybersecurity Index had risen from 24.8 points in 2020 to 66.1 points in 2024, but warned against complacency in the face of growing threats in cyberspace.
He also highlighted the entry into force of Law 13/2026 on Cybersecurity and Law 14/2026 on Cybercrime, both approved on 1 July, which establish the legal framework for protecting the State in the digital environment and holding those responsible for cybercrime accountable.
The government is also working on updating the National Cybersecurity Policy and Strategy for 2026–2030, focusing on identifying and protecting critical infrastructure, strengthening incident response teams and establishing security operations centres.
Muchanga further stressed the importance of training Cybersecurity specialists, upgrading the skills of information and communication technology professionals and raising public awareness to reduce exposure to digital threats.
The International Cybersecurity Week aims to strengthen cooperation between public and private institutions and formulate practical recommendations to improve the prevention, detection and response to cyber incidents.
Source:  AIM

items.title: Mozambique: Government accused of destroying 510 hectares of farmland in Gaza through “Infrastructured Land Project”

original_payload.original_title: Mozambique: Government accused of destroying 510 hectares of farmland in Gaza through “Infrastructured Land Project”
original_payload.original_body:
Photo: O País Over 500 households accuse the government of destroying 510 hectares of agricultural fields and moving forward with the “Infrastructured Land Project” without consulting the local communities of Ngulelene, in Limpopo district, southern province of Gaza.
The government’s project is linked to the Housing Fund Program.
According to local sources, cited by the independent paper  “O País” , parts of the land are covered by formal Land Use and Exploitation Rights (known as DUATs).
“They invaded and seized the areas where we grow our crops. They are thieves, while they should be protecting us. On 9 September of last month, an excavator arrived. It destroyed the peanuts and other crops I had in my field, without any prior notice regarding this urban development project they intend to build here in our area of Ngulelene”, a source said.
“They didn’t give us any money, or anything else. So, we won’t provide them with the land to work”, the same source added.
Reacting to the population’s position, the Secretary of State for Gaza province, Jaime Neto, acknowledged shortcomings in the dialogue process and guaranteed the suspension of activities, with the aim of finding a resolution to the conflict.
“As government, we cannot impose our will. We are still in discussions, and we have tasked local authorities with continuing the dialogue. We stand to create many jobs there, provide land with infrastructure for young people, and also attract investment. However, it is difficult to convey this message to a community that has become somewhat frustrated with the procedures”, Neto said.
Source:  AIM

items.title: Mozambique: Malnutrition affects about 37% of the population

original_payload.original_title: Mozambique: Malnutrition affects about 37% of the population
original_payload.original_body:
FILE – For illustration purposes only. [File photo: Lusa] About 37% of the Mozambican population faces malnutrition, especially in the northern region of the country, according to the Technical Secretariat for Food and Nutrition Security (SETSAN).
Speaking on Monday during the launch of the week marking the World Fisheries Day, which is celebrated on November 21, Judith Mussácula, SETSAN head, said that malnutrition is more incisive in the northern region of the country.
Citing the latest data from the 2022–2023 Demographic and Health Survey (DHS), Mussácula noted that the findings reveal a particularly concerning situation in the country’s central and northern regions.
While the southern part of the country shows a chronic malnutrition prevalence of approximately 11% below the 20% threshold recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO), several provinces in the central and northern regions record figures exceeding 30%.
“We have the case of Nampula, which is at approximately 47%. Then there are Zambézia, Cabo Delgado, and Niassa. The impacts of malnutrition extend beyond the realm of health and directly affect children’s development”, she said.
“When we talk about 40% or more, it means that for every 100 children, 40 or more may struggle to learn to read and write”, she added.
According to Mussácula, ensuring food and nutrition security requires a multisectoral approach, involving areas such as agriculture, health, education, social protection, disaster management, and statistical planning.
“Discussing food and nutritional security should not be a matter isolated to a single ministry, a single sector, or a single province,” she stated.
Mussácula also expressed concern regarding the low consumption of animal protein in the country, despite its national productive potential. “We consume very little meat and very little fish, even though we possess vast areas for production”, she said.
Source:  AIM

items.title: Julgamento de Venâncio suspenso após defesa apresentar contestação de 223 páginas

original_payload.original_title: Julgamento de Venâncio suspenso após defesa apresentar contestação de 223 páginas
original_payload.original_body:
A primeira sessão do julgamento do político Venâncio Mondlane, que decorreu esta terça-feira no Tribunal Supremo, foi suspensa cerca de uma hora antes da hora prevista para o seu encerramento, na sequência de um desentendimento entre o juiz e a equipa de defesa, devido à apresentação tardia de uma contestação com 223 páginas.
O incidente ocorreu já na fase final da audiência, quando os advogados de Mondlane comunicaram ao colectivo de juízes a existência de uma contestação escrita, solicitando que as respectivas cópias fossem disponibilizadas às restantes partes do processo no dia seguinte.
A iniciativa mereceu a reprovação do juiz conselheiro Luís Mondlane, que questionou a razão pela qual um documento daquela extensão não tinha sido apresentado com maior antecedência, tendo em conta que a acusação do Ministério Público era conhecida há vários meses.
“A acusação foi apresentada há meses”, recordou o magistrado, sublinhando que uma contestação com 223 páginas deveria ter sido entregue atempadamente, de modo a permitir que os restantes intervenientes processuais tivessem oportunidade de analisar o seu conteúdo.
A defesa justificou que pretendia facultar o documento às outras partes, mas reconheceu que não dispunha, naquele momento, das respectivas cópias para distribuição.
Perante a situação, o juiz apelou à responsabilidade dos advogados, considerando que a dimensão da peça processual exigia uma preparação e apresentação prévias.
Na sequência deste episódio, o tribunal decidiu interromper a sessão pouco antes das 14h30, hora local (12h30 em Lisboa), antecipando em cerca de uma hora o fim dos trabalhos. O julgamento deverá prosseguir na quarta-feira, às 10h00.
A sessão inaugural ficou igualmente marcada por vários debates de natureza processual. Entre os momentos mais relevantes esteve a leitura dos 107 pontos da acusação, distribuídos por 44 páginas, apresentada pela procuradora-geral adjunta da República, Amabélia Chuquela.
Registou-se também um momento de tensão durante a intervenção da assistente, representada pela Rede Viária de Moçambique (Revimo), concessionária que reclama prejuízos decorrentes da destruição de portagens e da falta de cobrança de taxas de utilização das vias durante os protestos pós-eleitorais.
A equipa de defesa contestou a intervenção da Revimo, alegando que a acusação particular não foi apresentada dentro dos prazos legalmente estabelecidos e que o respectivo conteúdo não tinha sido previamente comunicado aos restantes intervenientes do processo.
Por seu turno, a representação da concessionária defendeu a sua adesão à acusação do Ministério Público, considerando existirem fundamentos para o prosseguimento da acção penal relativamente aos dois crimes associados ao terrorismo.
De acordo com a acusação do Ministério Público, Venâncio Mondlane terá recorrido a diversas intervenções públicas para mobilizar cidadãos e grupos sociais para greves, paralisações de actividades, manifestações, marchas e outras formas de contestação. Estas acções são associadas pela acusação aos episódios de violência, destruição de infra-estruturas e perturbação da ordem pública verificados no país no período que se seguiu às eleições de 2024.
Na exposição dos factos, o Ministério Público sustentou que o político procurou criar um clima de “medo e instabilidade”, incentivando cidadãos e grupos a praticarem actos considerados hostis ao Estado de Direito.
A acusação refere ainda que Mondlane terá tomado medidas para retirar a família para um lugar seguro e preparado a sua própria saída do território nacional, perante a expectativa de agravamento dos confrontos.
A Procuradoria afirma dispor de elementos de prova documental, audiovisual e testemunhal para sustentar as acusações, incluindo vídeos divulgados entre Outubro e Dezembro de 2024.
O antigo candidato presidencial responde por cinco crimes: apologia pública ao crime, incitamento à desobediência colectiva, instigação pública a um crime, instigação ao terrorismo e incitamento ao terrorismo.

items.title: PR, Exxonmobil e Eni analisam desenvolvimento dos projectos de gás

original_payload.original_title: PR, Exxonmobil e Eni analisam desenvolvimento dos projectos de gás
original_payload.original_body:
O Presidente da República, Daniel Chapo, recebeu, em audiências, no seu Gabinete, representantes da ExxonMobil e da Eni, que apresentaram os avanços da reorganização estratégica entre as duas multinacionais e os planos de desenvolvimento dos projectos   de gás natural na Bacia do Rovuma, com destaque para o aumento da participação da ExxonMobil no Rovuma LNG para 50 por cento e a perspectiva de uma decisão final de investimento até ao final deste ano.
Falando à imprensa, no final do encontro, o Presidente para o Segmento Upstream da ExxonMobil, Dan Ammann, afirmou que a operação, realizada através de uma transacção com a Eni, reforça   o compromisso da empresa com Moçambique e com a implementação do projecto Rovuma LNG.
Segundo Dan Ammann, o empreendimento poderá gerar mais de 100 mil milhões de dólares norte-americanos em valor para Moçambique e criar mais de sete mil postos de trabalho, caso avance conforme as perspectivas anunciadas. A empresa espera
alcançar a decisão final de investimento até ao final de 2026, criando condições para passar à fase de execução.
Por sua vez, o Director de Operações da Eni, Guido Brusco, explicou que a reorganização estratégica estabelece uma participação de 50 por cento da empresa nos projectos Coral Sul, Coral Norte e nas demais iniciativas de gás natural liquefeito flutuante (Floating LNG) da Área 4, permitindo tornar os modelos operacionais mais eficientes e acelerar a produção de recursos.
Relativamente ao Coral Sul, que já se encontra em produção, Guido Brusco indicou que o projecto criou 1.400 postos de trabalho e permitiu adjudicar mais de mil milhões de dólares norte- americanos a empresas moçambicanas, além de mobilizar 19 milhões de dólares para iniciativas de sustentabilidade, com benefícios para aproximadamente 650 mil pessoas.
Quanto ao Coral Norte, o responsável da Eni informou que o projecto apresenta um nível de execução de 70 por cento, estando o início das operações previsto para 2028. Durante a sua vida útil, deverá proporcionar adjudicações superiores a três mil milhões de   dólares a empresas nacionais e mobilizar 60 milhões de dólares para actividades de sustentabilidade, com impacto estimado em um   milhão de pessoas.
Guido Brusco anunciou igualmente que a Eni prevê tomar, no próximo ano, uma decisão de investimento relativa à terceira unidade flutuante de produção de gás natural liquefeito, denominada Mamba Easte. Com a inclusão desta unidade, juntamente com Coral Sul e Coral Norte, a capacidade total de produção deverá atingir três milhões de toneladas por ano.
No domínio da energia, o Director de Operações da Eni revelou que a empresa prevê tomar, no segundo trimestre de 2027, uma decisão de investimento para a construção de uma central eléctrica, cujo início de operações está projectado para 2029.
O dirigente acrescentou que a multinacional já investiu 60 milhões de dólares na transição energética e prevê aplicar mais 200 milhões de dólares em iniciativas de agronegócio, cozinha limpa, reflorestamento e agricultura sustentável, visando beneficiar 100 mil agricultores até 2030 e proporcionar acesso à cozinha limpa a dois milhões de pessoas.
As duas multinacionais manifestaram o interesse em prosseguir a colaboração com Moçambique, tendo Guido Brusco reiterado o propósito de “criar valor durável e uma economia sustentável para benefício do país e dos cidadãos moçambicanos”, enquanto a
ExxonMobil reafirmou o seu compromisso com o avanço do projecto Rovuma LNG e com a próxima fase da sua execução.

items.title: Caçadores furtivos envenenam animais no Parque Nacional do Limpopo e extraem troféus de leão e elefante

original_payload.original_title: Caçadores furtivos envenenam animais no Parque Nacional do Limpopo e extraem troféus de leão e elefante
original_payload.original_body:
Um leão e um elefante foram envenenados por caçadores furtivos no Parque Nacional do Limpopo, na província de Gaza. Depois de desactivarem os sistemas de localização dos dois animais e extraírem os respectivos troféus, os indivíduos alargaram a acção aos abutres, dos quais 32 foram envenenados. A administração do parque alerta para os riscos desta prática, que ameaça também as comunidades circunvizinhas.
A desactivação dos sistemas de localização, o envenenamento de um leão e de um elefante e a extracção dos respectivos troféus marcam a mais recente incursão de caçadores furtivos no Parque Nacional do Limpopo. Uma operação que, segundo o administrador da área de conservação, Abel Nhanbanga, revela o regresso de práticas que se julgavam controladas.
“O que achávamos que já tinha sido controlado, que é o envenenamento de leões, voltou a acontecer. Foi envenenado um leão, macho, jovem, que tinha um colar de localização via satélite, e também um elefante, subadulto, macho, que foi encontrado já com os troféus extraídos”, revelou o administrador.
A acção não se limitou aos animais de grande porte. No interior do parque, cerca de 32 abutres foram igualmente envenenados, ampliando o número de vítimas e a dimensão dos danos provocados pela operação furtiva.
Para Abel Nhantumbo, o uso de veneno representa um perigo que ultrapassa a fauna bravia e pode atingir directamente as comunidades que vivem nas imediações da área de conservação, abrangendo os distritos de Mabalane, Massingir, Mapai e Chicualacuala.
“Esse é um segmento muito perigoso, porque, além de matar os animais selvagens, também cria bastante perigo para as próprias pessoas”, alertou.
O Parque Nacional do Limpopo alberga mais de 20 mil grandes mamíferos, uma população que exige medidas permanentes de protecção. Perante a persistência da caça furtiva, a administração garante estar a reforçar as acções de segurança e vigilância.
O administrador reconhece que a actividade ilegal assume diferentes modalidades, desde a caça para comercialização até à extracção de troféus, e assegura que estão em curso trabalhos para travar estas operações.
“Alguns fazem a caça para a venda comercial e outros fazem-no especificamente para a obtenção de troféus. Estamos, neste momento, a trabalhar para mitigar isso, sem perturbar o andamento das acções e investigações que estão em curso. Não iremos pronunciar-nos muito sobre essa matéria, mas os trabalhos estão em curso e, brevemente, iremos dar mais notícias”, afirmou.
As investigações prosseguem com vista à identificação e responsabilização dos envolvidos. Entretanto, o envenenamento de diferentes espécies coloca sob ameaça não apenas os animais do Parque Nacional do Limpopo, mas também as comunidades que partilham os limites de uma das maiores áreas de conservação do país.

items.title: Dois tiroteios fazem 17 mortos na África do Sul

original_payload.original_title: Dois tiroteios fazem 17 mortos na África do Sul
original_payload.original_body:
Pelo menos 17 pessoas morreram em dois tiroteios registados no mesmo dia, em diferentes pontos da África do Sul. As autoridades policiais ainda não conseguiram apurar as motivações dos ataques, ocorridos em locais separados por cerca de 530 quilómetros, mas garantem que as investigações estão em curso.
Os dois episódios de violência voltaram a expor o problema da criminalidade no país, que continua a registar elevados índices de homicídios.
Segundo informações avançadas pela AfricaNews, no primeiro incidente, nove pessoas foram encontradas mortas, na manhã de segunda-feira, numa comunidade informal nos arredores de Pretória. As vítimas, seis homens e três mulheres, apresentavam ferimentos provocados por armas de fogo e foram encontradas no interior de uma barraca.
O segundo caso ocorreu numa zona semi-rural, a leste da capital sul-africana. Na noite de domingo, a Polícia encontrou um veículo crivado de balas e, no seu interior, oito homens com múltiplos ferimentos de arma de fogo. As vítimas foram declaradas mortas no local.
Os ataques provocaram consternação entre os sul-africanos, que exigem o esclarecimento dos crimes e a responsabilização dos seus autores. Até ao momento, as autoridades não avançaram possíveis motivações para os homicídios.
A África do Sul enfrenta níveis persistentemente elevados de violência armada. Dados da Polícia sul-africana indicam que, em média, cerca de 60 pessoas são assassinadas diariamente no país. Entre os factores associados à criminalidade estão o tráfico de drogas, a mineração ilegal e a disputa por rotas de transporte colectivo.

items.title: President Taye Receives Credentials of 16 Ambassadors

original_payload.original_title: President Taye Receives Credentials of 16 Ambassadors
original_payload.original_body:
Addis Ababa, November 17, 2026 (ENA)— President Taye Atske Selassie has received letters of credence of 16 newly appointed ambassadors to Ethiopia during an official diplomatic ceremony held at the National Palace today.
The ambassadors are from the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, United Arab Emirates, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Ireland, India, Austria, Norway, Finland, Malta, Chad, Republic of Korea, Italy, Barbados, Luxembourg, and Grenada.
Following the formal presentation of credentials, President Taye welcomed the diplomats and wished them success in their missions, reaffirming Ethiopia's commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation and strategic partnerships across various sectors with their respective nations.
Speaking after the ceremony, several ambassadors highlighted their priorities for deepening ties with Ethiopia.
United Arab Emirates Ambassador Abdallah Hassan Ubaid Hassan Al Shamsi expressed delight at his appointment, describing Ethiopia as a strategic partner of UAE with a bright future for bilateral relations.
Similarly, Indian Ambassador Devesh Uttam characterized Ethiopia as a reliable partner and pledged to build upon the two nations' already strong ties across multiple areas of cooperation.
Cyprus's Ambassador, Savvas Vladimirou, the first Ambassador of Cyprus to Ethiopia, noted that investment will be a primary focus of his tenure alongside culture and trade.
Ireland's Ambassador, Ciaran Madden, who noted that the Irish mission in Addis Ababa is Ireland's largest embassy, praised Ethiopia's rapid growth and stated that initiatives to strengthen cultural ties will take place soon.
Ambassador of Czech Republic, Jan Rouček, said he will prioritize the completion of ongoing projects initiated by the Czech government.
Austria's Ambassador Peter Elsner-Mackay pointed to Ethiopia's remarkable growth, stating that he will focus on enhancing economic cooperation and strengthening Austrian-backed projects.
Norwegian Ambassador Yngvild Berggrav, Finnish Ambassador Erik Ingmar Lundberg, and Maltese Ambassador Bernard Hamilton also expressed gratitude for the warm welcome and affirmed their commitment to advancing long-standing bilateral cooperation across various sectors.

items.title: Africans Must Reclaim Cultural Narratives: Nebiyou

original_payload.original_title: Africans Must Reclaim Cultural Narratives: Nebiyou
original_payload.original_body:
Addis Ababa, November 17, 2026-- African scholars and institutions should take greater ownership of the study, interpretation and promotion of the continent’s cultural heritage, Ethiopia’s State Minister for Culture and Tourism, Nebiyou Baye has said.
aIn an interview with the Pulse of Africa, Nebiyou emphasized that Africans must tell their own stories to reshape how the world sees the continent.
He argued that African cultures have long been examined largely through foreign perspectives, some of which have portrayed the continent’s traditions as inferior or backward.
He said African researchers, anthropologists and sociologists should take the lead in documenting and interpreting the continent’s cultural wealth, adding that a stronger understanding of African heritage is essential to promoting it internationally.
“So, primarily, what we have to do is that we have to start studying our culture by ourselves. African anthropologists, African sociologists, African cultural scientists, and African leaders in general, scholars in particular, should be in the front seat in any discussion about African cultural heritages,” Nebiyou said. “So, it’s when we know what we have that we will be able to promote that endowment to the world.”
He also stressed the importance of strengthening cultural exchanges among African countries, arguing that the continent should build greater familiarity with its diverse traditions before seeking wider global recognition.
The official, who is one of the most recognizable figures in Ethiopia’s theatre and cinematic industry, cited Ethiopian cuisine, music, traditional clothing and festivals as cultural assets that could be shared more widely across Africa, encouraging countries to create opportunities for their people to experience one another’s cultural expressions.
Said Nebiyou: “You know, before we go global, in my view, we have to go African. Do you know, for instance, how many Africans were able to taste kitfo? Let alone how many Africans, our neighbors, for instance. Neighbors from Kenya, Sudan, Djibouti. How many of our neighbors were able to taste, let’s just say, injera? So, we need first to reach out to our African brothers and sisters.”
The State Minister further identified music, cinema and other creative industries as powerful instruments of cultural diplomacy and soft power, pointing to the international reach of West African music, Ethiopian jazz and traditional Eskista dance.
He cited musicians such as Mulatu Astatke and filmmaker Haile Gerima as examples of African creative figures who have drawn on local cultural traditions and experiences to produce artistic works that resonate with international audiences.
Among the films he highlighted was Haile Gerima’s Harvest: 3,000 Years, a landmark 1976 Ethiopian film.
A longtime actor and writer himself, Nebiyu previously taught in the School of Theatre Arts at Addis Ababa University as an Assistant Professor. He also served as director of the Ethiopian National Theatre before moving into government.
He said African artists and filmmakers have demonstrated how the continent can communicate its identity and experiences through original creative expression.
“So that now, those African artists, African creative people, they have showed us a way to follow, a method to emulate, and then become world-class artists. And in a way, in doing that, we’ll be able to tell our stories, to promote our culture, to show the world who we are. The world would know that this is Africa,” the Master of Arts holder said.
“The world would know this is Ethiopia. So through the arts and through beautiful minds, through powerful minds, through creative minds, we can promote our culture. We can show the world a different kind of making art.”

items.title: Liberia: Weah Targeted for Arrest? - a Reality or Mere Propaganda

original_payload.original_title: Liberia: Weah Targeted for Arrest? - a Reality or Mere Propaganda
original_payload.original_body:
Is former President George Manneh Weah being monitored and considered for a possible arrest by the Liberian government?
That is the boggling question confronting Liberians, mainly his supporters, as unconfirmed and unproven reports about such plans have been swirling in the past few weeks, leaving many to wonder if truly the former President is on the radar for arrest.
The swelling question is whether the information has any iota of reality or mere political chicanery intended to stir tension and debate.
What is true is that there is no official government statement to the effect, neither has the government rebuffed such reports.

items.title: Owono did not deserve 12-match ban - Pique

original_payload.original_title: Owono did not deserve 12-match ban - Pique
original_payload.original_body:
Owono did not deserve 12-match ban - Pique
Image source,  Getty Images
Image caption,    Jesus Owono said he was experiencing "the most difficult days of my life" after the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel earlier this month
By  Lorraine McKenna   BBC Sport journalist
Published
6 hours ago
FC Andorra owner Gerard Pique says goalkeeper Jesus Owono did not deserve the 12-match suspension he received following his challenge which resulted in the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.
Owono, 25, was sent off after colliding with De Miguel late on in the second-tier match between Andorra and Tenerife on 2 November.
De Miguel died the following day, aged 30, and a disciplinary committee from the Spanish football federation confirmed Owono's ban last week.
In a video posted on social media, Pique said players past and present, plus coaches and other goalkeepers, felt the incident was "an accident".
The former Spain and Barcelona defender added: "I truly believe that imposing the maximum sanction on Jesus for this action puts him in a situation he does not deserve, because he is not to blame for all of this having happened."
Tenerife striker De Miguel dies after on-field collision
Published
3 November
Goalkeeper involved in fatal collision gets 12-game ban
Published
3 days ago
The 12-match suspension was the maximum punishment Owono, 25, could have received, as the disciplinary committee could only consider the offence on the pitch and not "the tragic outcome of the incident".
Following the decision, Tenerife manager Alvaro Cervera said he accepted the regulations do not specifically account for what happened, but acknowledged the ban "might feel light".
Pique also highlighted a recent on-field incident in Spain, when Albacete winger Jose Corpas accidentally kicked Sabadell midfielder Quadri Liameed in the head during a Spanish second division match.
Nigerian Liameed was knocked unconscious but was later discharged from hospital following medical checks, while Spaniard Corpas was shown a straight red card and handed a three-match ban.
"Fortunately Quadri is fine, the consequences in this case were not fatal, and the committee decided to sanction Corpas with three matches," Pique said.
"With all this, my reflection is: what is being sanctioned, the action or the consequences?"
Owono has withdrawn from Equatorial Guinea's squad for Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Zimbabwe this month, and Pique said it was unlikely he would return to action as soon as his suspension is served.
He added: "Jesus is going to need far more than 12 matches before he is available and able to compete.
"No sanction is going to bring [De Miguel] back to us."

items.title: Niger : 350 artisans de trois régions à l’école de l’utilisation du numérique dans leurs métiers

original_payload.original_title: Niger : 350 artisans de trois régions à l’école de l’utilisation du numérique dans leurs métiers
original_payload.original_body:
Niamey, 17 nov (ANP)- La Ministre de Tourisme et de l’Artisanat, Mme Guichene Kari Aghaichata a présidé, ce mardi 17 novembre 2026 à Niamey, la cérémonie officielle du lancement de la formation de 350 artisans des régions de Niamey, Dosso et Tillaberi, aux métiers du numérique, suivie de la pose de la première pierre de construction d’une salle informatique au village artisanal de Wadata, avec l’appui financier du Programme des Nations Unies pour le Développement PNUD.
Cette formation de 72h, « qui marque une nouvelle étape dans la dynamique de modernisation de l’artisanat et du tourisme au Niger, est une ambition nationale, celle de faire de nos secteurs de l’artisanat et du tourisme des leviers plus performants de création de richesses, d’emplois, de valorisation de nos ressources locales et de souveraineté économique » a souligné la ministre en charge de l’artisanat en prenant la parole à cette cérémonie.
La vision portée par les plus hautes autorités de notre pays, sous le leadership du Général d’Armée Abdourahamane Tiani, Président de la République et sous la conduite du Premier Ministre Ali Mahamane Lamine Zeine, Premier Ministre,  « accorde une place essentielle à la valorisation des potentialités nationales, au développement du capital humain et à la promotion d’une économie endogène, résiliente et souveraine » a-t-elle fait savoir.
Cependant, a-t-elle déploré, « l’artisanat nigérien malgré son potentiel considérable, demeure confronté à plusieurs contraintes structurelles, notamment la faible structuration des unités artisanales, les difficultés d’accès aux marchés, l’insuffisance de certains équipements et surtout la maîtrise encore limitée des outils numériques ».
Par conséquent, « à l’heure où les technologies de l’information et de la communication transforment profondément les modes de production, de commercialisation et de consommation, nos artisans ne peuvent rester en marge de cette évolution car aujourd’hui, un produit de qualité ne suffit plus toujours à garantir le succès commercial, il faut également savoir le présenter, le promouvoir, le rendre visible et le commercialiser au-delà de son environnement géographique immédiat ».
A ce niveau, « le numérique devient un puissant instrument de développement » a préconisé la ministre Aghaichata, selon qui grâce aux outils numériques, « un artisan installé à Niamey, Dosso ou Tillabéri pourra désormais présenter ses créations à une clientèle située à l’intérieur comme à l’extérieur de nos frontières, développer son réseau commercial, accéder à de nouvelles opportunités et mieux valoriser son savoir-faire ».
C’est pourquoi, a-t-elle poursuivi, «mon Département ministériel, en concertation avec le Programme des Nations Unies pour le Développement, a élaboré un programme ambitieux de renforcement des capacités numériques au bénéfice de 900 artisans et professionnels du tourisme issus des huit régions du Niger et la  session qui nous réunit aujourd’hui  et qui concerne 350 artisans de ces trois régions, constitue la première phase opérationnelle de ce programme ».
À travers cette initiative, a-t-elle indiqué, « nous voulons notamment renforcer les compétences pratiques de nos artisans en matière de marketing digital, de promotion en ligne, de commerce électronique et d’utilisation des solutions numériques adaptées à leurs activités  et notre ambition permettra à chaque artisan nigérien de faire connaître son savoir-faire, de valoriser ses produits et de conquérir de nouveaux marchés ».
Outre le lancement de cette formation, la ministre en charge de l’artisanat qu’accompagnent le gouverneur de la région de Niamey et le représentant du PNUD au Niger, a donné le coup d’envoi de la pose de la première pierre de construction d’une salle informatique au village artisanal de Wadata.
Cette infrastructure, a-t-elle précisé, « représente bien plus qu’un simple ouvrage matériel, elle symbolise notre volonté de doter durablement le secteur de l’artisanat d’un cadre approprié pour l’apprentissage, la formation continue, l’innovation et l’appropriation des technologies numériques ».
En posant la première pierre de cette infrastructure informatique, s’est t-elle réjouie,  « nous posons les fondations d’un artisanat nigérien plus moderne, mieux structuré, plus compétitif et davantage ouvert sur le monde », rappelant ainsi que «le numérique ne doit nullement être perçu comme une menace pour nos traditions et nos valeurs culturelles, il constitue une opportunité exceptionnelle de les préserver, de les promouvoir et de leur donner une visibilité à l’échelle nationale et internationale ».
Se prononçant également à cette occasion, le représentant résident du PNUD au Niger, M. Mamadou N’Daw a salué le leadership de la Ministre, « qui a fait de la modernisation de l’artisanat une priorité, ainsi que l’engagement de la Direction Générale de l’Artisanat », précisant que l’artisanat n’est pas seulement un secteur économique, c’est un patrimoine culturel, un facteur de cohésion sociale, un moteur d’emploi, et une vitrine de l’identité du Niger ».
Partenaire de cette initiative, le PNUD, a-t-il fait savoir, « est fier d’accompagner cette vision du  Ministère qui associe une plateforme nationale de vente en ligne, la formation pratique de 900 artisans et professionnels du tourisme, dont 300 ici à Niamey, un accompagnement de trois mois jusqu’aux premières ventes, et la remise d’ordinateurs par le PNUD ».
Le gouverneur de la région de Niamey, le  Général de Division Assoumane Abdou Harouna, pour sa part,  a transmis aux participants, « avec responsabilité, les fraternelles salutations, les encouragements et l’assurance de l’accompagnement des Plus Hautes Autorités de notre pays sous les Hautes Directives Eclairées de Son Excellence le Général d’Armée Abdourahamane Tiani, Président de la République, Chef d’État ».
Au regard du thème, a-t-il indiqué,  « il s’agit d’un processus dont les avantages essentiels consistent à améliorer les méthodes traditionnelles par des actions numériques qu’offrent la technologie, la digitalisation en vue, de transformer des activités ou produits visant leur amélioration en terme de qualité, d’efficacité et d’accessibilité ».
A cet effet, « la digitalisation offre aux utilisateurs, une gamme de choix dont la plus en vue est la plateforme en ligne avec, des avantages aussi multiples que variés » a laissé entendre le gouverneur de la région de Niamey selon qui, « cet espace numérique exige tout naturellement, le respect des principes de la concurrence dans tous ses contours ».

items.title: Tillabéri : Lancement d’un tournoi de handball sous le signe de la paix et de la cohésion sociale

original_payload.original_title: Tillabéri : Lancement d’un tournoi de handball sous le signe de la paix et de la cohésion sociale
original_payload.original_body:
Tillabéri, 17 Nov (ANP) – Un tournoi de handball dénommé « Coupe du président du Conseil communal de la jeunesse de Tillabéri » a été officiellement lancé le lundi 16 novembre 2026 au stade régional de Tillabéri, sous le thème : « Le sport, un levier de la paix et de la cohésion sociale ».
Considéré comme un puissant instrument de rassemblement et de promotion de la paix, le sport constitue un vecteur d’unité entre les jeunes et contribue au renforcement du vivre-ensemble au sein des communautés. C’est dans cette dynamique que la Ligue régionale de handball de Tillabéri, sous le parrainage du président du Conseil communal de la jeunesse, M. Abdoul Aziz Maliki, a initié cette compétition afin de faire du sport un véritable moyen de rapprochement et de cohésion sociale.
Cette compétition regroupe 5 équipes de la ville de Tillabéri, réunies autour d’une même passion. Elle se déroule du 16 au 19 novembre 2026 dans un esprit de solidarité, de discipline et de fair-play. Elle vise notamment à promouvoir les talents locaux et à donner davantage de visibilité à la pratique du handball dans la région.
La cérémonie d’ouverture s’est déroulée en présence du Secrétaire Général de la commune urbaine de Tillabéri, M. Salou Issa, du directeur régional de la Jeunesse, des Sports et de la Culture, du chef du village de Tillabéri ainsi que de plusieurs autres personnalités.
Dans son allocution de lancement, le président du Conseil communal de la jeunesse de Tillabéri, M. Abdoul Aziz Maliki, a souligné la pertinence du thème retenu, au regard du contexte sécuritaire que connaît la région. Il a rappelé que l’insécurité a progressivement dressé des barrières entre les communautés et fragilisé les liens sociaux.
Selon lui, le sport représente un cadre privilégié de retrouvailles, de rapprochement et de promotion du vivre-ensemble. Il a ainsi salué le choix de cette thématique par la Ligue régionale de handball, tout en exprimant l’espoir que cette compétition permettra aux jeunes de devenir davantage des acteurs engagés dans la promotion de la paix, de la cohésion sociale et du vivre-ensemble.
Avant de terminer son intervention, M. Abdoul Aziz Maliki a vivement salué la présence des autorités communales et coutumières, dont le soutien témoigne de l’intérêt accordé aux initiatives en faveur du sport et de l’épanouissement de la jeunesse.
Auparavant, le secrétaire général de la commune urbaine de Tillabéri, représentant l’administrateur délégué, ainsi que le chef du village de Tillabéri ont pris la parole pour féliciter et remercier la Ligue régionale de handball et le Conseil communal de la jeunesse pour leur engagement en faveur de la promotion du sport. Ils ont également exhorté les différentes équipes participantes à faire preuve de discipline, de courage et de responsabilité tout au long de la compétition.
Deux rencontres étaient au programme de cette première journée du tournoi. La première affiche, dans la catégorie masculine, a opposé l’AS Dogoney à l’AS Le Mafé dans une ambiance conviviale et empreinte de fair-play. Au coup de sifflet final, l’AS Dogoney s’est largement imposée en dominant son adversaire sur le score de 16 buts à 6.
La deuxième rencontre a mis aux prises deux équipes féminines, à savoir l’AS Stade, vêtue de jaune, et l’AS AMA, habillée en vert. Au terme d’un match très disputé, c’est l’AS Stade qui a remporté la victoire sur le fil, avec un score serré de 4 buts à 3.
Au-delà de la compétition sportive, cette Coupe entend ainsi faire du handball un cadre d’expression de la solidarité, de l’unité et de la fraternité entre les jeunes de Tillabéri.
MAM/KPM/ANP-150 Novembre 2026

items.title: Les fonctionnaires de l’Information et les journalistes nigériens visitent plusieurs entreprises à Changsha dans la province de Hunan

original_payload.original_title: Les fonctionnaires de l’Information et les journalistes nigériens visitent plusieurs entreprises à Changsha dans la province de Hunan
original_payload.original_body:
Changsha, 17 Nov (ANP)-Dans le cadre du séminaire des fonctionnaires de l’Information et les journalistes nigériens, ces professionnels des medias nigériens, ont effectué, ce mardi 17 novembre 2026, une visite au niveau du Group BROAD et au parc industriel des camions intelligents de SANY.
Cette première étape de la visite a conduit les fonctionnaires et les journalistes nigériens au niveau du Group Broad qui est grande entreprise privée chinoise basée à Changsha, dans la province de Hunan. Fondée en 1988. Le groupe est mondialement reconnu comme un pionnier des technologies écologiques, de la climatisation non électrique et de la construction modulaire Ultra-rapide.
La délégation nigérienne conduite par le conseiller du Président de la République, M. Abdoulaye Tiemogo, a reçu d’amples explications au niveau de chaque endroit où se trouvent les machines de cette entreprise.
Parmi les machines nous avons, des machines pour filtrer l’air, des machines pour échanger l’air chaud et froid, le modèle de refroidissement, le modèle de renouveler les méthodes de chauffages, et un modèle pour la gestion de l’énergie etc…
Le groupe Broad exporte ses solutions dans plus de 80 pays à travers le monde, il est le leader mondial des refroidisseurs à absorption fonctionnant au gaz naturel ou grâce à la chaleur résiduelle industrielle, sans utiliser des compresseurs électriques ni de fluides frigorigènes nocifs.
L’entreprise fabrique des purificateurs d’air et des systèmes de ventilation capables de filtrer 99,9% des particules fines, note-t-on.
Le parc industriel des camions intelligents de ‘’SANY’’ avec une production annuelle de 300 000 unités, est une usine qui produit plusieurs types de véhicules, notamment des tracteurs électriques, des camions légers électriques, des tracteurs à hydrogènes, des tracteurs diesels, des camions malaxeurs et des camions bennes, mais aussi des grues.
D’une superficie de 1 000 000 mètres carré, ce parc est la plus grande base de production de camions lourds électriques au monde.
Quant à l’usine d’une superficie de 220 000 mètre carré, elle est la plus grande usine entière combinée de camions lourds en Chine.
En 2025, la flotte opérationnelle de camions lourds électriques de ‘’SANY’’ atteint près de 50 000 unités, avec un chiffre d’affaires en hausse de 125% par rapport à l’année precédente. Le groupe confirme ainsi son leadership mondial dans le secteur des poids lourds à énergie nouvelle et atteste du succès de sa stratégie bas carbone.
Organisé par le Ministère du commerce de la République populaire de chine, ce séminaire, rappelle-t-on, vise à renforcer l’amitié traditionnelle entre la chine et les pays e développement et à promouvoir leur coopération dans le domaine, mais aussi à contribuer au développement des ressources humaines, de l’économie et de la société des pays en développement.
AAM/SML/ANP/Novembre 2026

items.title: Changsha : Immersion au centre d’innovation des semences du Mont Yuelu, le laboratoire des graines de demain

original_payload.original_title: Changsha : Immersion au centre d’innovation des semences du Mont Yuelu, le laboratoire des graines de demain
original_payload.original_body:
Par Abdoulaye Issa Ounteini, envoyé spécial de l’ANP à Changsha(Chine)
Changsha, 17 nov(ANP)-La délégation de journalistes nigériens qui séjourne en chine a visité dans la matinée de ce mardi 17 novembre 2026, le centre d’innovation semencière du Mont Yuelu, une avancée technologique du secteur semencier dans la province de Hunan.
A son arrivée, la délégation nigérienne a été accueillie par M. Liu Zhixian, directeur général adjoint exécutif du Centre, qui a dans une vidéo présenté brièvement le centre. La délégation a eu droit par la suite à une visite guidée au sein du centre, passant des panneaux qui retracent l’histoire du centre, aux résultats des recherches sur le riz hybride, les poissons, le thé, le porc.
Le Hunan bénéficie d’un riche patrimoine dans le secteur semencier, de solides plateformes d’innovations et de fructueuses réussites en recherche scientifique. Il se classe premier au niveau mondial pour la sélection de riz hybride, de poivron hybride et poisson d’eau douce et est un chef de file national dans la sélection de colza et de camélia.
Le Centre d’innovation de l’industrie semencière de Yuelushan est une initiative majeure du Comité du Parti et du gouvernement provincial du Hunan, visant à mettre en œuvre les directives importantes du secrétaire général Xi Jinping concernant la revitalisation du secteur semencier et à s’aligner sur le plan directeur des « trois sommets et quatre nouveautés ».
Cet institut de recherche et développement d’un nouveau genre a été créé conjointement par le gouvernement provincial et le groupe CITIC, s’appuyant sur les deux technologies clés de Huazhi Biotechnology : la sélection moléculaire et le traitement intelligent des données massives.
Il réunit des institutions de recherche, industrielles et académiques de premier plan à l’échelle nationale. Il fait office de centre de valorisation et d’application industrielle des résultats du laboratoire de Yuelushan et de centre d’innovation technologique pour l’industrie semencière biologique de la province du Hunan.
Il ambitionne de devenir un pôle d’innovation collaborative national pour les technologies semencières, un centre national de promotion de la valorisation des acquis scientifiques et technologiques du secteur, et un centre international d’échange et de services technologiques pour l’industrie semencière, contribuant ainsi à l’autonomie et au renforcement du secteur semencier national.
Le Hunan est une importante base de production de produits agricoles de haute qualité en Chine, se classant première en termes de superficie cultivée en riz et de rendement. Elle produit également des légumes et d’autres produits agricoles. La production de tortues à carapace molle, de thé, d’agrumes et de plantes médicinales chinoises figure parmi les meilleures du pays.
Guidée par l’Initiative pour le développement mondial, la Chine renforce sa coopération avec les Nations Unies et la coopération Sud-Sud dans le cadre de l’initiative « la Ceinture et la Route ». Elle collabore avec la communauté internationale pour faire face à la crise alimentaire mondiale et a publié, avec les pays concernés, une Vision et des Actions pour la promotion conjointe de la coopération agricole dans le cadre de cette initiative, participant ainsi à la gouvernance mondiale de l’alimentation et de l’agriculture.
C’est dans cette perspective de coopération que la délégation nigérienne a visité le centre. Les échanges ont porté sur le partage d’expériences notamment dans la production du Riz hybride surtout pour le Niger qui a entamé sa marche vers la souveraineté alimentaire.
AIO/AS/ANP 0149 novembre 2026

items.title: Le Chef de l’État procède à de nouvelles nominations au sein de l’administration publique…

original_payload.original_title: Le Chef de l’État procède à de nouvelles nominations au sein de l’administration publique…
original_payload.original_body:
Le Président de la République, Chef de l’État, Son Excellence le Général d’Armée Abdourahamane Tiani, a signé plusieurs décrets portant mesures individuelles, selon un communiqué publié le 16 novembre 2026, par le Secrétariat Général du Gouvernement.
Ces nominations concernent plusieurs ministères et institutions stratégiques, notamment la Défense nationale, l’Intérieur, la Santé, les Transports, l’Équipement, les Mines, l’Environnement, les Affaires étrangères, l’Énergie, la Fonction publique, la Culture, le Commerce et l’Industrie.
Ainsi au titre du ministère de la Défense nationale, le Général de Brigade Mamane Souley a été nommé Secrétaire Général, tandis que le Colonel-major Noma Dari devient Secrétaire Général Adjoint.
Au titre du ministère de l’Intérieur, de la Sécurité publique et de l’Administration du territoire, M. Ayouba Abdou Rahamane est désigné Secrétaire Général. M. Aboubacar Issaka Oumarou prend les fonctions de Directeur Général de la Police Nationale, avec M. Abdoulaye Mamam comme Directeur Général Adjoint.
Dans le secteur de la santé, plusieurs responsables ont été nommés afin de renforcer la gouvernance du système sanitaire. M. Tinga Abdoulaye Karim est nommé Directeur Général de l’Hôpital National de Zinder. Madame Ibrahim Halimatou Alio Abdou devient Directrice des infrastructures et équipements sanitaires, tandis que M. Abou Yahaya est désigné Directeur de la santé communautaire. D’autres nominations concernent la statistique sanitaire, la santé de la mère, de l’enfant, des adolescents et des jeunes, ainsi que l’inspection des services.
Le ministère des Transports et de l’Aviation civile enregistre également plusieurs nouvelles désignations. M. Dicko Arzika Mahaman Laminou est nommé Directeur Général de la circulation et des transports routiers. Madame Ibrahim Boubé Ramatou prend la direction générale des transports ferroviaires, maritimes et fluviaux.
Les nominations touchent aussi la formation aux techniques du transport routier, de la logistique, des transports multimodaux, la mobilité urbaine, les archives et les relations publiques.
Au titre du ministère de l’Équipement et des Infrastructures, M. Saidou Ghoumar est nommé Secrétaire Général. Il sera épaulé par de nouveaux responsables chargés de la gestion et du suivi des réseaux, de la planification et de l’entretien routier, ainsi que de l’inspection générale des services.
Au titre du ministère des Mines, M. Alfari Salou est désigné Inspecteur Général des services.
Dans le domaine de l’environnement, de l’hydraulique et de l’assainissement, le Colonel Zoumari Salifou est nommé Directeur Général de l’Agence Nigérienne des Parcs et Réserves (ANPR).
Cette nomination intervient dans un contexte où la protection des aires protégées, la gestion des ressources naturelles et la préservation de la biodiversité demeurent des priorités nationales.
Le ministère des Affaires étrangères, de la Coopération et des Nigériens à l’extérieur voit également son appareil institutionnel renforcé. M. Zakariou Adam Maiga est nommé Président du Conseil d’administration de l’Institut National des Études Diplomatiques et Stratégiques (INEDS), tandis que M. Tcheko Amadou devient Directeur Général de cette institution.
Plusieurs autres nominations ont été faites dans les secteurs de l’enseignement supérieur, de l’énergie, de la fonction publique, de la jeunesse, des sports et de la culture, de l’urbanisme, de la communication, ainsi que du commerce et de l’industrie.
Elles concernent notamment des postes de secrétaires généraux, directeurs généraux, directeurs, inspecteurs, conseillers techniques et présidents de conseils d’administration.
Au ministère de la Jeunesse, des Sports et de la Culture, M. Moussa Harou est nommé Directeur Général de la Culture et des Arts. Madame Arzika Mahamadou Rabiatou devient Présidente du Conseil d’administration du Bureau Nigérien du Droit d’Auteur (BNDA).
Le Centre Culturel Nigérien Moustapha Alassane sera désormais présidé par M. Hamani Himou Kassoum, connu sous le nom de JHONEL, artiste slameur.
Au ministère du Commerce et de l’Industrie, les nominations visent notamment le renforcement de la normalisation, de la métrologie, de la certification, de la promotion des investissements, de la compétitivité des entreprises, de la concurrence et de la protection des droits des consommateurs. M. Abdou-Kader Zakari Oumarou est nommé Directeur Général de l’Agence Nigérienne de Normalisation, de Métrologie et de Certification.
Ces décisions traduisent la volonté des autorités de renouveler et de renforcer les cadres de gestion au sein de l’administration publique. Elles interviennent dans plusieurs secteurs considérés comme essentiels pour la sécurité, le développement des infrastructures, l’accès aux services sociaux, la mobilité, l’environnement, l’innovation et la promotion économique du pays.
