items.title: Sa Majesté Oumarou Ibrahim Oumarou : un Sultan empreint de sagesse et d’hospitalité !

original_payload.original_title: Sa Majesté Oumarou Ibrahim Oumarou : un Sultan empreint de sagesse et d’hospitalité !
original_payload.original_body:
Au Niger, les Chefs traditionnels sont bien plus que des dirigeants : ce sont les gardiens bienveillants de notre histoire, de nos valeurs et de notre vivre-ensemble. Ils jouent un rôle essentiel au quotidien au cœur de nos communautés. Loin d’être en marge de la modernité, leur statut et leur intégration au sein de l’organisation administrative de l’État sont rigoureusement ancrés dans la loi n° 2015-01 du 13 janvier 2015 et ses textes d’application.
Véritables pont entre l’administration et les citoyens, les Chefs traditionnels incarnent l’autorité de proximité. Ils bénéficient d’une écoute profonde et d’un respect presque sacré de la part de leurs administrés. Cette légitimité, profondément humaine, crée un lien unique. Leurs populations font leur force, et en retour, ils se dressent comme boucliers protecteurs. Dépositaires de nos valeurs ancestrales, ils demeures les piliers incontestables de la gestion du territoire, guidés par une connaissance intime et bienveillante de leur communauté.
En poursuivant notre cheminement, nous sommes ravis de vous ouvrir aujourd’hui les coulisses de notre réflexion sur le portrait du Sultan de l’Aïr. Au 15ème siècle, l’Aïr faisait face à une anarchie intérieure et des menaces extérieures qui incitèrent les communautés Touarègues à chercher une solution durable au problème d’unité et d’identité.
Compte tenu du comportement des Confédérations qui n’acceptent pas la suprématie de l’une d’elles sur les autres, la solution trouvée est de chercher un Chef à l’étranger. Cependant, il doit descendre d’une monarchie qui est reconnue respectée par de nombreux peuples dans le monde. C’est ainsi que les Confédérations Sandals composées des Itéseyens, Inoussoufa, Ilissawen, Kel Ewey, Kel Gress et Kel Fadey, décidèrent de se rendre à Istamboul pour chercher un Sultan.
Le Prince Younous, fils du Sultan Ottoman fut désigné et intronisé Sultan de l’Aïr ou Sultan d’Agadez en 1405.
Après une période de nomadisme, les Sultans qui se succèdent s’installèrent à Assodé, Tadliza et définitivement à Tin Chaman, l’actuel Palais royal d’Agadez.
La contrée d’Agadez est une région désertique dont l’économie repose principalement sur l’élevage, le maraichage, le commerce, aujourd’hui sur l’uranium, l’or, le pétrole et le tourisme. Le nom « Agadez », trouverait son origine dans le mot Tamasheq « Tagades », qui signifie « visite », illustrant dès l’origine la vocation d’accueil. Au cœur du Ténéré nigérien, la ville d’Agadez, surnommée « porte du désert », fut un carrefour caravanier exceptionnel et un centre d’échanges culturels transsahariens majeur.
Aujourd’hui encore, cette tradition d’échanges demeure portée par la pérennité du Sultanat. À sa tête, Son Altesse Oumarou Ibrahim Oumarou. Ce Souverain, empreint d’humilité et de dignité, dirige par l’exemple en plaçant le respect d’autrui au centre de sa gouvernance. Ce Sultan est un Haut Dirigeant toujours à l’écoute, dont la discrétion et le silence témoignent d’une grande capacité d’observation, ainsi que d’une aptitude profonde à faire preuve d’empathie envers sa communauté.
Devenu une figure morale incontournable sur la scène nationale et régionale, le Sultan de l’Aïr incarne bien plus qu’une simple autorité coutumière. Il est reconnu pour son engagement en faveur du dialogue social, de la culture, de l’art, de la promotion de la jeunesse et d’une société plus inclusive.
À l’origine, un Sultan d’Agadez jouait un rôle de Médiateur et d’arbitre entre les différentes Confédérations touarègues, telles que les Kel Ewey ou les Kel Gress. La force du Sultanat a favorisé le rassemblement de ses tribus dans le respect des anciens campements, installant une ossature urbaine atypique, entièrement construite en briques de terre séchées au soleil. Dans la ville d’Agadez, le visiteur y reçoit toujours un accueil chaleureux, que ce soit pour s’y promener ou pour y découvrir des activités artisanales, dont la plus célèbre reste la fabrication de bijoux en argent et en cuir, réputés bien au-delà des frontières nigériennes.
Son Altesse Oumarou Ibrahim Oumarou a accédé au trône par consensus, le 25 mai 2012, succédant à son père, le Sultan Ibrahim Oumarou dit Tsofo, décédé, le 21 février 2012 à l’âge de 80 ans après 52 ans de règne. Devenu ainsi le 52ème Sultan d’Agadez, ce Souverain d’une grande générosité a été officiellement intronisé, le 15 décembre 2016 au cours d’une cérémonie grandiose au stade municipal de la ville. Il est profondément respecté pour sa sagesse, sa bienveillance, sa clémence et son refus de l’arbitraire.
Malgré son tempérament très pacifique, sa réserve naturelle et son silence solennel, il n’en demeure pas moins proche de son peuple. Sa nature réservée met en avant un goût prononcé pour la religion et la lecture du Saint Coran. Symbole d’unité, il œuvre constamment à l’apaisement des tensions et à garantir une justice équitable, permettant à chaque habitant du Sultanat de faire appel directement à lui. Sa vision repose sur une conviction intime : la paix et la prospérité matérielle ne suffisent pas au bonheur des populations s’il n’y a pas d’amour et de considération mutuelle. Pour le Sultan Oumarou, savoir aimer et se savoir aimé permet au plus pauvre d’oublier sa misère et au malade sa souffrance.
Héritier d’une longue dynastie qui a suscité toutes les convoitises à travers les siècles, il jouit de véritables pouvoirs moraux et intervient régulièrement pour appeler au dialogue communautaire, à la sécurité et au renforcement du vivre-ensemble. Selon la tradition, un Sultan de l’Aïr descendrait symboliquement du Sultan de Constantinople, une ascendance mythique qui lui confère une autorité arbitrale au-dessus des rivalités de clans. Son art de gouverner repose sur la recherche permanente du consensus : au sein de son palais royal, on discute et l’on concède jusqu’à ce que chaque partie soit convaincue, refusant qu’une simple loi de la majorité n’étouffe la voix des minorités.
Le Sultan de l’Aïr reste le garant des liens de sang et de l’histoire du Sultanat en passant par le Damergou et l’Ader. Les attaches unissant les localités d’Agadez, Illéla, Dogaraoua, Tamaské et les descendants du Sultan Makitan à Tanout et Gangara reposent sur une histoire dynastique et des réseaux de parenté issus de la grande Confédération touarègne et de la noblesse de l’Aïr. Les Makitanawa sont les descendants de Makitan, qui a occupé le trône d’Agadez de 1906 à 1908 avant d’être destitué par les colons. Le Sultan Makitan était le grand frère d’Ibrahim Dassouki, ancien Chef de Canton de Doguéraoua. De cette lignée est né Attawel Ibrahim, également ancien Chef de Canton de Doguéraoua.
Ces liens de sang s’articulent autour de deux grands axes historiques : la lignée des Istanboulawas (l’Aïr et l’Ader). Les Souverains d’Agadez, d’Illéla, de Dogaraoua et de Tamaské partagent une consanguinité directe ancrée dans l’histoire du Sultanat de l’Aïr. Leurs familles régnantes proviennent de la même souche aristocratique, qualifiée d’Istanboulawas, les descendants du premier Sultan de l’Aïr, Yunus, rattachées aux vagues successives de Princes de l’Aïr.
À Illéla (siège du Sultan Mohamed Agaba, portant le titre de Sarki Ader avec une ramification à Doundayé au Nigeria. Le titre est attribué au Chef de Canton d’Illéla, Elhadji Yacouba Habibou, élu Chef après le décès du Chef de Canton Elhadji Kadi Oumani qui a succédé à son père, le Chef de Canton Elhadji Oumani Attou), à Dogaraoua, siège de la Chefferie, Sarkin Abzin comme à Tamaské, siège de la Chefferie des Tamaskaoua. Ces titres témoignent directement de leur filiation avec la maison royale d’Agadez.
S’agissant de la branche des Makitanawa du Damergou, établis à Tanout et à Gangara, dans la région historique du Damergou, les descendants du Sultan Makitan forment une autre ramification de ces grands ensembles Touaregs (issus historiquement des Kel Owey ou des Kel Gress).
Au gré des migrations et du partage des zones d’influence entre le nord (Aïr / Agadez) et le Sud-Est (Zinder / Damergou), des princes et des guerriers nobles sont descendus sécuriser et contrôler les routes caravanières. À travers des alliances matrimoniales stratégiques avec les élites de l’Aïr et de l’Ader, ils s’y sont solidement ancrés. Aujourd’hui encore, des Chefs coutumiers et de grandes familles de Tanout et de Gangara entretiennent des liens de cousinage et de lignage très étroits avec Agadez, Illéla, Doguéraoua et Tamaské.
En somme, il s’agit d’une seule et même famille d’origine saharienne (les Abzinawa) qui s’est déployée au fil des siècles. Une branche est demeurée au cœur du Sultanat de l’Aïr (Agadez), une autre a établi les Chefferies de l’Ader (Illéla, Dogaraoua, Tamaské), et la dernière s’est installée dans le Damergou (Tanout, Gangara) sous l’étendard des descendants du Sultan Makitan. Les Makitanawa descendent du sultan Makitan, qui a régné de 1906 à 1908 avant d’être destitué par l’administration coloniale. Ce dernier était le frère aîné d’Ibrahim Dassouki, Chef de canton de Doguéraoua, lequel donna sa sœur Tamorika en mariage à Jackou, Chef de Canton de Kornaka. C’est de cette alliance historique que découlent les liens de parenté qui unissent aujourd’hui les Toyamana des Chefferies de Doguéraoua, Illéla, Tamaské, Agadez, Tanout, Gangara…
Ainsi, face aux enjeux actuels de sécurité, de cohésion sociale et d’emploi des jeunes, la figure du Sultan Oumarou Ibrahim Oumarou rappelle une vérité immuable : les sables se déplacent et les empires passent, mais la justice, l’écoute et l’hospitalité demeurent les plus sûrs remparts de la paix. Fidèle à la dynamique de la refondation et à l’ambition de souveraineté, Son Altesse a vu son influence nationale renforcée suite à son élection, le jeudi 11 décembre 2025 à Maradi, à la présidence de l’Association des Chefs Traditionnels du Niger (ACTN), lors de sa 10ᵉ Assemblée générale. Cette nouvelle responsabilité consacre la noblesse et la persévérance légendaire de ce Souverain hors norme. À ce titre, le succès de Sa Majesté Oumarou Ibrahim Oumarou ne doit rien au hasard ; il est le fruit d’une discipline de fer. Si la motivation est un élan éphémère, la discipline, elle, demeure le pilier constant de sa progression. Ce bâtisseur incarne un leadership rare, fondé sur une bienveillance qui transcende tous les clivages. Loin des discours partisans, son engagement se traduit par des actions concrètes envers ses populations, replaçant l’humain au centre du pouvoir.
Son écoute des attentes de ses proches n’est pas de la naïveté, mais un choix moral courageux pour transformer notre diversité en force collective. En permettant à chaque habitant de se sentir vu et protégé, ce leader inspirant recrée le lien social et redonne confiance en l’avenir. Devant les défis de notre époque, il nous montre qu’un grand rassembleur ne divise pas pour régner, mais unit pour avancer. En ce sens, il choisit délibérément de rester à l’écart des affaires qui ne le concernent pas, faisant preuve d’une éclatante sagesse. La réserve du Sultan Oumarou rappelle une vérité fondamentale : la légitimité s’use dans la mêlée et se fortifie dans la hauteur. Le rôle d’un guide traditionnel n’est donc pas de descendre dans l’arène des rivalités politiques ou des faits divers. Son silence est plus éloquent que les déclarations : il prouve que le véritable pouvoir réside dans la maîtrise de soi. En demeurant le gardien des traditions sans interférer dans les affaires d’autrui, le Sultan Oumarou Ibrahim Oumarou préserve toute son influence. Il s’assure ainsi le respect indéfectible de ceux qui voient en lui l’ancre de la cité du nord. En plaçant l’excellence au cœur de ses choix, le Sultan de l’Aïr refuse le compromis de la médiocrité, érigeant chaque action, même la plus modeste, en un devoir de perfection.
Que le Très-Haut, Maître de l’univers, l’Omniscient et l’Omnipotent, veille sur le Sultan de l’Aïr, lui accorde sa guidance, le bien-être et le bonheur. Qu’Il le guide vers ce qu’Il aime et l’entoure de conseillers pieux et de notables sincères pour l’accompagner vers le bien. Puisse Allah fasse du Sultan de l’Aïr un Artisan de Justice, de paix et de prospérité pour la région, le Niger et ses habitants. Amen ! Moustapha Kadi Oumani

items.title: Fresh clashes at the Eritrean border — is Ethiopia sliding into a regional war?

original_payload.original_title: Fresh clashes at the Eritrean border — is Ethiopia sliding into a regional war?
original_payload.original_body:
Politics   Ethiopia
Ethiopia-Eritrea border clashes raise fears of regional war
David Ehl
11/17/2026  November 17, 2026    As Ethiopian troops push Tigrayan forces toward the Eritrean border, fears of a new regional war are growing. With tensions rising between Ethiopia, Eritrea and Sudan, the Horn of Africa faces uncertain times ahead.
https://p.dw.com/p/5PXwP
Prefer DW on Google
Tensions in the Horn of Africa are at an all-time high Image: EDUARDO SOTERAS/AFP/Getty Images       Advertisement
After  a few weeks of relative stability , fresh clashes in the contested  Ethiopia-Eritrea border area have raised fears of a full-fledged war. Meanwhile, diplomatic relations between  Ethiopia  and  Sudan have hit new lows.
Fighters allied with the  Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF)  launched their  offensive on September 23 . It was aimed at overthrowing the Ethiopian government as part of a larger rebel coalition. But the Ethiopian National Defense Forces (ENDF), backed by pro-government militia, have steadily  pushed the TPLF out of Tigray, a region in northern Ethiopia .
According to the conflict tracker of the monitoring organization ACLED, the ENDF have pushed further into Tigray, effectively driving the Tigrayan Defense Forces (TDF)  towards the border with Eritrea.  Skirmishes have been reported from several locations, while the ENDF have fired heavy artillery towards dwellings close to the Eritrean border town of Badme.
While no census data is publicly available, Badme appears to be a small rural town on satellite images. However, the locality is historically significant for both sides because it was the ground zero of the Eritrean-Ethiopian War from 1998 to 2000, sometimes dubbed the Badme War.
The war ended with the Algiers Agreement    , in which both countries agreed to honor the rulings of a newly formed Eritrea-Ethiopia Boundary Commission. The commission awarded Badme to  Eritrea , a decision that Ethiopia challenged at times. Abdurahman Sayed, director of the London-based  Horn of Africa  Center for Regional Integration, told DW that Ethiopia might see an advantage in reclaiming Badme to resolve its current internal struggles.
"It seems now if the Eritreans withdrew and the Ethiopians came back, it could be to calm down the Tigrayans, especially those who are now supporting the party in power in Ethiopia", Sayed said.
Ethiopia: Who is fighting whom — and why?
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that  supports HTML5 video
He suggested that people like Getachew Reda, a former spokesman for the TPLF and current advisor to  Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed,  might be able to win the Tigrayan people over to side with the federal government through territorial gains for the Tigray region.
The ever-looming threat of a full-fledged war with Eritrea
"The coming of the forces to the Eritrean-Ethiopian border clearly indicates that the  conflict can be triggered any time ", Abdurahman Sayed said.
Eritrean and Ethiopian government troops  allied against the Tigrayan forces during the 2020-22 Tigray conflict. Since then, Eritrea's allegiances have shifted towards the TPLF and away from Abiy Ahmed's central government. In October,  the two neighbors cut diplomatic ties . At one point,  Eritrean troops reportedly crossed the border into Tigray .
Ethiopia's broken Tigray peace deal opens old wounds
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that  supports HTML5 video
Magnus Taylor, a regional analyst with the International Crisis Group (ICG), believes that Addis Ababa's prime objective for the moment might rather be securing its northern border and destroying supply lines between Eritrea and Tigrayan forces.
"So what we might actually be seeing is a kind of a function of the attempts by the Ethiopian military to consolidate its control of Tigray, which includes pushing Tigray's borders with Eritrea", Taylor told DW.
However, securing control over Tigray could also involve  direct conflict with Eritrea  at one point, Taylor said: "If this happens, then it's quite likely that the Ethiopians would attempt to carry out all their objectives in Eritrea at one time."
Since Eritrea seceded from Ethiopia in 1993, Ethiopia has been the world's largest landlocked country by population. Prime Minister Abiy has repeatedly described the country's lack of sea access as an existential threat. While stating a preference for peaceful means to gain access, he said this could also mean capturing  Eritrea's easternmost port, Assab , by force.
The ongoing clashes have displaced many local residents like this Amhara woman to other parts of Ethiopia Image: Marco Simoncelli/AFP
Ethiopia-Sudan relations at crossroads
At the same time, the  diplomatic relations between Ethiopia and its northwestern neighbor, Sudan, have deteriorated  even further.
Sudan  and  Egypt , both downstream the river Nile, have been on edge for years because of  Ethiopia's Grand Renaissance Dam (GERD) . The massive GERD, built on the Blue Nile just kilometers from Ethiopia's border with Sudan, gives Addis Ababa significant leverage over the timing and regulation of water flows downstream, raising concerns in Sudan and Egypt over water security and dam operations. The Ethiopian government has rejected claims that the dam could be used as a  means to pressure Sudan and Egypt .
The RSF militants reportedly receive support from Ethiopia and the United Arab Emirates. However, both countries deny the allegations Image: Rapid Support Forces/AFP
Since 2023, Sudan has been  embroiled in a civil war  between two rival military forces: the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), led by General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, and the  Rapid Support Forces (RSF )  , led by Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti . In mid-November, both sides accused the other of direct participation in each other's internal conflicts.
Two countries with severe internal conflicts and mirroring alliances: Could the situation deteriorate further into potential direct fights between the two armies? ICG's Magnus Taylor believes there is a risk, but at least not for now.
"The most likely scenario is we just get a continuation of this kind of proxy style of involvement with each other's opposition groups rather than formal direct involvement on the ground in the conflict," Taylor said.
Sayed also believes that, at the moment, there is no need for direct confrontation.
"The RSF can do the job that Ethiopia and any other country backing them wants them to do," Sayed said. "But if there is a need and the RSF are failing, the Ethiopian army could be pushed to get involved."
David Ehl   Reporter and editor          David_Ehl

items.title: Minister tasks states, investors on implementation of National Care Policy

original_payload.original_title: Minister tasks states, investors on implementation of National Care Policy
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Minister tasks states, investors on implementation of National Care Policy
By  Folashade Adeniran   ·   18 seconds ago   ·  5 min read
✓
✓
By Babajide Awoyinfa
The Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Hajiya Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim, has called for increased investment in childcare and essential care services, describing them as critical infrastructure for Nigeria’s economic growth.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the minister made the call in a special address delivered through her representative, Andrew Ali Madugu, Director, Child Development Department, at the World Bank Group’s National Care Forum in Lagos.
The forum, held at the Lagos Marriott Hotel, Ikeja, has the theme: “Advancing Nigeria’s Care Economy: Jobs, Growth and Productivity”.
Sulaiman-Ibrahim said Nigeria must recognise childcare and other essential care services as economic infrastructure capable of improving productivity, expanding businesses and strengthening women’s participation in the workforce.
“If we want to increase productivity, grow small businesses and expand women’s participation in the economy, we must begin to treat childcare and other essential care services as infrastructure that support economic growth,” she said.
She said developing a sustainable care economy required strategic partnerships, adequate financing and institutional arrangements reflecting Nigeria’s diverse social and economic realities.
According to her, the National Care Policy provides an opportunity to engage investors, employers, development partners and service providers in developing practical and scalable solutions.
The minister stressed that state and local governments must drive implementation and investment, while communities, development partners and private-sector actors contribute to accessible and sustainable care services.
She also emphasised the need to develop a skilled, protected and adequately remunerated care workforce, including childcare workers, social workers, domestic workers and other professionals.
Sulaiman-Ibrahim challenged the private sector to regard the care economy as an investment opportunity, noting that government alone could not finance or deliver the required services.
She identified translating the National Care Policy into measurable implementation, strengthening institutional coordination, mobilising financing and developing community-based care infrastructure as key priorities.
Earlier, Gov. Babajide Sanwo-Olu of Lagos State, represented by the Commissioner for Finance, Mr Abayomi Oluyomi, said sustainable care solutions required stronger collaboration between government and private-sector investors.
In his welcome address, Oluyomi said economic productivity depended not only on employment opportunities, infrastructure and investment capital, but also on support systems enabling people to participate effectively in economic activities.
He observed that many workers, particularly women, faced challenges balancing employment and business responsibilities with childcare and other family obligations.
“These responsibilities determine whether they can take up employment opportunities, expand their businesses or pursue opportunities that will improve their livelihoods,” he said.
Oluyomi said Lagos state’s development agenda recognised that infrastructure development and human development must advance together.
He listed investments in transportation, healthcare, education, economic opportunities and social protection as part of the state’s efforts to improve residents’ productivity and wellbeing.
The commissioner called for financing arrangements bringing together governments, development partners, employers and private investors to expand access to quality care services.
He said government must establish appropriate regulations, quality and safety standards and a supportive business environment without making essential care services unaffordable for ordinary families.
Also speaking, Christian Mulamula, Head of Office, Nigeria, International Finance Corporation (IFC), World Bank Group, described the care economy as central to women’s economic participation, children’s development, job creation and inclusive growth.
Mulamula said Nigeria had taken an important step with the National Care Policy, adding that its successful implementation required collective commitment from government, employers, care providers, financial institutions and development partners.
He said employers could support the agenda through workplace childcare facilities and family-friendly policies, while financial institutions and investors could provide capital for viable childcare businesses.
According to him, the World Bank Group is supporting efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s childcare sector through skills development, private-sector engagement and improved policy frameworks.
He disclosed that the World Bank’s Innovation Development and Effectiveness in the Acquisition of Skills (IDEAS) Project supported the development of Nigeria’s first National Occupational Standards for childcare.
Mulamula said more than 4,500 aspiring caregivers and entrepreneurs, approximately 90 per cent of them women, were undergoing training based on the standards.
He explained that the standards covered safety, hygiene, nutrition, responsive caregiving and early childhood stimulation.
He added that the IFC’s Nigeria Gender Country Programme and Care Works Nigeria were working with employers, strengthening childcare enterprises and exploring financing opportunities for businesses operating within the sector.
Mulamula further said the proposed Nigeria Early Childhood Development operation, being prepared with the Federal Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning, was expected to support integrated services across all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.
He said the initiative would also support childcare regulation and financing, helping to establish a quality childcare market across the country.
The forum explored the economic case for investing in childcare, particularly its implications for women’s workforce participation, job creation and business productivity.
Discussions also examined financing opportunities for childcare businesses, implementation of Nigeria’s National Care Policy and partnerships required to build an accessible, sustainable care economy.
Participants included senior government officials, representatives of the IFC, UN Women, development partners and private-sector leaders.
The discussions highlighted that closing gender gaps in key sectors can  add nearly 23 billion dollars to Nigeria’s economy, underscoring the economic importance of expanding women’s participation and investing in care services. (NAN)

original_payload.original_title: RTEAN chairman urges Lagos to strengthen LagRide, e-hailing industry
original_payload.original_body:
Generative AI  RTEAN chairman urges Lagos to strengthen LagRide, e-hailing industry
By  Folashade Adeniran   ·   6 minutes ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Henry Oladele
The Road Transport Employers Association of Nigeria (RTEAN), Ojo, Zone 4, has urged the Lagos State Government to strengthen LagRide and improve the operating environment for e-hailing drivers.
The Zonal Chairman, Mr Nurudeen Eniafe, made the appeal in a statement issued on Tuesday in Lagos.
He called for improved collaboration among government, e-hailing companies, transport unions and other stakeholders to promote sustainable transportation services.
Eniafe said that driver welfare was important to the development of the e-hailing industry.
He identified fuel, vehicle maintenance, insurance, vehicle rentals and other operational expenses as issues requiring attention.
Eniafe said that the changing cost of fuel and vehicle maintenance had made it necessary to review the industry’s operating arrangements.
He urged e-hailing platforms to consider transparent commission structures and fare arrangements that reflected prevailing operating costs.
He also recommended regular engagement between platform operators and driver representatives on issues affecting the industry.
The transport unionist called for stronger representation of e-hailing drivers to enable them participate effectively in discussions concerning their welfare and working conditions.
Eniafe urged the state government to reposition LagRide as a competitive local alternative in the digital transportation market.
He recommended expanding access to properly maintained vehicles, affordable hire-purchase arrangements, and electric and compressed natural gas-powered vehicles.
‘’Other proposals included accessible vehicle maintenance facilities, improved customer service, transparent commission structures and stronger driver welfare programmes, ‘’ he said.
Eniafe urged the government to also publish performance reports detailing LagRide’s financial and operational outcomes.
Citing his experience during a visit to Qatar for a transportation conference, he highlighted the importance of effective government regulation of e-hailing operations.
He said that government oversight was necessary to promote safety standards, protect passengers, encourage investment and ensure an organised transportation system.
Eniafe also called on e-hailing companies to commence discussions with recognised driver representatives and relevant transport authorities.
He identified commission reviews, transparent trip deductions, appropriate fare structures and fair account suspension procedures as areas requiring attention.
He urged the state government, particularly the Ministry of Transportation, to convene a stakeholders’ meeting involving e-hailing operators, driver associations, transport unions and industry experts.
‘’The meeting should examine driver earnings, platform charges, vehicle financing, maintenance costs, passenger safety and the industry’s sustainability, ‘’ he said.
Eniafe further recommended an independent assessment of the local e-hailing market to determine the economic conditions of drivers.
He stressed that transportation development should balance profitability, passenger satisfaction, effective regulation and the welfare of service providers.
Eniafe urged the government and private operators to build a sustainable transportation system that recognised drivers as important partners in the industry. (NAN)

items.title: AfDB approves $102m facility to finance SMEs, create 6,000 jobs in Nigeria

original_payload.original_title: AfDB approves $102m facility to finance SMEs, create 6,000 jobs in Nigeria
original_payload.original_body:
Economy/Business  AfDB approves $102m facility to finance SMEs, create 6,000 jobs in Nigeria
By  Ndubisi Ijeoma   ·   1 hour ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
​‌‌‍‌‌⁠‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‌‌​​‍‌‌ By Lucy Ogalue
The African Development Bank (AfDB) has approved a 102 million dollar financing package for Sterling Bank Nigeria Ltd. to expand access to finance for businesses.
This is contained in a statement released by the bank on Tuesday in Abuja.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the facility is expected to support at least 200 businesses and create up to 6,000 jobs across Nigeria.
The package comprises a 50-million-dollar line of credit, a 20-million-dollar sustainable loan, a two-million-dollar concessional loan and a 30-million-dollar trade finance guarantee.
The bank said the financing would support SMEs, women and youth-led enterprises, sustainable investments and vulnerable farming communities.
It said the facility would provide competitively priced, long-term financing to businesses in healthcare, education, agriculture, renewable energy and transportation.
“At least 30 per cent of the line of credit will be allocated to eligible women-owned, women-led and youth-owned enterprises.
“The concessional loan, provided under the bank’s Agri-Food SME Catalytic Financing Mechanism, will support vulnerable smallholder farmers and agricultural SMEs.
“Through Sterling Affordable Microlending Programme, the financing is expected to reach more than 5,000 farmers affected by displacement, insecurity and climate-related shocks,” it said.
According to AfDB, the programme is being implemented in collaboration with the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees.
“The package will also support qualifying green and social projects under Sterling Bank’s Sustainable Financing Framework.
“In addition, the trade finance guarantee is expected to support up to 150 million dollars in transactions, helping businesses access new markets,” it said.
Dr Abdul Kamara, AfDB Acting Vice-President for Regional Development, Integration and Business Delivery, and Director-General for Nigeria, said businesses faced different financing challenges.
“A vibrant private sector is critical to Nigeria’s economic transformation, but different businesses face different financing challenges,” Kamara said.
He said the package combined financing for SMEs, women and youth-led enterprises, vulnerable farming communities, sustainable investments and trade.
Abubakar Suleiman, Sterling Bank’s Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, said long-term economic growth depended on strengthening local businesses’ productive capacity.
He said the partnership would help address financing gaps affecting SMEs, women, young entrepreneurs and underserved communities.
According to him, the approval builds on AfDB’s earlier financing support for Nigerian enterprises through local financial institutions.
“Earlier this year, the bank approved a 61-million-dollar package for the Development Bank of Nigeria to support women-led businesses.
“It also approved a 200-million-dollar facility for the Bank of Industry to strengthen enterprise growth and industrial development,” he said.(NAN)
Edited by Kadiri Abdulrahman

original_payload.original_body:
General News  Adesina to launch women’s empowerment initiative in Abuja
By  Funmilayo Adeyemi   ·   1 hour ago   ·  Updated  47 seconds ago   ·  2 min read
✓
✓
By Adesewa George
A US-based Nigerian, Mrs Faithful Adesina, says she will launch a women’s empowerment initiative, Esther’s Conclave, in Abuja on Dec. 12.
Adesina, convener of the initiative, in a statement on Tuesday said the programme would focus on the spiritual, intellectual and financial development of women.
She said the initiative was inspired by a vision of women gathering to receive spiritual guidance, financial management training and other personal development support.
According to her, the biblical Queen Esther provided the model for the initiative, especially her courage and influence in securing the deliverance of her people.
Adesina said the initiative was intended to encourage women to develop their knowledge, financial capacity and influence alongside their spiritual lives.
She said her motivation was also informed by the need for believers to build supportive communities.
“I am passionate about this mission because we are in the last days, and I sense that God is beckoning on us believers to begin to build communities where we can share and grow spiritually, financially and intellectually.
“This will enable us to thrive in the difficult days ahead and also establish His will and agenda on earth. I know we are called for such a time as this.
“Registration is free through  https://forms.gle/3Tefp242LXyFcpw39  ,” she said.
She said Esther’s Conclave was an offshoot of Kingdom Giantess Ministries (KGM), an organisation focused on women’s spiritual and personal development.
Adesina explained that the Esther’s Conclave Community would operate through a WhatsApp platform to facilitate interaction, information-sharing and mutual support among members.
She said the community would also promote resource-sharing, drawing inspiration from the biblical account of early Christians in Acts 4:32.
According to her, the maiden gathering will introduce participants to the initiative’s objectives and planned activities through discussions, fellowship and spiritual activities.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the programme is open to women aged 18 to 45 and will hold in Abuja. (NAN)

The Institute of Public Health (IPH), College of Health Science, Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), Ile-Ife will  organise free medical outreach for older persons in Ilesa, Osun on Nov.21.
The Director of IPH, Prof. Oluwafemi Aluko, made this known during a phone interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Tuesday in Abuja.
NAN reports that IPH in OAU, Ile-Ife was founded in 1994 to advance health development, disease prevention, and multi-disciplinary public health scholarship, policy, and practice.
According to Oliwafemi, the IPH will collaborate with Ijesaland Geriatric Centre in Ilesa, a specialised medical facility dedicated to healthcare for senior citizens aged 60 and above to carry out the programme.
The director said the programme would afford the public access to eye screening and cataract surgery for eligible patients and cervical cancer screening and clinical breast examinations for older women.
Others he listed were: men’s  prostate cancer screening; dental care (scaling and polishing); general checks: blood pressure; blood sugar; hepatitis; malaria and urine tests.
He added that there would be free drugs for common conditions; health talks on healthy ageing, nutrition and disease preservation; and physical exercise sessions with a fitness instructor.
Aluko reiterated that beneficiaries would be older persons of age 60 years and above, with their families and caregivers.
He explained that the outreach themed: “Key into WHO Decade of Healthy Ageing: A Global collaboration’’ would be in memory of the 15th APAL Annual Prof. Adetokunbo Lucas posthumous 95th birthday (1931- 2020) slated for Nov.25.
Aluko described late Lucas, who was born in Lagos Nov. 25, 1931, as a public health icon that grew into one of the most respected names in world public health.
“Prof. Lucas became Professor of Preventive and Social Medicine at the University of Ibadan at about 33 years. His research on meningitis, malaria and schistosomiasis broke new grounds.
“He was the pioneer Chairman of the Nigerian Medical Research Council (1973) and, in 1984, chaired the Committee on Nigeria`s National Health Policy. He helped shape how our country thinks about health.
“In 1976, Prof.  Lucas became the first Director of TDR, the Special Programme for Research and Training in Tropical Diseases Based at WHO in Geneva which he led for ten years,’’ he said.
According to him, late Lucas pioneered a new  partnership between public health and the pharmaceutical industry, starting with Merck, to use ivermectin against river blindness.
“At the Carnegie Corporation of New York (1986- 1990), Prof. Lucas launched the Prevention of Maternal Mortality Programme, working with universities across West Africa to save women`s lives in childbirth.
“A Rockefeller fellowship first took Prof. Lucas to Harvard in the 1950s. In 1990 he returned as Professor of International Health at the Harvard School of Public Health, and remained an adjunct professor there.
“Prof. Lucas received the Prince Mahido Award (1999), the Jimmy and Rosalynn Carter Humanitarian Award (2013), a Harvard Medal at the university`s 350th anniversary, and Nigeria’s national honour, Officer of the Order of the Federal Republic (OFR),” he said. (NAN)

original_payload.original_title: SGF, Surveyor-General urge African countries to invest in geospatial technology
original_payload.original_body:
Metro  SGF, Surveyor-General urge African countries to invest in geospatial technology
By  Philip Daniel Yatai   ·   37 minutes ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Angela Atabo
The Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Sen. George Akume, and the Surveyor-General of the Federation (SGOF), Abdulganiyu Adebomehin, have urged African countries to invest in geospatial technology to accelerate development.
They made the call at the opening of the 57th Meeting of the Governing Council of the African Regional Institute of Geospatial Information Science and Technology (AFRIGIST), on Monday in Abuja.
Akume, represented by the Permanent Secretary, General Services Office, OSGF, Dr Abubakar Kana, said geospatial information had become indispensable in addressing the continent’s growing developmental challenges through informed, ta-driven and innovative solutions.
“The African continent is increasingly confronted with complex developmental challenges that require informed, data-driven, and innovative solutions.
“Whether in the areas of land administration, or urban planning, agriculture, environmental management, infrastructure development, disaster risk reduction, security, or climate resilience, the role of geospatial information has become indispensable.
“Accurate and timely geospatial data now serves as a critical foundation for effective governance and sustainable development.”
Akume urged AFRIGIST, as Africa’s foremost regional institution dedicated to capacity building on geospatial science and technology, to continue to provide leadership in developing the human and institutional capacities.
He said this would aid in providing the required capacity to harness the immense potential of geospatial information for the benefit of African nations and its people.
He said reliable geospatial data and skilled professionals were essential to achieving the African Union’s Agenda 2063, the Sustainable Development Goals and other regional development frameworks.
He urged the Governing Council to use the meeting to review the institute’s programmes, strengthen partnerships, explore innovative funding mechanisms and establish a strategic direction to enhance its relevance.
The SGF said the challenges confronting Africa transcended national boundaries and required collective action and regional cooperation.
Akume noted that as digital transformation continued to reshape economies and societies, geospatial information would remain vital to evidence-based decision-making.
On his part, Adebomehin said the meeting provided an opportunity to review the institute’s performance and strengthen its governance and sustainability.
Adebomehin, who is also the Chairman of AFRIGIST governing council, said growing demand for geospatial information across Africa had made the institute’s mandate increasingly important to economic planning, food security, environmental management, public health and national security.
He noted that emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, earth observation systems, unmanned aerial systems and geospatial data analytics, required the institute to continually adapt to changing needs.
He said the council would examine policy and financial matters, assess the institute’s activities and consider strategic initiatives to ensure its continued relevance.
Adebomehin urged member states to sustain their support through collaboration, investment and active participation in AFRIGIST programmes.
The Executive Director of AFRIGIST, Prof. Lazarus Ojigi, said the institute has trained no fewer than 4,000 professionals from over 29 African countries since its establishment in 1972.
Ojigi said the institute had continued to build critical human capacity in the application of aerospace and geospatial information science and technology across the continent.
He said the trainees included civil servants, military and paramilitary personnel, including technicians to postgraduate qualifications, professional master’s degrees and PhDs.
He described the institute as a bilingual pan-African institution operating in English and French under the auspices of the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA).
Ojigi commended the Federal Government for sustaining the institute’s vision and mandate, noting that Nigeria had satisfactorily fulfilled its obligations as host country, particularly in infrastructure development.
He said eight member states, namely Benin, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Ghana, Mali, Niger, Nigeria and Senegal, currently supported the institute through biennial recurrent budget contributions.
The executive director said the institute was expanding its membership base, with discussions ongoing with Côte d’Ivoire, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, South Africa, Rwanda, Togo and Sierra Leone.
Ojigi identified UNECA as a strategic partner, adding that the institute also maintained academic and technical partnerships with Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife, the Federal University of Technology, Akure, and the University of Abomey-Calavi, among others.
He however, identified the need for additional funding to establish an Advanced Geospatial Data Processing Laboratory for e-learning and Geospatial Artificial Intelligence (GeoAI).
According to him, the laboratory, already approved for establishment, will strengthen advanced geospatial analytics, remote capacity building, cloud computing, machine learning and research collaboration. (NAN)

items.title: Single window second phase to go live Dec. 14 – Director

original_payload.original_title: Single window second phase to go live Dec. 14 – Director
original_payload.original_body:
Economy/Business  Single window second phase to go live Dec. 14 – Director
By  Abdulrahman Kadiri   ·   1 hour ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Lucy Ogalue
The National Single Window (NSW) Project Director, Mr Tola Fakolade, says the second phase of the platform, focusing on exports, will go live on Dec. 14.
Fakolade said this at a stakeholder sensitisation programme on the implementation of Phase 2 of the NSW in Abuja on Tuesday.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that NSW is a centralised digital trade facilitation platform established by the Federal Government of Nigeria to unify and automate import, export, and transit processes.
It aspires to catalyse economic development by positioning Nigeria as a global leader in trade efficiency.
The director said the export phase would enable exporters to submit regulatory documents through one platform, accessible to relevant government agencies.
He said the platform would simplify export procedures and reduce the burden of dealing separately with multiple regulatory agencies.
He said the project would also make exporters’ activities easier and improve the efficiency of Nigeria’s export processes.
“Overall, the key takeaway from here is single window phase 2 export is launching on Dec. 14.
“With that, exporters will be able to use the single window for all their documents and regulatory requirements to export.
“Overall, we believe single window will help to simplify that process, to make the lives of exporters easier,” he said.
Fakolade said the first phase, which focused on import regulatory licences and certificates, had processed more than 169,000 licences, certificates and permits.
He said users had provided feedback that helped improve the platform, adding that adoption had increased after initial learning challenges.
The Controller of Customs on ICT Modernisation, Aondona Fayam, said the platform would enable exporters to submit documents once for access by relevant agencies.
He said the first phase was operating at 99.9 per cent and had improved documentation and clearance through digitalisation.
Fayam said the second phase would cover export documentation, reducing the need for exporters to visit several regulatory agencies.
He said the Customs Service was working to ensure compliance while making export processes more predictable for businesses.
Fayam identified knowledge gaps as an initial challenge with the platform and said sensitisation was being extended to exporters nationwide.
The Director of Trade Information at the Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC), Mr Ndubueze Okeke, said the engagement was aimed at sensitising exporters, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises.
Okeke said the platform would harmonise export documentation and procedures across agencies, supporting the transition from paper-based to digital processes.
He said the rollout would be phased, with additional export processes, including EEG and CBN-related requirements, expected in March 2027.
This collaborative effort is expected to pave the way for a future where trade is seamless, transparent and mutually beneficial for all stakeholders.(NAN)
Edited by Kadiri Abdulrahman

items.title: ​‌‌‍‌‌⁠‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‌​‌‍NEPC to integrate export registration, EEG platforms into Single Window

original_payload.original_title: ​‌‌‍‌‌⁠‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‌​‌‍NEPC to integrate export registration, EEG platforms into Single Window
original_payload.original_body:
Economy/Business  ​‌‌‍‌‌⁠‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‌​‌‍NEPC to integrate export registration, EEG platforms into Single Window
By  Ndubisi Ijeoma   ·   1 hour ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Lucy Ogalue
The Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC) says it is integrating its export registration and Export Expansion Grant (EEG) platforms into the National Single Window (NSW) to simplify export procedures and reduce delays.
The Executive Director of NEPC, Mrs Nonye Ayeni, said this at a stakeholder engagement on Phase Two of the NSW export implementation in Abuja on Tuesday.
Ayeni said the integration would simplify export procedures and address delays caused by multiple documentation and approval requirements across government agencies.
She said exporters currently faced repeated documentation and approval processes, sometimes resulting in delayed shipments and cancelled contracts.
“By the time the approval arrives, the buyer is already tired, frustrated, and this has led to contract cancellations,” she said.
Ayeni said delays could also affect perishable agricultural products, which might change colour or form before reaching their destinations.
She said NEPC would integrate its export certification and registration services, currently hosted on its electronic registration portal, into the NSW.
Ayeni added that the council’s automated EEG platform, developed by PwC, would also be connected through an application programming interface.
She said the connection was expected within one or two weeks, according to the implementation timeline presented at the meeting.
“What used to take weeks of frustration running around by different people will now become very seamless and very easy,” Ayeni said.
The NEPC chief urged exporters and other stakeholders to familiarise themselves with the platform and provide feedback to improve its implementation.
Also speaking, the Executive Chairman of the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS), Mr Zacch Adedeji, described the NSW as more than an information technology project, saying it represented a comprehensive reform of Nigeria’s trade processes.
Adedeji was represented by Mr Alfred Okoh, Group Director, Transformation and Strategic Management Office, NRS.
“For the NRS, it represents a paradigm shift from revenue collection at the borders to trade facilitation for growth, from fragmented compliance to integrated data-driven efficiency,” he said.
He said Phase Two involved sensitisation, institutional alignment and preparation of the export ecosystem, including defining data flows and harmonising requirements.
Adedeji said the NRS would support the platform through technical and institutional collaboration, adding that it could strengthen voluntary compliance and competitiveness.
“If they are not on the platform, there is no trade we are facilitating,” he said, emphasising the importance of private sector participation.
The NSW Project Head, Mr Tola Fakolade, said Phase One of the project was inaugurated on March 27.
He said Phase Two was expected to be inaugurated in December, while Phase Three remained a major component of the project.
Fakolade explained that the platform would provide a central portal through which traders could submit regulatory documents once for transmission to relevant agencies.
He said the system would reduce multiple submissions and improve transparency, traceability and coordination among agencies.
The Director of Trade Information at NEPC, Mr Ndubueze Okeke, said the platform would simplify trade procedures and improve coordination among government agencies.
He urged exporters to share practical experiences and raise concerns to ensure a smooth transition to the new system.
The Director of Information and Communication Technology at NAFDAC, Mr Femi Balogun, said agencies involved in cross-border trade needed to embrace digital transformation.
He said Phase Two would digitalise more aspects of trade processes, adding that NAFDAC supported efforts to improve service delivery.
The NSW is designed to provide a single-entry point for trade-related documentation and approvals without taking over the statutory responsibilities of participating agencies.(NAN)

items.title: Kalu pledges to help Otti restore Enyimba’s lost glory

original_payload.original_title: Kalu pledges to help Otti restore Enyimba’s lost glory
original_payload.original_body:
Politics  Kalu pledges to help Otti restore Enyimba’s lost glory
By  Nefisetu Yakubu   ·   3 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Nefishetu Yakubu
Sen. Orji Kalu has promised to support Gov. Alex Otti of Abia in restoring Enyimba Football Club to its former glory, after years of decline.
Kalu, representing Abia North Senatorial District, made the promise on Tuesday in Abuja while fielding questions from newsmen shortly after receiving the Senate Press Corps’ Best Impactful Representation Award.
He recalled promising Abia residents in 1999 to build stadia in Aba and Umuahia, and make Enyimba African champions, stressing that he fulfilled both promises.
“I told Aba and Umuahia people I would build two stadia, which I built. I told Aba people we would be African champions,” Kalu said.
He recalled that Enyimba won the league title for about five or six seasons and also lifted the FA Cup during his administration in Abia.
Kalu attributed the club’s success to discipline, recalling that he travelled from Umuahia to Aba before dawn to train with players before resuming official duties.
“Enyimba Football Club was really a disciplined club. You know that discipline is everything,” he said.
He blamed the club’s decline on what he described as Nigeria’s collapsing work ethic, calling for reorientation and fundamental reforms across the country’s institutions.
“The Nigerian working system is very bad; not only in Enyimba but in every aspect. We need reorientation and a surgical operation in our entire system,” he said.
Kalu expressed readiness to assist Otti in reviving the club, saying that he would accept an advisory appointment if the governor considered him suitable for the position.
“After Gov. Otti wins again, he will look into Enyimba. I will be his technical adviser to bring the club back to glory,” Kalu said.
He added that he could serve as a special adviser on Enyimba, insisting that the club deserved a return to its former status in African football.
The senator also commended Rangers International of Enugu for their continental performance, saying that he hoped another Nigerian club would win the prestigious African title in future.
“I want to see a second Nigerian club carrying that cup. Chief M.K.O. Abiola tried it, Chief Iwuanyanwu also made efforts,” he said.
He recalled Enyimba’s semi-final encounter with Al Ahly of Egypt, alleging that two long-range goals were disallowed before officials awarded a controversial late penalty.
“We were going to carry it for a third time. We gave them two goals during the semi-final in Egypt, but they disqualified both and later awarded them a penalty,” Kalu recounted.
The former governor urged Nigerians, particularly journalists, to demonstrate professionalism, take their responsibilities seriously and keep to time when carrying out their professional duties.
“Whatever you want to do, do it well. If you want to be a journalist, be a journalist well; stand up to your duties,” he said.
Kalu urged citizens across professions to remain committed to their work, adding that national development required discipline, responsibility and dedication.(NAN)
NY/WAS

items.title: FG seeks stronger private sector role to end open defecation

original_payload.original_title: FG seeks stronger private sector role to end open defecation
original_payload.original_body:
Environment  FG seeks stronger private sector role to end open defecation
By  Tosin Kolade   ·   3 hours ago   ·  Updated  2 hours ago   ·  6 min read
✓
✓
By Tosin Kolade
The Federal Government has urged private sector organisations to support efforts to end open defecation in Nigeria through their Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) programmes.
The Minister of Water Resources and Sanitation, Prof. Joseph Utsev, made the call at the 6th National Retreat for States on the Clean Nigeria Campaign (CNC) in Abuja on Tuesday.
The retreat has the theme: ‘Accelerating and Sustaining Progress: Financing, Data and Systems for an ODF Nigeria’.
Utsev said sustainable sanitation required stronger collaboration among the Federal, State and Local Governments, development partners, civil society organisations and the private sector.
He said government resources alone were insufficient to address the country’s sanitation challenges, urging businesses to complement public funding through strategic partnerships and investments.
The minister also called on all tiers of government to make deliberate budgetary provisions for sanitation, emphasising that the sector should not depend solely on occasional interventions or development partner support.
He identified financing, reliable data and institutional strengthening as three critical priorities for accelerating progress and sustaining open defecation-free (ODF) achievements.
Utsev said 185 Local Government Areas (LGAs) had attained ODF status since the inauguration of the Clean Nigeria Campaign in November 2019.
He, however, said the achievement remained below expectations, adding that the government was working to accelerate progress and exceed 400 ODF LGAs by 2027.
The minister said President Bola Tinubu had signed the Executive Order on Open Defecation-Free Nigeria to strengthen the policy and institutional framework for achieving the target.
Utsev urged state governments, relevant institutions, development partners and civil society organisations to familiarise themselves with the provisions of the order and translate them into practical actions.
He also called for stronger monitoring and accountability, noting that the focus should not be limited to toilet construction but should include the proper use and maintenance of sanitation facilities.
Earlier, the National Coordinator of the Clean Nigeria Campaign, Mrs Chizoma Opara, also called for increased private sector participation, particularly through CSR initiatives and innovative financing arrangements.
Opara said inadequate and unpredictable financing, household poverty and affordability barriers remained major challenges to achieving the country’s ODF targets.
She said Nigeria had targeted 172 ODF LGAs by December 2025 but achieved 162, falling short of the target by 10.
According to her, the 2026 target is 234 LGAs, against which 185 have so far attained the status, while the 2027 target is at least 318 LGAs.
She said the figures showed that the country was not progressing at the pace required to achieve its sanitation targets.
Opara identified the campaign’s six strategic pillars as an enabling environment, public financing, service delivery, ministerial leadership and advocacy, monitoring and evaluation, and effective coordination.
She said the campaign was targeting at least 300 ODF LGAs by 2027 and at least three additional states achieving ODF status.
The coordinator listed Kano, Benue and Bauchi among the states being supported to accelerate progress, adding that Sokoto was also making progress.
The Country Director of Self Help Africa, Mrs Joy Aderele, commended the Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation and the Clean Nigeria Campaign Secretariat for their leadership and continued commitment to improving sanitation.
Aderele said the campaign had provided an important platform for coordinating government and non-state actors through advocacy, stakeholder engagement, environmental education and community mobilisation.
She, however, emphasised that achieving ODF status was not enough without measures to sustain the gains and prevent communities from returning to open defecation.
She called for stronger community monitoring and institutional accountability, urging stakeholders to use the retreat to share experiences, challenges and practical solutions.
Also, UNICEF’s WASH Manager, Ms Jolly Maulit, said Nigeria had made progress since inaugurating the Clean Nigeria Campaign in 2019, with Jigawa becoming the first state to achieve statewide ODF status in 2022 and Katsina following in 2025.
Maulit said the revised National ODF Roadmap, completed in 2025 and recently gazetted, provided further direction for improving sanitation and accelerating progress towards the 2030 target.
She called for reliable performance data to help identify areas requiring support and improve the tracking of progress across states and local governments.
The UNICEF official also urged governments to integrate sanitation into their policies, budgets and dedicated financing mechanisms rather than relying solely on development partner-supported projects.
She said sustainable sanitation financing should involve government budgets, development finance, private sector investment and financial sector partners.
Similarly, the World Health Organisation (WHO) Representative, Dr Edwin Isotu-Edeh, said a large proportion of Nigeria’s population still practised open defecation, leaving affected communities vulnerable to cholera and other diseases of public health concern.
Isotu-Edeh said sanitation should become a way of life through sustained behavioural change and a culture of cleanliness in homes, institutions and communities.
He identified the gap between awareness and actual behavioural change as a major challenge, noting that knowledge about hygiene did not always translate into consistent practices.
The WHO representative called for improved access to handwashing facilities and sustained hygiene promotion as part of the Clean Nigeria Campaign.
He also urged a coordinated, multi-sectoral approach involving the ministries responsible for water resources, health and environment, stressing that sanitation was not only a WASH and public health concern but also an economic issue.
Meanwhile, the General Manager of the FCT Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Agency (RUWASSA), Dr Joyce Echoke, said more than 300 communities in Kwali Area Council had been certified ODF and submitted for national-level validation.
She said the FCT was working towards achieving statewide ODF status by 2027, expressing optimism that the target could be attained through collective commitment and stakeholder support.
The RUWASSA general manager said the agency’s next priority was to intensify public education and advocacy to ensure that residents used available toilets properly.
She observed that some residents continued to practise open defecation even where toilet facilities were available, underscoring the need for sustained sensitisation and behavioural change.
Speaking on behalf of state commissioners responsible for water resources, environment and sanitation, Mr Samuel Akange, who represented Benue State Commissioner Mr Odo Ogwu, said states were central to implementing national sanitation policies.
Akange said states would strengthen their State Task Groups on Sanitation and provide the political commitment and budgetary support required to drive the campaign.
He also called for stronger Community-Led Total Sanitation interventions to ensure that no community was left behind.
The Clean Nigeria Campaign was inaugurated in November 2019 to mobilise Nigerians towards ending open defecation and improving sanitation practices nationwide.( NAN )

items.title: Le Bénin sélectionné parmi les 27 meilleures destinations au monde à visiter en 2027 selon Condé Nast Traveler

original_payload.original_title: Le Bénin sélectionné parmi les 27 meilleures destinations au monde à visiter en 2027 selon Condé Nast Traveler
original_payload.original_body:
Cotonou, le 16 novembre 2026 -  Le Bénin figure parmi les 27 meilleures destinations au monde à visiter en 2027 selon Condé Nast Traveler, l’un des médias internationaux de référence dans le secteur du voyage. Publiée le 13 novembre 2026, cette sélection annuelle, intitulée « The 27 Best Places to Go in 2027 », met à l’honneur les destinations qui se distinguent par la richesse de leurs expériences, leur dynamisme et les nouvelles perspectives qu’elles offrent aux voyageurs. Une nouvelle reconnaissance internationale qui témoigne de l’attractivité grandissante du Bénin sur la scène touristique mondiale.
Appartenant au prestigieux groupe de médias Condé Nast, Condé Nast Traveler s’est imposé comme une référence mondiale en matière de tourisme et d’art de voyager. Suivi par des millions de lecteurs à travers le monde, le média joue un rôle majeur dans la découverte et la mise en lumière des destinations internationales. Sa sélection annuelle « Best Places to Go », élaborée par ses équipes éditoriales avec le concours de journalistes et d’experts du voyage, constitue ainsi une reconnaissance particulièrement significative pour les destinations retenues. Pour son édition 2027, le magazine distingue notamment le Bénin pour la richesse de son patrimoine historique, le dynamisme de sa scène artistique et les transformations engagées pour développer une nouvelle offre de tourisme culturel.
Dans son article consacré au Bénin, Condé Nast Traveler souligne particulièrement les perspectives ouvertes par les projets muséaux à Cotonou, Ouidah et Abomey, la valorisation des traditions Vodun, ainsi que les initiatives permettant aux Afro-descendants de renouer avec leurs origines. Le média met également en lumière les Vodun Days, dont la prochaine édition se tiendra du 2 au 9 janvier 2027 à Ouidah, mais aussi la cité lacustre de Ganvié et l’émergence du Bénin dans les itinéraires de croisières internationales.
Cette distinction s’inscrit dans la continuité des reconnaissances obtenues par la destination ces dernières années. Après son intégration au Top 10 des pays à visiter en 2024 selon Lonely Planet et sa présence dans la sélection « Where to Go in 2025 » du magazine américain AFAR, le Bénin a récemment remporté quatre distinctions majeures aux Africa Tourism Awards 2026 : « Destination touristique de l’année »,
« Destination culturelle de l’année », « Vidéo touristique de l’année » et « Agence nationale du tourisme de l’année », cette dernière ayant été attribuée à Bénin Tourisme.
« Cette sélection par Condé Nast Traveler constitue un signal particulièrement encourageant pour la destination Bénin. Elle témoigne de l’intérêt grandissant que suscitent notre patrimoine, notre culture et les transformations engagées pour enrichir l’expérience des visiteurs. C’est également une reconnaissance du travail collectif mené pour faire découvrir le Bénin à de nouveaux publics. Notre ambition est de poursuivre cette dynamique et de faire du Bénin une destination touristique de référence, reconnue pour la singularité et la qualité de ses expériences »,  a déclaré Sindé CHEKETE, Directeur général de Bénin Tourisme.
Porté par la marque-pays « Bénin, un Monde de Splendeurs », le pays poursuit ainsi son rayonnement sur la scène touristique internationale. À travers le développement de son offre, la valorisation de ses patrimoines et le déploiement de campagnes de promotion, le Bénin entend renforcer son attractivité et inviter toujours plus de voyageurs à découvrir ses multiples richesses.
Découvrez l’article consacré au Bénin dans la sélection « The 27 Best Places to Go in 2027 » de Condé Nast Traveler.
À propos de Bénin Tourisme
L’Agence Béninoise pour le Développement du Tourisme (Bénin Tourisme) est l’organisme public chargé de la mise en œuvre opérationnelle de la stratégie nationale de développement touristique du Bénin. À travers la marque-pays « Bénin, un Monde de Splendeurs », elle œuvre à la promotion et au rayonnement international du pays, au développement d’une offre touristique attractive et compétitive, ainsi qu’à l’accompagnement des professionnels du secteur. Par ses initiatives, Bénin Tourisme contribue à positionner le pays comme une destination touristique de référence sur les scènes africaine et internationale. original_payload.original_body:
Karim Oscar ANONRIN
Le Ministre délégué auprès du Ministre de l’Economie et des Finances, chargé de la mobilisation des ressources extérieures et de la gestion de la dette Hugues Oscar Lokossou, était ce mardi 17 novembre 2026 devant la Commission budgétaire de l’Assemblée nationale. Ce projet de budget est reparti en dépenses du personnel estimées à 5,14 milliards Fcfa et en achat de biens et services à hauteur de 1,88 milliards Fcfa (Répartition par nature). Du document présenté aux députés hier, il ressort que le ministère a prévu six orientations stratégiques pour la gestion 2027. Il s’agira d’accroître la mobilisation des financements innovants et durables, de renforcer la transparence et la responsabilité dans la gestion de la dette publique, de restructurer les portefeuilles des bailleurs en les alignés sur les priorités actuelles, de mettre en cohérence les stratégies pays des différents bailleurs avec le PAG/PND, d’assurer un suivi rapproché des projets en grande difficulté et de mobiliser davantage de financements et d’assistance techniques auprès des bailleurs
Le ministère chargé de mobilisation des ressources extérieures et de la gestion de la dette a prévu deux programmes pour ce projet de budget. Il s’agit du programme Pilotage et soutien aux services du MMG avec une dotation de 438,47 millions Fcfa soit 6,2% du budget du ministère avec pour objectifs d’optimiser le pilotage stratégique et la coordination des services du ministère, de moderniser les systèmes d’information et de gestion des connaissances du ministère et d’optimiser le processus de planification et de gestion des ressources du ministère. Le second programme est celui de la gestion des ressources de financement avec une dotation de 6,58 milliards Fcfa représentant 93,8% du budget du ministère. Il a pour objectifs de mobiliser de façon optimale les ressources extérieures pour le financement du développement, de promouvoir le Bénin comme un modèle de gestion transparente, innovant, proactive et diversifiée de la dette publique, de renforcer le suivi du portefeuille des programmes et projets et de renforcer la dette publique coopération technique et économique sectorielle avec les pays identifiés

items.title: Projet de loi de finances, gestion 2027 : Rodrigue Chaou défend 18,61 milliards Fcfa pour la fonction publique

original_payload.original_title: Projet de loi de finances, gestion 2027 : Rodrigue Chaou défend 18,61 milliards Fcfa pour la fonction publique
original_payload.original_body:
Karim Oscar ANONRIN
Le Ministre délégué chargé du Budget et de la Fonction publique, Monsieur Rodrigue S. CHAOU, a présenté ce mardi 17 novembre 2026, devant le Commission budgétaire de l’Assemblée nationale, le projet de budget de son département ministériel pour la gestion 2027. Ledit budget proposé s’élève à 18,61 milliards Fcfa en crédits de paiement, en hausse de 51,40 % par rapport à la loi de finances rectificative 2026. Il représente 0,39 % du projet de budget de l’État. Il s’agit d’un budget résolument tourné vers l’investissement. La hausse des crédits profite aux investissements du ministère. Les crédits de biens et services sont reconduits à l’identique, par souci de discipline budgétaire. L’investissement explique l’essentiel de l’augmentation et occupe désormais une place nettement plus importante dans le budget du ministère. Ces crédits d’investissement financent quatre projets structurants à savoir la construction du bâtiment de la Direction générale du Budget, pour les conditions de travail et la conservation des archives, mémoire budgétaire de l’État ; le projet de consolidation et d’accélération de la transformation numérique de l’administration publique (PCATNAP) ; le projet de pilotage de la performance et de modernisation de l’administration publique (P3MAP) ; et le projet de gouvernance budgétaire ouverte et de redevabilité.
Le projet de budget 2027 du ministère chargé du budget et de la fonction publique est assorti d’indicateurs de résultats soumis au contrôle des députés, parmi lesquels davantage de services publics dématérialisés de bout en bout ; une meilleure satisfaction des usagers des services concernés par le P3MAP ; une plus grande interopérabilité des systèmes d’information de l’administration ; l’ensemble des transferts aux communes répartis selon une formule officiellement approuvée, à travers le FIC. Au cours des échanges, le Ministre a apporté des éclaircissements sur plusieurs sujets d’intérêt public dont notamment recrutement sur titre des AME. Sur le sujet,  il ressort que le gouvernement a opté pour un recrutement sur titre, par vagues successives, après fiabilisation de la base de données des aspirants.  Il a été aussi question du dialogue social  avec la 4ème édition des élections professionnelles qui est en préparation. Le Gouvernement travaille à un cadre pluriannuel de planification et de traitement des doléances des travailleurs. Les députés se sont aussi intéressés à la simplification administrative. Là, le Ministre Rodrigue S. Chaou, a rassuré les députés en évoquant la dynamique engagée à travers le Prix national de la simplification administrative et sa plateforme dédiée, qui recense et valorise les initiatives d’allègement des procédures au profit des usagers. Enfin, il a été question de la réforme de l’avancement automatique. A ce sujet,  le Ministre a présenté l’économie de la réforme et son calendrier de mise en œuvre, en vue d’un déroulement de carrière des agents de l’État plus prévisible et plus équitable. Aussi, le Ministre Rodrigue S, Chaou, au nom du Gouvernement a  t-il annoncé d’autres réformes majeures pour 2027 aussi bien dans le domaine budgétaire que dans la gouvernance administrative. Il s’agit notamment de la relecture du code des pensions civiles et militaires de retraite, dans la continuité des réformes déjà engagées, afin d’assurer la soutenabilité du régime de retraite des agents de l’État et de sécuriser les droits des pensionnés ; la relecture du code de transparence dans la gestion des finances publiques, afin de renforcer l’accès des citoyens à l’information budgétaire et leur participation au processus budgétaire ; la relecture de la loi organique relative aux lois de finances, afin de consolider la gestion budgétaire axée sur les résultats et de l’adapter aux nouvelles exigences de la gestion des finances publiques ;
Le ministère chargé de mobilisation des ressources extérieures et de la gestion de la dette a prévu deux programmes pour ce projet de budget. Il s’agit du programme Pilotage et soutien aux services du MMG avec une dotation de 438,47 millions Fcfa soit 6,2% du budget du ministère avec pour objectifs d’optimiser le pilotage stratégique et la coordination des services du ministère, de moderniser les systèmes d’information et de gestion des connaissances du ministère et d’optimiser le processus de planification et de gestion des ressources du ministère. Le second programme est celui de la gestion des ressources de financement avec une dotation de 6,58 milliards Fcfa représentant 93,8% du budget du ministère. Il a pour objectifs de mobiliser de façon optimale les ressources extérieures pour le financement du développement, de promouvoir le Bénin comme un modèle de gestion transparente, innovant, proactive et diversifiée de la dette publique, de renforcer le suivi du portefeuille des programmes et projets et de renforcer la dette publique coopération technique et économique sectorielle avec les pays identifiés
