items.title: UPDATE- Party registration: Court grants AAP permission to enforce proceedings against INEC

original_payload.original_title: UPDATE- Party registration: Court grants AAP permission to enforce proceedings against INEC
original_payload.original_body:
Judiciary  UPDATE- Party registration: Court grants AAP permission to enforce proceedings against INEC
By  Funmilayo Adeyemi   ·   4 hours ago   ·  5 min read
✓
✓
By Taiye Agbaje
The Federal High Court in Abuja has granted the African Alliance Party (AAP) the go-ahead to begin enforcement of proceedings before it with respect to the judgment of the Court of Appeal.
The court of appeal had ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to register APP as a political party.
Justice Salim Ibrahim, in a ruling on Tuesday, held that the motion ex-parte filed by Mr Peters Olusegun on behalf of AAP and moved by their lawyer was meritorious.
“Having complied with the provisions of the law regarding enforcement of judgment, and having placed sufficient material before the court, this court finds this application meritorious, and this application is hereby granted.
“Consequently, leave is hereby granted to the judgment creditor/applicant to commence enforcement proceedings before this court with respect to the judgment of the Court of Appeal, Makurdi Judicial Division delivered on June 11 2026, in appeal no. CA/MK/102/26 between Peters Iyaobaje Olusegun (For APP) v. INEC & 2 Ors,” the judge ruled.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Olusegun had filed the suit as judgment creditor/applicant on behalf of AAP.
In the motion ex-parte dated and filed on Oct. 20, marked: FHC/ABJ/CS/2548/2026, the applicant sued INEC, its Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, and the Secretary, Dr Rose Oriarian-Anthony, as 1st to 3rd judgment debtors, respectively.
They sought an order granting leave to them to commence enforcement proceedings before the court with respect to the appellate court judgment, among other prayers.
In an affidavit in support of the motion ex-parte deposed to by Sylvia Nkemakosi, a member of the team of counsel representing the applicant, Olusegun said Justice Anyalewa Onoja-Alapa of the Federal High Court (FHC) in Lafia heard the original suit.
He stated that in the suit marked: FHC/LF/CS/3/2026, Justice Onoja-Alapa dismissed their case on April 14.
Dissatisfied with the judgment, Olusegun said they filed an appeal at Makurdi division of the Appeal Court and the appellate court gave its judgment on June 11, directing INEC to register AAP as a political party.
He said they wrote to notify the judgment debtor (INEC) of the judgment on June 15 and to which was attached a copy of the enrolled judgment order.
“The acknowledged copy of the letter of 15th June, 2026 and the enrolled judgment order are here attached as Exhibit MTE-2” he said.
Olusegun told the court that INEC, however, failed to comply with the judgment and instead, filed notices of appeal on July 8 and July 24 to the Supreme Court.
“On the back of this, they filed a motion for stay of execution at the Court of Appeal, but same was ultimately withdrawn on 13th August, 2026, in spite of the fact that the judgment debtors had still not entered an appeal at the Supreme Court.
“The applicants wrote to the judgment debtor again on that same Aug. 13, demanding compliance with the judgment of the Court of Appeal,” he said.
He said the Aug. 13 letter was attached as Exhibit MTE-3.
According to him, the judgment debtors did not dignify either Exhibit MTE-2 or MTE-3 with a response.
He said: “They ultimately served the applicant what purported to be a similar motion for stay at the Supreme Court bearing SC NO: SC/ML/296/2026.
“The said motion was thus purportedly listed in the Supreme Court for hearing along with other applications on Oct. 20.
“However, when the matter was called, it was discovered that the said motion was not filed in accordance with the Supreme Court (Mandatory Upload of Electronic Copies of Processes, Record of Appeal, and Other Matters) Practice Direction, 2026 and therefore the court did not countenance the motion.
“The court only heard the motion for leave to appeal in the proceedings in SC NO: SC/ML/296/ 2026 and despite finding the applications to be faulty, graciously granted leave to appeal and granted the judgment debtors (INEC) the indulgence to file a notice of appeal within 14 days.
“The judgment debtors had, in the meantime, proceeded and entered an appeal at the Supreme Court under SC NO: SC/CV/560/ 2026.
“It was also listed on 20th October, 2026 but in light of the proceedings in SC NO: SC/ML/296/2026, the Supreme Court struck out the appeal as it was entered on an incompetent notice of appeal.
“The ultimate effect is that as it stands now, the judgment debtors (INEC) do not have any appeal pending at the Supreme Court of Nigeria, neither have they secured any valid order staying execution of the judgment of the Court of Appeal in appeal no. CA/MK/102/26 which has been subsisting since 11th June, 2026 without compliance to date.”
Olusegun said that except INEC, its chairman and secretary are enforced, “they are unlikely to willingly comply with the judgment.”
“The net effect of all these delays is that the applicant will be denied the opportunity of participating in the 2027 general elections which seems to be the ultimate design of the judgment debtors (INEC).
“The intervention of this court is therefore necessary to ensure that the judgment is complied with,” he said.
Olusegun said it would be in the interest of justice to grant the motion ex-parte.(NAN)
Edited by Sadiya Hamza

items.title: Stakeholders seek reforms to strengthen criminal justice system

original_payload.original_title: Stakeholders seek reforms to strengthen criminal justice system
original_payload.original_body:
Judiciary  Stakeholders seek reforms to strengthen criminal justice system
By  Ismail Abdulaziz   ·   6 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
​‌⁠‍‍‌‍⁠⁠‍‍‍​‌‍‌
By Blessing Tanko/Ebere Agozie
Stakeholders have called for stronger institutional collaboration, sustained policy reforms and improved judicial preparedness to tackle emerging challenges confronting Nigeria’s criminal justice system.
‎They made the call at the 8th Annual Criminal Law Review Conference organised by the Rule of Law Development Foundation (ROLDF) on Monday in Abuja.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the theme of the five-day conference is `The Future of the Nigerian Criminal Justice System: Institutional Synergy, Policy Reforms and Judicial Readiness.”
Speaking at the event, the Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, identified delays in criminal proceedings, inadequate investigations and prolonged pretrial detentions as persistent challenges requiring practical solutions.
“The effectiveness of any criminal justice system depends on the quality of investigations, diligent prosecution, efficient courts and the capacity of correctional institutions.‎
‎‎“Hence, closer cooperation between investigators and prosecutors, particularly in complex cases, will help identify evidential gaps, improve case preparation and reduce avoidable delays.”
‎Fagbemi stressed that such cooperation must respect the constitutional and statutory responsibilities of the institutions, without compromising judicial independence or prosecutorial discretion.
He added that the administration of criminal justice remains one of the most important responsibilities of the State.
“It is through the criminal justice system that society seeks to hold offenders accountable, protect the innocent, safeguard individual rights and maintain public confidence in the rule of law.
“However, in spite of the progress recorded over the years, our system continues to grapple with familiar challenges, especially insufficient coordination among criminal justice institutions.
“These challenges are neither new nor peculiar to Nigeria. What matters is our willingness to confront them with practical and sustainable solutions.’’
‎He commended the founder and coordinator of the foundation, Chief Joseph Bodunrin Daudu, SAN, for sustaining the annual conference as a platform for engagement among criminal justice stakeholders.
‎Similarly, the President of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Mrs Oyinkansola Badejo-Okunsanya, SAN, ‎drew attention to critical human experiences within the justice system.
“These experiences range from victims seeking closure and defendants demanding fair hearings to the high percentage of inmates awaiting trial, and urged stakeholders to adopt actionable recommendations with clear implementation timelines.’’
‎She underscored the pressing challenges facing inmates of the Nigerian Correctional Services awaiting trial.
‎“Approximately 65 per cent of those in custody are awaiting trial, 53,670 are awaiting trial inmates out of a total custodial population of 82,195’’.
On judicial readiness, she stated that a judge’s readiness cannot compensate for poorly conducted investigations, absence of witnesses, incomplete prosecution files or defendants lacking competent representation.
She noted how victims, defendants, and persons in custody review the system through deeply personal questions about fairness and dignity.
She ‎applauded the foundation’s dedication to bridging the gap between legal principles and institutional practice.‎
‎The Coordinator of the ROLDF, Daudu, had earlier gave the assurance that the conference is designed to provide an annual forum for the review of all developments particularly novel developments in criminal justice administration.
“The discussions will address crime apprehension, crime prosecution, crime adjudication, and the important activities of the post adjudicatory processes and institutions of the criminal justice system, such as the Correctional Centres and Borstals.
“The foundation routinely considers the state of the existing laws governing the powers and functions of all relevant criminal justice institutions such as the Nigerian police and all other law enforcement agencies operating in Nigeria.
“It equally considers the law courts with criminal jurisdiction, the applicable criminal procedure and sentencing legislations and the role, state and efficacy of the correctional centres.”
He acknowledged the strenuous conditions under which courts perform their duties annually.(NAN)

items.title: Minister urges African countries to harmonise frameworks for recovering stolen funds

original_payload.original_title: Minister urges African countries to harmonise frameworks for recovering stolen funds
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Minister urges African countries to harmonise frameworks for recovering stolen funds
By  Abdulrahman Kadiri   ·   6 hours ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Isaac ​‌‍‌​⁠‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‌‌​‍‌‌‌​Aregbesola
The Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Mr Lateef Fagbemi, has urged African countries to harmonise frameworks for tracing, seizing and repatriating stolen public funds and other criminal proceeds stashed abroad.
Fagbemi gave the advice while declaring open the Maiden General Assembly of the African Asset Recovery Practitioners’ Forum (AARP-F) on Tuesday in Abuja.
The four-day assembly, themed “From Commitment to Action”, brought together delegates from all 55 Member States of the African Union, as well as international partners, under the auspices of the African Union.
Fagbemi urged the forum to develop a harmonised continental Standard Operating Procedure for asset tracing, freezing, seizure, confiscation, repatriation, management and disposal.
Such a framework, he said, must respect the domestic laws and sovereignty of Member States.
He said that such must still set common minimum standards, clear channels for timely mutual legal assistance, secure information-sharing protocols, and safeguards for due process and third-party rights.
“We should also strengthen beneficial ownership transparency, digital asset-tracing capabilities, professional training and independent reporting on the use of recovered assets.
“Our objective must be simple: to make cooperation faster, recovery more effective, and the management of recovered wealth more transparent and accountable to the African people,” he said.
Fagbemi said history would not judge the Assembly by the beauty of its declarations, but by the assets recovered, the obstacles removed and the difference made in the lives of the people.
He described illicit financial flows as eating away at the roots of Africa’s development, depriving the continent of resources that should educate children, equip hospitals, build infrastructure and secure the future.
The minister said asset recovery was not just tracing bank accounts or securing forfeiture orders, but a struggle for accountability, economic sovereignty and restoration of public trust.
He urged the Assembly to move the Forum from an interim body to a fully established, practitioner-led continental institution.
Fagbemi recalled that the Common African Position on Asset Recovery (CAPAR) was adopted on Feb. 10, 2020, to provide a unified framework for detecting assets, recovering and returning them, transparently managing them, and strengthening cooperation.
He said recovered assets must be protected against dissipation, mismanagement and re-entry into illicit channels, and that success should be measured not only by value recovered, but by transparency and developmental benefit to citizens.
The Independent Corrupt Practices Commission (ICPC) Chairman, Dr Musa Aliyu, SAN said the importance of asset recovery to Africa’s development could not be overstated, because every resource lost through corruption represented an opportunity denied to the people.
According to him,  every asset stolen from Africa is not just money lost, but a school not built, a hospital not equipped and a job not created.
“Resources that could otherwise support education, healthcare, infrastructure, security, employment and other essential public services are lost when assets are stolen and hidden abroad.”
He said behind every successfully recovered asset lies an opportunity to restore public value, strengthen institutions, advance justice and rebuild confidence in governance.
Aliyu, who is also Chairman of the Interim Steering Council of AARP-F, said asset recovery must be understood not merely as enforcement or financial investigation.
According to him, it must be understood , as an essential instrument of accountability, national development and protection of public resources.
“The responsibility of practitioners does not end with identifying and recovering stolen assets, but by ensuring that recovered proceeds are returned and managed in accordance with law, so they can serve the public interest,” he said.
The Head of Development Cooperation at the German Embassy, Dr Karen Jansen, expressed concern over the enormous resources Africa continues to lose through illicit financial flows.
She said recovery of these resources was imperative for financing development, improving citizens’ welfare and restoring public confidence in governance.
Hon Kwami Senanu, the Chairperson of the African Union Advisory Board Against Corruption (AUABC), said the successful commencement of the First General Assembly demonstrated what Africa could achieve through unity, shared responsibility and cooperation.
Senanu commended Nigeria for its support and consistent championing of the Common African Position on Asset Recovery (CAPAR), calling for existing commitments to be consolidated through practical actions and stronger institutional engagement.
Also, Amb. Bankole Adeoye, the Head of the Political Affairs, Peace and Security Department of the African Union Commission, said the initiative was designed to move Africa’s asset recovery commitments beyond policy declarations to tangible actions and measurable results.
Adeoye was represented by Mr Isiaka Garba, an officer in the commission,  ( NAN ) www.nannews.ng

items.title: State Police: Poorly defined boundaries, political interference a challenges– Senior lawyer

original_payload.original_title: State Police: Poorly defined boundaries, political interference a challenges– Senior lawyer
original_payload.original_body:
Judiciary  State Police: Poorly defined boundaries, political interference a challenges– Senior lawyer
By  Ismail Abdulaziz   ·   6 hours ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
⁠By Ebere Agozie
JB Daudu, the Coordinator of the Rule of Law Development Foundation (ROLDF) has warned that poorly defined boundaries and political interference could spark institutional challenges in the operation of state police.
Daudu gave the warning at the ongoing five day 8th annual Criminal Law Review conference and book launch of Volume II of his book `JB Daudu SAN Through the Cases’ on Tuesday in Abuja.
He, therefore, called for the establishment of a workable multi-policing system before the establishment of the State Police Service across the nation.
He warned that when the amendments come into law, the journey to a firm, workable dual or multi-policing system would have just commenced in Nigeria.
“The existence of legislation that permits states to participate in the policing of their territories does not automatically mean that there would be a ready-made sound security architecture to take up the gauntlet.
“A clear example of slow previous efforts by states to jump onto the bandwagon of progress anticipated by constitution alteration is the 5th amendment.
“The 5th amendment allows the states to approach the issue of electricity and Correctional Centres as items on the concurrent legislative list.
“All available evidence show that in the earlier item, electricity, only a few states have taken up the challenge, while no state has yet set up its own correctional centre,’’ he noted.
The senior lawyer said that the state police establishment would require at least five years from now to set a solid foundation for its emergence and effective delivery.
He noted that the infrastructure required by the 36 states to set up police stations in communities, districts, Local Government Headquarters and state capital would be enormous.
“It will not be tolerable for the federal and state police to operate out of the same premises at any point in time.
“This venture requires the ascertainment of the scope and volume of communication gadgets and armoury that will be required to set up the new security architecture.’’
He advised that the training and kitting of state police for each of the 36 states must be uniform for a harmonised effective policing.
“It will be complicated to have a situation where state A seeks to import its munitions and other police gadgets from, by way of example, Russia, whilst state B brings in its policing equipment from China and state C decides to manufacture its own requirement in Nigeria.
“This will introduce into the entire system a cacophony of allegiances and needless bonds that will otherwise introduce additional corruption, tension and strain into the system.’’
Daudu added that the biggest problem for state police would emerge from demarcating the jurisdiction of the existing federal police and the jurisdiction of the newly introduced state police.
“What will be the territorial or indeed subject matter jurisdiction of the state Police? The latter should not be able to interrogate or investigate or prosecute Federal offences.
“In the event that there is a hot pursuit of criminals within the boundaries of state A and the criminals flee into state B, will the state police of A have the power and the capacity to pursue those criminals into the territory of state B?
“These and other serious matters of jurisdiction must be ironed out by the respective Houses of Assembly before the inauguration of even one State police,’’ he advised.
The learned silk also advised that a statute should set out the minimum educational limit and entry point into either the states or federal police as being a graduate from a recognised university.
The best way to demarcate their respective operational jurisdictions, he said, was to ensure that their standards of training and the literacy level of their officers is the same and at the highest at all times.
”It must be settled right from the get-go that matters relating to insecurity is not the primary purpose or feature of a state police’’.
“The primary objective of state police should be to maintain law and order within the territory of that state.
“It is submitted that in the foreseeable future grave matters of insecurity such as terrorism, kidnapping, drug trafficking, banditry, illegal mining, cultism etcetera should be left with the federal police.
“The federal police apparently have a database for the monitoring and all policing of such species of organised crime’’.(NAN)
Edited by Sadiya Hamza

items.title: FG inaugurates CNG stations in four university campuses

original_payload.original_title: FG inaugurates CNG stations in four university campuses
original_payload.original_body:
Oil & Gas  FG inaugurates CNG stations in four university campuses
By  Folasade Akpan   ·   6 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Isaiah Eka
The Federal Government has inaugurated Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) stations to boost transportation in four university campuses in the country.
The stations were inaugurated on Tuesday by the Minister of Petroleum Resources, Gas, Mr Ekperikpe Ekpo.
The benefiting universities are: University of Uyo, University of Calabar, University of Nigeria, Enugu Campus, and Federal University of Petroleum Resources, Effurun.
In his remarks, Ekpo said that establishing the four stations within university communities was a practical demonstration of President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda.
He said that the stations represented a significant milestone in the efforts to translate Nigeria’s abundant natural gas resources into tangible economic and social benefits.
The minister said that Nigeria was endowed with over 215 trillion cubic feet of proven natural gas reserves.
He further said that the nation’s responsibility was to translate the resource into improved livelihoods, industrial development, employment opportunities and greater energy access.
Ekpo said that the gas stations would provide students, lecturers, university staff and surrounding communities with access to a cleaner and potentially more economical transportation alternative.
“Beyond transportation, these facilities offer an opportunity to deepen awareness of natural gas and its importance to Nigeria’s energy future,” he said.
The minister described universities as critical centres of research, innovation and technical skills development.
He said that their participation in the CNG ecosystem would nurture the next generation of engineers, technicians, entrepreneurs and energy professionals.
Ekpo urged the management of the benefiting institutions to explore partnerships with industry stakeholders in research, technical training, and the development of local expertise in CNG technologies.
In his remarks, the Executive Director, Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund, Mr Oluwole Adama, said that the stations were established in partnership with FEMADEC Energy Limited.
He said that the collaborations showed that greater progress could be achieved with strong stakeholder collaboration.
Adama said that the mobile integrated unit with a storage capacity of 8,100 standard cubic metres of gas could fill about 540 vehicles daily.
He said that the CNG stations were an infrastructure investment creating the conditions for academic growth and future careers.
The Executive director stated that gas infrastructure could reduce operating costs, improve the movement of people and goods, attract private investment.
“It can also create work across construction, operations and technical service sectors,” he said.
Mr Fola Akinnola, the Chief Executive Officer, FEDAMEC Energy Limited, said that gas infrastructure would directly address the commuting challenges faced by the university communities.
Akinnola said that clean, reliable, and significantly cheaper energy was no longer a distant promise but a reality on campuses.
“A milestone of this scale is only possible through the power of deliberate and high-impact collaboration,” he said.
He said that beyond fuel dispensing, the CNG stations would create living laboratories for engineering and energy students to witness clean gas technology in action.
The Vice Chancellor, University of Uyo, Prof. Christopher Ekong, thanked the Federal Government for inaugurating the gas station, and described the gesture as timely.
Ekong assured that the infrastructure would be safeguarded by the university community. (NAN)
Edited by Azubuike Okeh

items.title: Trachoma: Nigeria cuts at-risk population from 41m to under 5m ​‌‌‌​‍‌‍⁠⁠‍‍‍​⁠⁠⁠​​‌​

original_payload.original_title: Trachoma: Nigeria cuts at-risk population from 41m to under 5m ​‌‌‌​‍‌‍⁠⁠‍‍‍​⁠⁠⁠​​‌​
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Trachoma: Nigeria cuts at-risk population from 41m to under 5m  ​‌‌‌​‍‌‍⁠⁠‍‍‍​⁠⁠⁠​​‌​
By  Abdulrahman Kadiri   ·   7 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Justina Auta
Nigeria has reduced the population at risk of trachoma-induced blindness from 41 million to fewer than five million, recording 88 per cent progress in its elimination efforts.
Dr Nicholas Olobio, Director of the Trachoma Programme, said this on Tuesday in Abuja at a two-day Trachoma Annual Project Performance Review (APPR) meeting.
The meeting was organised by the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Sightsavers Nigeria and other partners to assess programme implementation and progress towards elimination.
Olobio said Nigeria had made significant progress since trachoma was mapped across 134 endemic Local Government Areas (LGAs).
“Right from inception, we had 134 LGAs that were endemic for the disease, but it is now down to about 16 LGAs where we are treating,” he said.
He explained that 118 LGAs had stopped Mass Drug Administration (MDA), representing about 88 per cent achievement in the elimination drive.
“After 16 LGAs, we will see how it goes from there. It shows the progress the programme has made,” Olobio said.
He said that states including Kano had reached elimination thresholds, while Katsina, Sokoto, Ebonyi and Edo were making significant progress.
Olobio said only Borno and Yobe remained active states where MDA was ongoing, adding that insecurity posed challenges to implementation.
“Borno has been very difficult, but we found ways. For Yobe, we still need to use another strategy,” he said.
He added that sustaining the gains required a stronger focus on Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) interventions.
“Without the environmental aspect, you cannot eliminate the disease,” he said.
Olobio emphasised that the Surgery, Antibiotics, Facial Cleanliness and Environmental improvement (SAFE) strategy remained central to the elimination effort.
He urged communities to adopt simple hygiene practices, including regular face washing and handwashing after using toilets.
“The fly perches on the faces of people, especially women and children. We need to sensitise people to wash their faces,” he said.
Mr Adebayo Peters, Neglected Tropical Diseases (NTD) Coordinator, Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, said elimination required sustained commitment and collaboration among stakeholders.
“The implementation of the SAFE strategy remains central to our national response,” he said.
Peters said progress depended on collaboration among government institutions, development partners, communities and implementing organisations.
He added that the Federal Government was strengthening state ownership and domestic financing for NTD interventions.
He said the ministry was working with relevant sectors, including education, environment, water resources and sanitation, to promote coordinated responses.
“WASH and social behaviour change communication campaigns are critical to sustaining the gains already made,” he said.
Dr Teyil Wamyil-Mshelia, Country Trachoma Coordinator, Sightsavers Nigeria, said improved sanitation would help reduce disease transmission.
“When we strengthen collaboration, we jointly plan to reach areas with poor water resources and sanitation,” she said.
Wamyil-Mshelia explained that contaminated faces, fingers and fomites could contribute to trachoma transmission through flies.
She said maintaining partnerships would help prevent the disease from returning after elimination.
Adeyemo Joseph, Assistant Director, WASH Tracking and Documentation, Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation, reaffirmed the ministry’s commitment to environmental health.
“We remain committed to strengthening intersectoral collaboration, particularly in WASH, which is critical to achieving this goal,” he said.
Mrs Ada Ofemens, Principal Environmental Health Officer, Federal Ministry of Environment, also pledged continued support for the elimination efforts.
She said environmental health and WASH remained essential components of Nigeria’s trachoma elimination programme.
The APPR meeting reviewed state-level progress, identified implementation gaps and developed strategies to accelerate the country’s elimination target.(NAN)
Edited by Abiemwense Moru

items.title: Partners seek more funding, collaboration to end open defecation by 2030

original_payload.original_title: Partners seek more funding, collaboration to end open defecation by 2030
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Partners seek more funding, collaboration to end open defecation by 2030
By  Abdulrahman Kadiri   ·   7 hours ago   ·  2 min read
✓
✓
By Justina Auta
Development partners on Tuesday called for increased funding, stronger collaboration and sustained community participation to make Nigeria open defecation-free (ODF) by 2030.
Representatives of UNICEF, the World Health Organisation (WHO), Sightsavers Nigeria, and other partners made the call at the fourth National Sanitation Retreat in Abuja.
The Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation organised the retreat with development partners to accelerate progress on sanitation.
Ms Jolly Ann Maulit, UNICEF Nigeria’s Public Health and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Leader, said 184 of the country’s 774 local government areas (LGAs) had attained ODF status.
She said Jigawa and Katsina were the first states to reach the milestone, even though about 48 million Nigerians still practised open defecation.
“We need to ensure proper use and maintenance of toilets and integrate sanitation into government policies and budgets,” she said.
Maulit also stressed the need to prevent ODF communities from relapsing.
Dr Edwin Isotu-Edeh, WHO National Technical Officer, Public Health and Environment, described open defecation as a major public health concern that has raised the risk of cholera and other diseases, particularly in vulnerable communities.
He said sanitation should become a culture, not an occasional activity.
“Despite widespread awareness of handwashing, only four per cent of the population consistently practise it,” he said.
Isotu-Edeh urged the integration of hand hygiene into the Clean Nigeria Campaign and said about four trillion naira was needed to sustain sanitation efforts.
Dr Teyil Wamyil-Mshelia, Sightsavers Nigeria’s Country Trachoma Coordinator, said the organisation was working closely with the water resources, environment, education and information sectors to promote behaviour change.
“We can’t work alone. We believe in collaboration and putting resources together because when we put our hands together, we go further,” she said.
Mrs Joy Aderele, Country Director of Self Help Africa, urged stakeholders to strengthen community mobilisation and monitoring to prevent setbacks.
She added that achieving an open defecation-free Nigeria by 2030 will require shared responsibility and commitment from all stakeholders. (NAN)
Edited by Emmanuel Yashim

items.title: UPDATED: Fountain of Life Church faces leadership crisis as board suspends Jimmy Odukoya

original_payload.original_title: UPDATED: Fountain of Life Church faces leadership crisis as board suspends Jimmy Odukoya
original_payload.original_body:
A LEADERSHIP crisis has erupted at The Fountain of Life Church in Lagos following the emergence of conflicting statements from the church’s Board of Trustees and another faction aligned with the church’s leadership under its Senior Pastor, Jimmy Odukoya.
While the Board of Trustees announced Odukoya’s removal as the church’s senior pastor, the pastor’s camp has rejected the decision, insisting that he remains in office.
In a  report  announcing his removal, the Board of Trustees said it had resolved to terminate Odukoya’s recognition as senior pastor following a review of a video recording containing what it described as the succession instructions of the late founder, Taiwo Odukoya.
The Board said the recording, made in December 2021 at the late pastor’s request, showed that the founder had designated another person as his successor while assigning Odukoya the roles of administrative assistant to the successor and head of the youth church. The arrangements, it said, were to take effect upon the founder’s death or inability to communicate.
The Board said the embattled pastor recorded the video at his father’s request but that it was not made available when it initially sought clarification about the founder’s succession plans.

items.title: École nationale de Police : Djibril MAMA CISSÉ à l'écoute des apprenants et des formateurs

original_payload.original_title: École nationale de Police : Djibril MAMA CISSÉ à l'écoute des apprenants et des formateurs
original_payload.original_body:
Le Ministre de l’Intérieur et de la Sécurité publique, Monsieur Djibril MAMA CISSÉ, a effectué, ce mardi 17 novembre 2026, une visite à l’École nationale des brigadiers et agents de Police à Porto-Novo. L’objectif de ce déplacement était de s’enquérir des conditions réelles de travail des apprenants et des formateurs, ainsi que de recueillir leurs doléances en vue d’une amélioration substantielle.
Revue des troupes, visite des locaux et séance d’échanges : tel était le programme de cette sortie, effectuée en compagnie du secrétaire général du ministère et de conseillers techniques à la sécurité. Face à l’autorité, les responsables des différentes structures abritées sur le site ont tour à tour présenté les cursus dispensés ainsi que les difficultés rencontrées au quotidien.
S’agissant des formations, le centre accueille actuellement la formation professionnelle de 714 agents de Police. Des stages statutaires sont également en cours pour les stagiaires de l’École nationale supérieure de la Police et du Centre de perfectionnement de police judiciaire. Toutefois, pour garantir une formation de qualité, les responsables ont attiré l’attention du ministre et du directeur général de la Police républicaine sur plusieurs défis majeurs : le déficit de personnel, l’état des infrastructures d’accueil, l’adaptation du cadre légal et la mobilité des apprenants.
Face à ces préoccupations, le Ministre Djibril MAMA CISSÉ  a salué l’engagement de tous les acteurs avant de réaffirmer la détermination du gouvernement à former des fonctionnaires de police qualifiés pour une meilleure protection des personnes et des biens. « Je prends la mesure de tous ces défis », a-t-il déclaré devant un auditoire composé de fonctionnaires de police de tous grades. Il a ainsi promis d’œuvrer à l’amélioration des conditions d’apprentissage et de s’employer à lever, dans les plus brefs délais, les goulots d’étranglement internes qui entravent le bon déroulement des formations.

items.title: Dépistage précoce du cancer du sein: L’AEB sensibilise les communautés de Djakotomey et d’Abomey-Calavi

original_payload.original_title: Dépistage précoce du cancer du sein: L’AEB sensibilise les communautés de Djakotomey et d’Abomey-Calavi
original_payload.original_body:
Dans le cadre de la campagne internationale Octobre Rose, l’Association des Énarques du Bénin (AEB) a organisé plusieurs activités de sensibilisation, de dépistage et de mobilisation communautaire. Initiative menée tout au long du mois d’octobre 2026, l’objectif poursuivi a été de promouvoir le dépistage précoce et renforcer la sensibilisation des femmes et des filles sur le cancer du sein. Elle a reçu l’appui de plusieurs partenaires notamment Conscience Féminine.
Deux grandes activités ! Deux dates ! Top départ dans une seule ville : Djakotomey ! Les activités s’y sont tenues les 9 et 10 octobre. En premier lieu, une séance de dépistage à l’Hôpital APH de Gohomey. Le jour suivant a eu lieu la grande marche rose démarrée à l’Hôpital APH et à l’usine de coton de Hagoumey. Cette première phase a été rythmée par des conférences, des échanges, des animations et un parcours santé. La seconde phase du programme a été exécutée dans la commune d’Abomey-Calavi, à l’École Nationale d’Administration (ENA). Elle a connu une deuxième séance de dépistage organisée le mercredi 28 octobre.
Elle a été suivie d’une grande marche rose le samedi 31 octobre 2026, débutée à l’esplanade de l’ENA. Ces dernières activités ont permis d’aller davantage à la rencontre de la population estudiantine et celle des environs du campus. Elles ont rappelé l’importance de l’autopalpation, de la consultation médicale et du dépistage régulier. Au total, près de 500 femmes et filles ont bénéficié des séances de dépistage organisées dans le cadre de cette campagne. Les différentes activités ont reçu un accueil favorable de la part des participantes et des bénéficiaires, témoignant de l’intérêt suscité par cette initiative.
À travers cette mobilisation, l’Association des Énarques du Bénin réaffirme son engagement citoyen et sa volonté de contribuer à la promotion de la santé féminine. Au-delà, le message demeure essentiel : le dépistage précoce sauve des vies et la lutte contre le cancer du sein relèvent de la responsabilité collective.

items.title: Sénégal : Bassirou Diomaye Faye exclu du PASTEF avec une trentaine de personnalités

original_payload.original_title: Sénégal : Bassirou Diomaye Faye exclu du PASTEF avec une trentaine de personnalités
original_payload.original_body:
L’exclusion de Bassirou Diomaye Faye du PASTEF marque un nouvel épisode dans les tensions internes au parti sénégalais. Réuni le mardi 17 novembre 2026, le Conseil national a constaté la perte automatique de la qualité de membres de 32 personnalités, dont le président de la République.
Le PASTEF-Les Patriotes a pris une décision aux conséquences politiques importantes. Son Conseil national a constaté la perte de la qualité de membres de plusieurs personnalités. Parmi elles figure le président sénégalais Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye.
Dans un communiqué référencé C N°02/PASTEF/CN/2026, l’instance annonce cette mesure. Elle s’appuie sur les dispositions de l’article 6 des statuts du parti. Le Conseil national a examiné cette question lors de sa réunion du mardi 17 novembre 2026.
Au total, 32 personnalités figurent sur la liste publiée par le parti. Outre Bassirou Diomaye Faye, cette liste comprend Kéba Ndiaye, Abib Diop, Cheikh Saad Bouh Diouf, Ndeye Fatou Modji, Alassane Guèye et Seni Diène.
Elle mentionne également Babacar Touré, Sokhna Ciss, Alioune Dione, Marie Angélique Mame Selbé Diouf, Ndeye Marième Samb et Moussa Balla Fofana. Thierno Alia Mbengue, Ousmane Abdoulaye Barro et Serigne Abdoul Ahad Ndiaye figurent aussi parmi les personnes concernées.
La seconde partie de la liste cite Bakary Sakho, Aldiouma Sow, Félicité Mbogane Sarr, Atoumane Sy et Yankhoba Diémé. On y retrouve également Lamine Niang, Bacary Sarr, Awa Ndoye, Maimouna Dia et Abdourakhmane Dabo.
Enfin, le document mentionne Ibrahima Sy, Fatou Kiné Diakhaté, Sokhna Diagne Badji, Diamé Signaté, Idy Watt et Rougui Sow.
Le Conseil national invoque les statuts du parti
Pour justifier sa décision, le Conseil national se réfère directement à l’article 6 des statuts de PASTEF-Les Patriotes. Le communiqué précise que les personnes concernées perdent automatiquement leur qualité de membres.
En conséquence, l’instance annonce leur radiation définitive de la liste des membres du parti. Elle formule clairement cette décision dans la dernière partie du document.
Bassirou Diomaye Faye au cœur d’une décision politique majeure
La présence de Bassirou Diomaye Faye sur cette liste donne une portée particulière à cette annonce. Élu président de la République en mars 2024, il avait accédé au pouvoir sous la bannière du PASTEF.
Cette décision intervient dans un contexte de tensions entre le chef de l’État et Ousmane Sonko. Ce dernier demeure une figure centrale de la formation politique.
Dès lors, la décision du Conseil national soulève des interrogations sur les rapports entre les deux hommes. Elle pose également la question de l’avenir des relations entre le président de la République et son ancienne formation politique.

items.title: Étude en commission du Projet de loi de finances, gestion 2027 : le Ministre Nicolas Yènoussi a parlé de 36,813 milliards Fcfa pour le MFM

original_payload.original_title: Étude en commission du Projet de loi de finances, gestion 2027 : le Ministre Nicolas Yènoussi a parlé de 36,813 milliards Fcfa pour le MFM
original_payload.original_body:
Karim Oscar ANONRIN
Le Ministre délégué auprès du Ministre de l’Economie et des Finances, chargé des finances et de la microfinance, Nicolas Yènoussi, a présenté ce mardi 17 novembre 2026, le projet de budget de son département ministériel à la Commission budgétaire de l’Assemblée nationale dans le cadre de l’étude en commission du Projet de loinde finances,  gestion 2027. Il s’agit d’un projet de budget en hausse de 15% avec un crédit de 36,813 milliards Fcfa portée essentiellement par les dépenses en capital. Il est reparti en dépenses ordinaires prenant en compte les dépenses du personnel à hauteur de 14.826.051.000Fcfa , les dépenses d’acquisitions de biens er services à hauteur de 6.204.226.000Fcfa, les transferts courants  à hauteur de 10.073.694.000 Fcfa et en dépenses en capital estimées à 5.710.000.000 Fcfa.
Ce projet de budget est orienté vers trois programmes au titre de l’année 2027. Il s’agit du programme Pilotage et soutien aux services du ministère. A ce niveau,  il s’agira d’optimiser le pilotage stratégique et la coordination des services du ministère,  moderniser les systèmes d’informations et de gestion des connaissances du ministère et optimiser les processus de planification et de gestion des ressources du ministère. Le 2 ème  programme est celui relatif à la Mobilisation des ressources intérieures et la gestion de la trésorerie de l’Etat. Là, le gouvernement à travers ce département ministériel entend améliorer la performance de l’administration des impôts,  améliorer la performance de l’administration des douanes, améliorer la performance de l’administration du trésor et la gestion de la trésorerie, optimiser la gestion du patrimoine foncier et des recettes domaniales et garantir l’intégrité des règles financières et la conformité du secteur des jeux. Le troisième programme est celui du Développement du secteur financier et l’inclusion financière. A ce niveau, le gouvernement ambitionne de renforcer la stabilité, la transparence et l’intégrité de l’écosystème financier national, accélérer l’inclusion financière et la transformation digitale des services financiers, faciliter l’accès aux financements de proximité et consolider la microfinance, améliorer la qualité des services financiers et la protection des usagers

items.title: US Fed’s Lisa Cook refuses to attend White House hearing

original_payload.original_title: US Fed’s Lisa Cook refuses to attend White House hearing
original_payload.original_body:
United States Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook has declined, through her lawyers, to appear next month before a Trump administration committee that is considering whether she should be fired, calling the process unfair and committed to a predetermined outcome.
The refusal extends the wrangling between the White House and Cook’s lawyers regarding her appearance before the committee, which the administration of US President Donald Trump initially demanded for November 6.
Recommended Stories

Administration officials have called on Cook to appear before the committee to address allegations that she committed mortgage fraud in 2021, before she joined the Fed’s board of governors, a charge she denies. Cook has not been charged with any crime.
Trump has sought to fire Cook since August 2025, and she has argued that the president’s efforts to do so represent a threat to the Fed’s independence and reflect Trump’s desire to force the central bank to reduce borrowing costs.
“Governor Cook has no legal obligation to participate in an unfair hearing — and indeed, has a duty to the Federal Reserve to decline to participate in any proceeding that would undermine the institution’s unique status and independence,” Abbe David Lowell, Cook’s lawyer, wrote in a letter released on Tuesday to White House counsel William Scharf. The three-person panel set up by the White House to consider the allegations “appears to be a facade designed to obscure a predetermined decision to fire Governor Cook”, the letter said.
In June, the US Supreme Court blocked Trump from removing Cook while litigation over the attempted firing continues, finding that “the fact of independence but also the appearance of independence is key to the Federal Reserve’s design”.

items.title: ‘Zero transparency’: Inside Trump’s plans for Venezuela’s oil money

original_payload.original_title: ‘Zero transparency’: Inside Trump’s plans for Venezuela’s oil money
original_payload.original_body:
The administration of United States President Donald Trump is facing criticism over how it has handled billions of dollars in oil revenue collected from Venezuela.
Since January 3, Trump’s government has controlled Venezuela’s oil exports, gathering the revenue in an account overseen exclusively by the US Treasury.
Recommended Stories

list 2 of 3  Venezuela’s Machado lauds Trump for ‘freedom’, urges 2027 elections

Last week, the Department of State released a 53-page report aimed at shedding light on the account’s activities. It revealed that at least $12.11bn have passed through the account since the start of the year.
But critics say the report lacks key details about where the money came from and who it is going to.
“There’s been zero transparency on all of the financial engineering associated with how $12bn of Venezuelan oil was changing hands and being utilised,” said Tyson Slocum, the director of the energy programme at Public Citizen, a US-based consumer advocacy nonprofit.
“All we have now is a very barebones narrative of how the funds were used, but not details on what entities were involved.”
Questions of sovereignty
Concerns about Trump’s plans for Venezuela’s oil sector began late last year, when his government began seizing oil tankers leaving the South American country.
Any oil on board, Trump said, would be kept or sold by the US. He and members of his administration framed the confiscated fuel as compensation for the losses incurred when Venezuela nationalised its oil industry decades ago.
“American sweat, ingenuity and toil created the oil industry in Venezuela,” White House aide Stephen Miller said at the time. “Its tyrannical expropriation was the largest recorded theft of American wealth and property.”

items.title: Whistleblower: Deadly drone strike in Kuwait could’ve been avoided

original_payload.original_title: Whistleblower: Deadly drone strike in Kuwait could’ve been avoided
original_payload.original_body:
Washington, DC  – An American soldier wounded in a deadly Iranian drone attack in Kuwait is accusing senior military officials of ignoring warnings and being ill-equipped ahead of launching the US-Israel war on Iran, according to a whistleblower complaint.
The complaint, obtained by Al Jazeera English on Tuesday, is tied to an Iranian one-way attack drone that evaded air defences at the outpost within the first 48 hours of the war. Six service members were killed, and dozens were injured, including the whistleblower. It remains the deadliest assault on US forces since the war commenced.
Recommended Stories

The 14-page letter, submitted on Friday to the House and Senate Armed Services committees, alleges that the army repeatedly brushed aside warnings that the Port of Shuaiba in Kuwait was vulnerable to drone attacks. Though the site was fortified, there was no roof.
“The drone threat to the port was raised directly to the commanding general of the 1st Theater Sustainment Command at least three times in the week before hostilities,” the complaint states.
“Each warning was dismissed.”
The soldier, who is not named, also alleges the installation had “no physician, no fixed aid station, and only one ambulance”, adding that at least one of those killed “could have survived” if there was adequate medical support on site.
The army says it has completed its investigation of the Port of Shuaiba attack but has not publicly released its findings.
In a news conference following the incident, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth described the drone as a “squirter” that “happened to hit a tactical operations centre that was fortified”.

items.title: Tensions rise over draft climate deal at COP31

original_payload.original_title: Tensions rise over draft climate deal at COP31
original_payload.original_body:
A contentious draft deal has laid bare divisions between delegates from states participating in this year’s United Nations climate COP31 talks in Turkiye.
The 18-page draft “cover decision” published by summit cohost Australia on Monday includes a broad range of demands, including calls for a phaseout of fossil fuels.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items    list 1 of 3  Turkiye pushes electrification top of climate agenda as COP31 set to open
list 2 of 3  Which countries and industries emit the most greenhouse gases?
list 3 of 3  COP31 opens amid energy crisis as activists demand climate action
end of list
The draft, as written, could make the negotiations “untenable”, said Wopke Hoekstra, the European Union’s climate envoy, adding that “the cover decision does not go in the right direction and needs significant change”.
“It’s very easy to draw red lines at the start of the process,” said Joao Paulo Capobianco, Brazil’s environment minister, adding that deadlocks can be overcome through “an adjustment in the wording” in the draft.
Australian Climate Minister Chris Bowen, who is steering COP31 negotiations, acknowledged that the text included elements “that not all parties agree on”, and that there might be “at least one more draft” introduced before the end of the week.
The talks are scheduled to end on Friday, but climate negotiations usually run into overtime as agreements must be reached by consensus, meaning even a single country can block the entire process.
The draft text includes a call for wealthy nations to achieve net zero emissions by 2030, and wording on phasing out fossil fuels that oil-rich countries have long resisted.
Consensus on the issue of net zero emissions at COP31 “might be very, very difficult”, said Michael Joseph, the environment minister of the island state of Antigua and Barbuda, adding that he “would love to see a commitment that calls on the phasing out of fossil fuels”.

The teleprompter operator, Gabriel Perez, received a three-year ban from the platform and was required to pay $65,000 in penalties, as well as relinquish his $107,000 in winnings to the CFTC. By August, the CFTC had begun an internal review of prediction markets, according to CNBC.
The move comes amid a new wave of scrutiny of prediction market platforms by the CFTC. That marks a shift from the stance of Chair Michael Selig, who had previously championed the emerging industry, but has now adopted a tougher tone, launching investigations into Kalshi and its competitor Polymarket, which is not regulated by the commission.
Kalshi, in particular, had been under investigation for developing new products without notifying the commission, according to a report by Politico earlier this month.
The development also comes as Donald Trump Jr, the president’s eldest son, stepped down from his role as a paid strategic adviser to the company last week.

Meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen on Tuesday, Carney and Chinese President Xi Jinping announced new tariff remissions, building on  an agreement they made in January  to open up trade and start to repair a strained diplomatic relationship.

Canada, in exchange, will keep tariff exemptions for certain Chinese steel and aluminium products in place for another two years, and add remissions to another 32 steel and aluminium items that Canada doesn’t have enough of.
Xi said stronger ties served both countries’ interests and supported global stability and prosperity.
“This is the right choice,” he said.
Carney praised the greater predictability in the relationship and said Canada was ahead of schedule on its goal of increasing exports to China by 50 percent by the end of the decade.
Under the January agreement, Canada lowered its 100 percent tariff on Chinese electric vehicles to 6.1 percent, allowing an initial 49,000 vehicles into the country each year. That cap is set to rise to 70,000 over five years.

France’s 5.8 million public sector employees were pushed to mobilise after talks with Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu on Friday failed to satisfy union demands. Tuesday’s rally is the third call for a united day of action and strikes in the public sector since September.
Unions have been pushing for across-the-board pay rises since last week’s boost to the minimum wage for private-sector workers.
Protesters say “they simply can’t make ends meet, and they want the government to help them put more money into funding in terms of salaries, in terms of raising the minimum wage”, Al Jazeera’s Natacha Butler reported from Paris.
“The government’s already offered about $30 extra a month on the minimum wage, but those here say that is simply not enough. With inflation, with the way the prices are going up, they say they actually need more.”
The unions put the loss of purchasing power for public servants at 16 percent since 2017, leading to increasing numbers of public employees ending up on or close to the minimum wage against a backdrop of inflation.

Cobalt, coltan, manganèse… L'Afrique centrale possède d'importantes réserves de ces minerais critiques devenus essentiels  à la transition énergétique, au numérique ou encore à la Défense. Les pays comme le Tchad et la RDC , se retrouvent donc en première ligne des intérêts géostratégiques .  Mais derrière cette richesse se développe une autre réalité : trafics, corruption et réseaux criminels.C'est ce qu'indique ce nouveau rapport de la Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime. Zobel Behalal, co-auteur de ce rapport, est notre invité.
Un drame secoue le Gabon : un enfant de 12 ans, Dylan, a été blessé par balles vendredi dans un stade de Libreville. Le tireur présumé n'est autre qu'un ancien ministre et général à la retraite, Jean Boniface Assélé, âgé de 87 ans. L'affaire suscite une immense émotion et des appels à la justice pour le jeune garçon. Le  parquet doit se prononcer sur les circonstances exactes de cette fusillade. Notre correspondant au Gabon, Ismaël Obiang Nze, s'est rendu ce matin à l'hôpital où Dylan est soigné.
original_payload.original_summary: L'élection du secrétaire général de l'Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF), au coeur d'un bras de fer entre République démocratique du Congo et Rwanda, a été reportée d'un an lundi faute de consensus, un "compromis" diversement accueilli. La sortante rwandaise Louise Mushikiwabo, qui a dénoncé des "pressions nombreuses et fortes" à son encontre, restera en place jusqu'à la tenue du nouveau scrutin, auquel le Rwanda ne présentera pas de candidat.

items.title: Koumra : le CLAC met les élèves à l’épreuve de la lecture et de la dictée

original_payload.original_title: Koumra : le CLAC met les élèves à l’épreuve de la lecture et de la dictée
original_payload.original_body:
Le Centre de lecture et d’animation culturelle (CLAC) de Koumra a organisé, le lundi 16 novembre 2026, dans ses locaux, un concours de lecture et de dictée à l’intention des élèves de quatre écoles primaires. Cette activité s’inscrit dans le cadre de la 10ᵉ édition du Mois du livre et de la lecture, placée sous le thème : « 10 ans du Mois du livre et de la lecture : de la mémoire écrite aux pratiques numériques ».
L’objectif est de susciter chez les élèves le goût de la lecture, d’améliorer leur maîtrise de la langue française et de leur faire découvrir le livre comme un outil essentiel d’apprentissage et d’ouverture sur le monde.
Dans son intervention, l’animateur principal du CLAC, Ngabo Sanga, a souligné l’importance de la lecture et de l’écriture dans la formation intellectuelle des enfants.
Lire aussi :  Journée mondiale du livre : à N’Djamena, étudiants et auteurs plaident pour le retour au goût de la lecture
Selon lui, ce concours vise à rapprocher les élèves du livre, à développer leurs capacités de compréhension et à cultiver chez eux le goût de l’effort et de la saine compétition.
Il a également invité les établissements scolaires, les enseignants et les parents à accompagner les enfants dans la pratique régulière de la lecture, afin de contribuer à leur réussite scolaire et à leur épanouissement intellectuel.
Lire aussi :  Tchad : la 10e édition du Mois du Livre s’ouvre sur le numérique
À l’issue des épreuves, l’école Saint-Kisito s’est classée première en lecture et en dictée, suivie de l’école La Floraison. Les meilleurs élèves seront récompensés à la clôture des activités, prévue le 27 novembre.
Au programme de cette célébration figurent également des projections de films, des exposés-débats ainsi que des campagnes de sensibilisation dans les établissements scolaires. Cette initiative contribue aussi à sensibiliser la communauté éducative à la nécessité de replacer le livre au cœur des apprentissages, à l’heure où les outils numériques occupent une place grandissante dans la transmission du savoir.
Alex Loubadjo Djassibaye

items.title: Médecine : le professeur Foumsou Lhagadang élu secrétaire général de la Conférence africaine des doyens des facultés de médecine d’expression française

original_payload.original_title: Médecine : le professeur Foumsou Lhagadang élu secrétaire général de la Conférence africaine des doyens des facultés de médecine d’expression française
original_payload.original_body:
Le professeur tchadien Foumsou Lhagadang a été élu secrétaire général de la Conférence africaine des doyens des facultés de médecine d’expression française. L’élection s’est tenue à Bangui, en République centrafricaine, à l’issue d’un processus ayant mobilisé 19 pays.
Le Tchad compte désormais un représentant à la tête du secrétariat général de la Conférence africaine des doyens des facultés de médecine d’expression française. Le professeur Foumsou Lhagadang a été élu à ce poste à Bangui, en République centrafricaine, remportant ainsi la confiance de ses pairs.
Cette élection constitue une reconnaissance du parcours de cet universitaire, considéré comme l’un des pionniers de la gynécologie-obstétrique au Tchad. Elle intervient dans un contexte de coopération entre les facultés de médecine francophones du continent, notamment autour de la formation et du développement de l’enseignement médical.
Actuel doyen de la Faculté des sciences de la santé de l’Université de N’Djamena, le professeur Foumsou Lhagadang exerce également comme chef du service d’obstétrique au Centre hospitalier universitaire de la Mère et de l’Enfant (CHU-ME). Il partage ainsi son expérience entre l’enseignement universitaire, la formation des futurs professionnels de santé et la pratique hospitalière.
Au fil de sa carrière, il a contribué à la formation de plusieurs générations de médecins et au développement de la gynécologie-obstétrique au Tchad.
Son élection à cette responsabilité continentale offre une visibilité supplémentaire aux compétences tchadiennes dans le domaine médical et universitaire. Elle constitue également une reconnaissance de son engagement dans la formation médicale et le renforcement des capacités des établissements d’enseignement supérieur.
Au CHU de la Mère et de l’Enfant, où il occupe des responsabilités médicales, cette élection est accueillie comme un motif de fierté. Elle vient distinguer le parcours d’un universitaire dont l’engagement se poursuit aussi bien dans les amphithéâtres que dans les services hospitaliers.

items.title: Lac : 100 nattes offertes aux retournés du Niger

original_payload.original_title: Lac : 100 nattes offertes aux retournés du Niger
original_payload.original_body:
À Daboua, dans le département de Fouli, un geste de solidarité vient apporter un soutien aux familles récemment retournées du Niger. Ce lundi 16 novembre 2026, le Conseil provincial du Lac leur a remis 100 nattes en plastique afin de contribuer à améliorer leurs conditions d’installation.
La cérémonie de remise s’est déroulée en présence du préfet du département de Fouli, Dimoya Souapebé. Le don lui a été officiellement remis par le président du Conseil provincial du Lac, Moustapha Mahamat Mamadou, entouré de plusieurs conseillers provinciaux.
À cette occasion, le président du Conseil provincial a indiqué que cette initiative traduit la volonté de son institution de soutenir les populations confrontées aux difficultés du déplacement et du retour. Il a également réaffirmé sa disponibilité à accompagner les autorités administratives et les partenaires humanitaires dans leurs actions en faveur des personnes vulnérables.
Lire aussi :  Lac : l’afflux des retournés du Niger mobilise les autorités
De son côté, le préfet de Fouli a salué ce geste de solidarité et exprimé sa reconnaissance au président ainsi qu’à l’ensemble des conseillers provinciaux. Il a souligné l’importance de cette contribution pour les familles accueillies dans son département.
Lire aussi :  Niger : des milliers d’Arabes sommés de quitter le pays avant le 31 décembre
Bien que ces 100 nattes ne suffisent pas à couvrir l’ensemble des besoins des nouveaux retournés, elles constituent un appui matériel concret pour ces ménages, confrontés aux premières difficultés de leur réinstallation.

items.title: Tchad : le gouvernement interdit les activités commerciales dans les établissements scolaires

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : le gouvernement interdit les activités commerciales dans les établissements scolaires
original_payload.original_body:
Le Premier ministre, Amb. Allah-Maye Halina, a signé, le 16 novembre 2026, une circulaire interdisant les activités commerciales et non scolaires au sein et aux abords des établissements scolaires publics et privés. Cette mesure vise à renforcer la sécurité des élèves et à préserver la vocation éducative des écoles.
La décision concerne un large éventail d’acteurs, notamment les membres du gouvernement, les délégués généraux auprès des provinces, les présidents des conseils provinciaux, les maires ainsi que les responsables des services déconcentrés de l’État et des établissements scolaires.
Dans sa circulaire, le chef du gouvernement dénonce la multiplication des installations anarchiques et des activités incompatibles avec la mission éducative des établissements scolaires. Selon lui, ces pratiques constituent une menace pour la sécurité physique des élèves, perturbent le bon déroulement des enseignements et portent atteinte à l’image des écoles.
Parmi les activités désormais interdites figurent les étals de rue, les kiosques, les boutiques et la vente ambulante. La mesure concerne également l’installation de pylônes de télécommunications et de panneaux publicitaires, l’élevage d’animaux sans lien avec un projet pédagogique préalablement validé, ainsi que les débits de boissons, bars et cabarets.
Les espaces de jeux de hasard, d’argent et de cartes, de même que les manifestations et fêtes non scolaires susceptibles de perturber la quiétude des lieux, sont également visés par cette interdiction.
Pour assurer l’application effective de cette décision, le Premier ministre, s’appuyant sur la loi organique n° 028/CNT/2024 du 4 novembre 2024 relative à la répartition des compétences, appelle les autorités administratives, municipales et éducatives à une action concertée.
Celles-ci sont notamment chargées de dresser un état des lieux exhaustif des installations irrégulières, de procéder aux opérations d’évacuation nécessaires et de veiller à la libération durable des espaces scolaires.
Un mécanisme de suivi régulier devra également être mis en place afin de garantir le respect strict de ces directives. À travers cette mesure, le gouvernement entend faire des établissements scolaires des espaces exclusivement consacrés à l’apprentissage, dans un environnement sain, sécurisé et propice à l’éducation.

original_payload.original_title: تشاد: الحكومة تحظر الأنشطة التجارية والإعلانية في محيط المدارس لحماية البيئة التعليمية
original_payload.original_body:
Tchad
تشاد: الحكومة تحظر الأنشطة التجارية والإعلانية في محيط المدارس لحماية البيئة التعليمية
أصدرت الحكومة التشادية قراراً حاسماً يحظر الأنشطة التجارية والإعلانية وتربية الحيوانات في محيط المدارس العامة والخاصة، بهدف توفير بيئة تعليمية آمنة ومواتية للطلاب.
Alwihda Info
17 nov. 2026
© Primature
قررت الحكومة التشadية التصدي للتشوهات التي تعطل البيئة المدرسية. ومن خلال منشور مشترك، حظرت السلطات رسمياً ممارسة الأنشطة التجارية، وإنشاء الهياكل الإعلانية، وتربية الحيوانات داخل المؤسسات التعليمية وفي محيطها المباشر، سواء كانت عامة أو خاصة.
الحفاظ على بيئة التعلم
في السنوات الأخيرة، تم توجيه أصابع الاتهام إلى انتشار المتاجر والأكشاك والبيع المتجول، فضلاً عن تركيب أبراج الاتصالات واللوحات الإعلانية بالقرب من المدارس. ووفقاً للحكومة، تعرض هذه المنشآت سلامة الطلاب للخطر، بالإضافة إلى تعطيل سير الدروس بشكل طبيعي.
تهدف التدابير إلى استعادة بيئة مواتية للدراسة. وأصبح محظوراً بصرامة:
* المتاجر والأكشاك والبسطات والبيع المتجول للسلع؛
* تركيب أبراج الاتصالات واللوحات الإعلانية؛
* أنشطة تربية الحيوانات غير المرتبطة ببرنامج تعليمي رسمي.
تطبيق على النطاق الوطني
يستهدف هذا التوجيه مباشرة الوزراء، والمندوبين الحكوميين لدى المقاطعات، ورؤساء المجالس الإقليمية، ورؤساء البلديات، فضلاً عن مسؤولي الخدمات التعليمية اللامركزية. كما تم تكليف مديري المؤسسات التعليمية بضمان التقشف الصارم بهذه الأحكام لضمان بيئة سليمة وآمنة لجميع الطلاب في جميع أنحاء البلاد.

original_payload.original_title: Tensions diplomatiques : la Somalie accuse les Émirats arabes unis d'ingérence
original_payload.original_body:
International
Tensions diplomatiques : la Somalie accuse les Émirats arabes unis d'ingérence
Le président somalien accuse vertement les Émirats arabes unis d'ingérence, dénonçant des accords régionaux contournant le pouvoir central et des implantations militaires illégales.
Alwihda Info
17 nov. 2026
© DR
Le président de la Somalie, Hassan Sheikh Mohamoud, a vivement mis en cause les Émirats arabes unis, les accusant d'interférer délibérément dans les affaires intérieures du pays. Selon lui, Abou Dhabi contourne systématiquement le gouvernement central en concluant des accords directs avec des autorités régionales.
Le chef de l'État somalien a également affirmé que les Émirats arabes unis avaient procédé à la construction illégale de bases militaires et au développement de forces paramilitaires sur le territoire national.
Par ailleurs, Mogadiscio reproche à Abou Dhabi d'avoir encouragé Israël à reconnaître le Somaliland, région séparatiste autoproclamée, et d'avoir utilisé le territoire somalien hors de tout cadre légal pour exfiltrer un dirigeant séparatiste yéménite.
« Le gouvernement des Émirats arabes unis a utilisé notre territoire en cachette, comme si nous étions un pays sans État ni autorité en charge », a déclaré le président somalien, illustrant la détérioration des relations entre les deux nations.

items.title: Tchad : au Moyen-Chari, des jeunes filles formées aux outils numériques pour renforcer leur autonomie

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : au Moyen-Chari, des jeunes filles formées aux outils numériques pour renforcer leur autonomie
original_payload.original_body:
Tchad
Tchad : au Moyen-Chari, des jeunes filles formées aux outils numériques pour renforcer leur autonomie
À Sarh, une session de formation organisée par le PATN et le cabinet Ebenyx initie des jeunes filles aux outils numériques pour stimuler l'entrepreneuriat féminin.
Alwihda Info
17 nov. 2026
Par Elwood Dk
L’accès aux nouvelles technologies devient un enjeu crucial pour l’autonomie des femmes et des jeunes filles. À Sahr, chef-lieu de la province du Moyen-Chari, le Projet d’appui à la transformation numérique du Tchad (PATN), avec l’accompagnement du cabinet Ebenyx, a organisé, ce mardi 17 novembre 2026, une session de formation consacrée à l’utilisation des outils numériques. La rencontre s’est tenue au Palais des Arts et de la Culture Ngarta Tombalbaye.
Cette activité a pour objectif de donner aux participantes les moyens de se servir efficacement des technologies numériques, aussi bien dans leurs activités quotidiennes que dans leurs initiatives économiques. Elle entend également réduire les difficultés d’accès aux connaissances numériques, particulièrement chez les femmes vivant dans les localités rurales, où les possibilités de formation restent limitées.
Durant les échanges, plusieurs aspects de l’utilisation du numérique ont été abordés. Les participantes ont notamment été initiées aux fonctions essentielles du téléphone portable, à la communication sur Internet, à la commercialisation des produits à travers les réseaux sociaux et aux précautions à prendre pour protéger leurs données personnelles.
Pour Layibé Patalet, ingénieur en cybersécurité au cabinet Ebenyx et formateur de la session, il est nécessaire de commencer par les notions élémentaires afin de permettre à chaque participante de suivre les enseignements. Selon lui, certaines femmes possèdent un téléphone sans pour autant connaître toutes les possibilités qu'offre cet appareil. « Notre objectif est de permettre aux filles et aux femmes de mieux comprendre les outils numériques et de savoir comment les utiliser pour améliorer leurs conditions de vie. Nous avons commencé par les fonctions de base du téléphone avant de passer aux autres possibilités, notamment le commerce en ligne et la protection sur Internet », a-t-il expliqué.
La formation accorde également une place importante à l'entrepreneuriat féminin. Les participantes ont découvert comment utiliser les plateformes numériques pour présenter leurs marchandises, trouver des clients et réaliser des ventes sans avoir nécessairement besoin d'ouvrir une boutique. Une possibilité qui pourrait faciliter le développement de petites activités génératrices de revenus. « Aujourd'hui, une femme peut proposer ses produits à plusieurs clients sans se déplacer. Avec un téléphone et une bonne utilisation des réseaux sociaux, elle peut faire connaître ses articles, recevoir des commandes et développer son commerce », a souligné le formateur. La sécurité sur Internet a constitué un autre point essentiel de cette rencontre. Les participantes ont été alertées sur les dangers liés aux mauvaises pratiques numériques, notamment les arnaques, les faux profils, les messages frauduleux et le vol de comptes.
Du côté des bénéficiaires, cette initiative est perçue comme une occasion d'acquérir des connaissances pratiques. Plusieurs participantes ont reconnu qu'avant cette formation, elles utilisaient leurs téléphones sans maîtriser suffisamment les différentes fonctionnalités disponibles. L'une d'elles témoigne : « Avant cette formation, je pensais que le téléphone servait principalement à appeler et à envoyer des messages. Aujourd'hui, j'ai compris qu'il peut aussi m'aider à vendre mes produits et à développer mes activités. C'est une nouvelle possibilité pour nous. Nous avons appris qu'il existe beaucoup de pièges sur Internet. Désormais, nous savons qu'il faut faire attention aux liens, aux messages inconnus et aux personnes qui cherchent à obtenir nos informations personnelles. »
Il faut noter que quatre jeunes filles ont été retenues pour assurer la continuité de cette initiative à travers des actions de sensibilisation.
original_payload.original_summary: À Sarh, une session de formation organisée par le PATN et le cabinet Ebenyx initie des jeunes filles aux outils numériques pour stimuler l'entrepreneuriat féminin.

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : au Mandoul, le BASE forme les prestataires de santé à la planification familiale et aux soins après avortement
original_payload.original_body:
Tchad
Tchad : au Mandoul, le BASE forme les prestataires de santé à la planification familiale et aux soins après avortement
Dans le cadre du projet PASFASS2 financé par l'AFD, le BASE organise une formation au Mandoul pour renforcer les compétences des prestataires en planification familiale et soins après avortement.
Alwihda Info
17 nov. 2026
Par Dominique Didéo
Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du projet PASFASS2, le Bureau d’Appui Santé et Environnement (BASE), avec le soutien financier de l’Agence française de développement (AFD), organise une session de formation à l’intention des prestataires de santé sur la planification familiale et les soins après avortement (PF/SAA).
Cette initiative vise à consolider les compétences techniques et pratiques des agents de santé, afin de contribuer à l’amélioration de la qualité et de l’accessibilité des services de santé sexuelle et reproductive dans la province du Mandoul.
À travers cet atelier, les participants sont invités à perfectionner leurs pratiques professionnelles pour garantir une prise en charge adaptée, efficace et respectueuse des droits des bénéficiaires.
L'accent est également mis sur la continuité des services, le respect des normes nationales en vigueur et la promotion d'un environnement préservant la dignité des patients.
À travers le projet PASFASS2, le BASE poursuit ainsi ses efforts en faveur du renforcement du système de santé et de l’accès élargi des populations aux services essentiels.

items.title: Tchad : le gouvernement interdit les activités commerciales et publicitaires aux abords des écoles

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : le gouvernement interdit les activités commerciales et publicitaires aux abords des écoles
original_payload.original_body:
Tchad
Tchad : le gouvernement interdit les activités commerciales et publicitaires aux abords des écoles
Face aux risques pour la sécurité des élèves, le gouvernement tchadien interdit formellement les commerces, les installations publicitaires et l'élevage d'animaux au sein et aux abords des établissements scolaires.
Alwihda Info
17 nov. 2026
© Primature
Le gouvernement tchadien a décidé de sévir contre les nuisances qui perturbent le milieu scolaire. À travers une circulaire conjointe, les autorités interdisent formellement l'exercice d'activités commerciales, l'installation de structures publicitaires et l'élevage d'animaux au sein et aux abords immédiats des établissements scolaires, qu'ils soient publics ou privés.
Préserver l'environnement d'apprentissage
Ces dernières années, la prolifération de boutiques, de kiosques, de ventes ambulantes, ainsi que l'implantation de pylônes de télécommunication et de supports publicitaires aux abords des écoles ont été pointées du doigt. Selon le gouvernement, ces installations compromettent la sécurité des élèves, en plus de perturber le déroulement normal des enseignements.
La mesure vise à restaurer un cadre propice à l'étude. Sont désormais strictement interdits :
* Les boutiques, kiosques, étals et la vente ambulante de marchandises ;
* L'installation de pylônes de télécommunication et de supports publicitaires ;
* Les activités d'élevage d'animaux non rattachées à un programme pédagogique officiel.
Une application à l'échelle nationale
Cette directive s'adresse directement aux ministres, aux délégués gouvernementaux auprès des provinces, aux présidents de conseils provinciaux, aux maires ainsi qu'aux responsables des services déconcentrés de l'éducation. Les chefs d'établissements scolaires sont également sommés de veiller au strict respect de ces dispositions afin de garantir un environnement sain et sécurisé pour l'ensemble des élèves à travers le pays.
original_payload.original_summary: Face aux risques pour la sécurité des élèves, le gouvernement tchadien interdit formellement les commerces, les installations publicitaires et l'élevage d'animaux au sein et aux abords des établissements scolaires.

items.title: Nairobi’s green identity under threat as construction boom drives tree loss

original_payload.original_title: Nairobi’s green identity under threat as construction boom drives tree loss
original_payload.original_body:
Housing market
In Kenya's capital, Nairobi, trees are being felled to make way for a new, bigger road. The sight of heavy machinery clearing green spaces has become increasingly familiar across the city.
Population growth has fuelled a construction boom in Nairobi over the last decade. Data from Kenya's Treasury shows that the country's construction sector grew by 6.8% in 2025 - up from 0.7% the previous year.
In Nairobi, private building completions hit 25,090 in 2025. "Nairobi city is growing, the population has really expanded. One thing we don't have is we don't have extra land, but the population keeps growing so we can only build on what we have. So if we are developing, maybe, the residential building infrastructure, we need to look at where are we building first.
original_payload.original_summary: In Kenya's capital, Nairobi, the push for bigger roads is coming at a cost to the city's green spaces, with trees increasingly being cleared to make way for construction.

items.title: Mozambique opposition leader charged with terrorism over 2024 unrest

original_payload.original_title: Mozambique opposition leader charged with terrorism over 2024 unrest
original_payload.original_body:
Terrorism
Mozambique's opposition leader Venâncio Mondlane has appeared in court to face terrorism charges, reopening tensions over the disputed 2024 elections and raising concerns about the country's political stability.
Mondlane, who leads the Anamola party, finished second to President Daniel Chapo in an election international observers said was marred by irregularities. He subsequently mobilised thousands of supporters in months of protests, which were met with a violent security crackdown that left at least 400 people dead, according to civil society groups.
Mondlane has rejected the charges, questioning the legality of the case. Speaking about the proceedings, he accused the Attorney General's Office of withholding the accusation for 130 days and presenting documents with serious procedural irregularities. He argued that the accusation should be declared null and void.
original_payload.original_summary: Mozambique's opposition leader Venâncio Mondlane is facing terrorism charges as his trial opens, reigniting tensions over the disputed 2024 elections. He previously led months of protests, met with a violent crackdown that left at least 400 people dead, according to civil society groups.
